20100103025709A	ON JANUARY 3, 2010 AT APPROXIMATELY 11:00 A.M. PACIFIC STANDARD TIME, PRIVATE PILOT MICHAEL FUQUA WAS FLYING N7417N, A CESSNA 182P FROM PALOMAR AIRPORT (KCRQ) IN CARLSBAD, CALIFORNIA, TO FALLBROOK AIRPORT (L18) ALSO IN CALIFORNIA. THE WEATHER IN THE AREA OF THE FLIGHT WAS IN VFR CONDITIONS AND WAS REPORTED TO BE CLEAR WITH WINDS LIGHT AND VARIABLE AND TEMPERATURES IN THE MID 60'S FAHRENHEIT.  THIS WAS THE FIRST TIME THE PILOT HAD ATTEMPTED A LANDING AT FALLBROOK.  THIS AIRPORT HAS A 2160 FOOT RUNWAY SITUATED ON TOP OF A HILL.  THE TERRAIN IN THE LOCAL AREA IS MADE UP OF ROLLING HILLS AND IRREGULAR LANDSCAPE.  HE ATTEMPTED TO CHECK THE AIRPORT WEATHER CONDITIONS ON THE CTAF FREQUENCY BUT WAS UNABLE TO RECEIVE ANY RECORDING.  AT APPROXIMATELY 11:15 A.M., HE SET UP A NORMAL DOWNWIND ENTRY WITH A LEFT TRAFFIC PATTERN TO RUNWAY 18.  HE CHECKED THE WINDSOCK AND SAW NO WIND INDICATED.   MR. FUQUA COMMENCED A DESCENT AND CONFIGURED THE AIRCRAFT WITH FULL FLAPS FOR HIS LANDING BUT REMAINED TOO HIGH AND TOO FAST DURING THE APPROACH.  HIS LANDING WAS BEYOND THE MID POINT OF THE RUNWAY AND HE BALLOONED SOME IN THE FLARE.  AFTER TOUCHDOWN, HE APPLIED MAXIMUM BRAKING AND SKIDDED OVER 600 FEET OFF THE END OF THE RUNWAY AND DOWN THE HILL THAT EXTENDED OFF THE RUNWAYS END.  AS THE AIRCRAFT WAS NEARING A STOP AT THE BOTTOM OF THE HILL, THE NOSE WHEEL DUG INTO THE SOFT DIRT CAUSING THE AIRCRAFT TO FLIP OVER ONTO ITS BACK AND COME TO REST.  THE PILOT WAS ABLE TO FREE HIS SEATBELT AND EXIT OUT THE PASSENGER SIDE OF THE AIRCRAFT.  THERE WAS NO FIRE AND NO DAMAGE TO THE AIRPORT PROPERTY OR SURROUNDING AREA.  THE NOSE WHEEL BROKE OFF AND THE AIRCRAFT RECEIVED SUBSTANTIAL DAMAGE.  THERE WAS SIGNIFICANT DAMAGE TO THE WING AND WING SPAR, FUSELAGE, TAIL, PROPELLER AND NOSE SECTION.  A FLIGHT INSTRUCTOR WHO WAS GOING TO FLY A DUAL INSTRUCTIONAL FLIGHT WITH MR. FUQUA WAS WAITING AT THE AIRPORT AND WITNESSED THE ACCIDENT.  THE PLAN WAS TO JOIN UP WITH MR. FUQUA AND PROVIDE FLIGHT TRAINING WITH A TRIP TO BIG BEAR, CALIFORNIA FOR HIGH ALTITUDE AIRPORT FAMILIARIZATION.  HE REPORTS THE APPROACH PATH WAS TOO HIGH AND THE APPROACH SPEED APPEARED TO BE ABOUT 10 TO 15 MPH TOO FAST.  THE TOUCHDOWN APPEARED TO BE ABOUT 2/3 OF THE WAY DOWN THE RUNWAY.  HE SAW THE AIRCRAFT SKID OFF THE END AND GO DOWN THE EMBANKMENT.  HE INDICATED THAT WINDS FOR THE MOST PART WERE CALM BUT THERE WAS OCCASIONAL LOW SPEED SOFT DRAFTS THAT WOULD HAVE FAVORED USING RUNWAY 36.  I HAVE DETERMINED THAT THIS SLIGHT INTERMITTENT TAILWIND WAS NOT SIGNIFICANT TO THE CAUSE OF THIS ACCIDENT.AN INTERVIEW WITH THE PILOT FOCUSED ON HIS POOR SHORT FIELD LANDING TECHNIQUE AND HIS FAILURE TO MAKE A DECISION TO GO AROUND WHEN IT BECAME APPARENT THAT HIS TOUCHDOWN POINT WAS BEYOND THE NORMAL TOUCHDOWN ZONE OF THE LANDING RUNWAY.  I ASKED HIM TO GIVE ME THE GO AROUND PROCEDURE FOR HIS AIRCRAFT AND HE WAS ABLE TO RECITE THE PROPER SEQUENCE OF POWER APPLICATION AND CONTROL IMPUTES AND FLAP CONFIGURATION CHANGES.  WHEN PRESSED FOR AN ANSWER AS TO WHY HE DID NOT GO AROUND, NO CLEAR REASON WAS GIVEN.  SOME OTHER ITEMS THAT WERE DISCUSSED INCLUDED THE IDEA THAT A FEW LOW APPROACHES TO AN UN FAMILIAR RUNWAY COULD HAVE BETTER PREPARED HIM FOR THE VISUAL REFERENCES NECESSARY TO MAKE A MORE NORMAL LANDING ATTEMPT.  ALSO DISCUSSED, WAS THE NEED FOR A STABILIZED CONFIGURATION AND PROPER AIRSPEED CONTROL.  HE SHARED WITH ME THAT HE WAS FOCUSED TOO MUCH ON THE UPCOMING FLIGHT TO BIG BEAR, CALIFORNIA AND THE MOUNTAIN TRAINING HE WAS ANTICIPATING.  HE RELATES THAT IN HIND SIGHT HE DID NOT GIVE ADEQUATE CONSIDERATION TO THE ISSUES INVOLVED WITH AN UN FAMILIAR AIRPORT THAT HAS A SHORT RUNWAY.

20100109044579A	WEATHER AT THE TIME OF THE EVENT WAS VFR.  THE TEMPERATURE WAS APPROXIMATELY -5 DEGREES CELSIUS WITH A DEW POINT OF -13.  THE BAROMETER WAS 30.02.  THE AIRCRAFT HAD AN STC FOR AUTO GAS, AND IT WAS RUNNING ON AUTO GAS AT THE TIME OF THE EVENT.  THE LEFT WING WAS PROPERLY PLACARDED FOR 80/100LL AND AUTO GAS.  THE RIGHT WING LACKED ANY PLACARDING NEAR THE CAP, AND THE PAINT AROUND IT SUGGESTED NONE HAD BEEN PRESENT.  BOTH TANKS WERE SAID TO CONTAIN FUEL.  THE OFFICE REQUESTED THE FUEL BE DRAINED FROM THE GASCOLATOR AND CARBURETOR BOWLS.  THE LIQUID DRAINED FROM THE GASCOLATOR WAS TINTED SLIGHTLY BLUE, AND THE SMELL WAS THAT OF GASOLINE.  IT IS THE OPINION OF AN INSPECTOR IS THAT THE SMELL AND COLOR WERE INDICATING A MIX OF AUTO GAS AND 100LL.  IN ADDITION WAS A RESIDUE OF FINE BLACK PARTICLES THAT SANK TO THE BOTTOM OF THE COLLECTION JAR.  THE SIZE OF THE PARTICLES WAS THAT OF A FINE GRIT, AND THE AREA THEY COVERED WAS ABOUT THE SIZE OF A NICKEL WHEN SPREAD OUT IN A SINGLE LAYER.  LIQUID DRAINED FROM THE CARBURETOR BOWL WAS A MIXTURE OF LIQUID IN THE GASCOLATOR AND WHAT APPEARED TO BE WATER.  THE ENGINE PROBLEMS STARTED AFTER POWER WAS REDUCED TO CRUISE POWER.  THE PILOT BELIEVED THE TAKE-OFF WAS ACCOMPLISHED ON THE RIGHT TANK.  WHEN THE AIRCRAFT ENGINE STARTED RUNNING ROUGH, THEY TRIED APPLYING CARBURETOR HEAT, WHICH HE SAID WAS SOMEWHAT SUCCESSFUL.  THEY SWITCHED FUEL TANKS, AND TESTED WITH AND WITHOUT CARBURETOR HEAT.  HE STATED THEY PUT THE CARBURETOR HEAT ON AND LEFT IT ON WHILE THEY ATTEMPTED TO RETURN TO BAYPORT.  WHEN THE ENGINE QUIT, IT WAS A COMPLETE STOP AND WAS NOT WINDMILLING.  HE STATED THE ENGINE WAS RUNNING ROUGH AND WAS LOOSING POWER.  THIS TREND CONTINUED UNTIL THE ENGINE SUFFERED A COMPLETE STOPPAGE.  AGAIN, INITIALLY THE CARBURETOR HEAT HELPED, TO WHICH AND WHAT EFFECT HE DID NOT ELABORATE, BUT AS THE SITUATION DETERIORATED, THE CARBURETOR HEAT AND ALL OTHER CHANGES HAD NO EFFECT.  WHEN ASKED ABOUT THE FUEL, HE STATED THAT THE OWNER USED BOTH 100LL AND AUTO GAS.   HE WAS UNAWARE OF ANY RECENT FUELING.  PRIOR TO THE FLIGHT OF JANUARY 9, THE PREVIOUS FLIGHT WAS ON 01-06-2010. THERE IS AN ENTRY IN THE LOGBOOK THAT THE AIRCRAFT WAS FUELED ON 12-15-2009 AT SPADARO (1N2).  THE AIRCRAFT HAD FLOWN APPROXIMATELY 4.7 TACH HOURS SINCE THEN.  A REVIEW WAS MADE OF A CARBURATOR ICING CHART, AND THE RESULT WAS THAT CARBURATOR ICING WAS POSSIBLE, BUT HIGHLY IMPROBABLE.THE ENGINE WAS REBUILT BY A ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ IN OKLAHOMA, A SPECIALIST ON FRANKLIN ENGINES TWENTY HOURS PRIOR.  THE FOUR YEAR TIME PERIOD THAT PASSED FROM ENGINE REMOVAL TO ENGINE INSTALLATION WAS DUE TO INSUFFICIENT FUNDS FROM MR. OLSON.  MR. OLSON INSTALLED THE ENGINE, AND THE SIGN-OFF AND ANNUAL WERE COMPLETED BY AN A/I.  ON THE DAY IN QUESTION, MR. OLSON STATED HE PRE-HEATED THE ENGINE FOR ABOUT 40 MINUTES, AND THEN RAN IT ON THE GROUND FOR ABOUT 20 TO WARM THE CABIN WHILE WAITING FOR HIS PASSENGER.  THE RUN-UP WAS UNEVENTFUL, AND THE TAKE-OFF AND INITIAL CRUISE WERE AS WELL.  MR. OLSON NOTED THE ENGINE WAS STRONG AND SMOOTH, AND FAR BETTER THAN THE ENGINE THAT WAS REMOVED FROM THE AIRCRAFT.  THEY FLEW FOR ABOUT 10 TO 12 MINUTES BEFORE THEY STATED HAVING TROUBLE. THE PILOT ELECTED TO DITCH AS ANY HOPE OF MAKING THE AIRPORT DISAPPEARED.

CREW PERFORMED FLY BY OF CONTROL TOWER THAT CONFIRMED LH MAIN AND NOSE GEAR APPEARED DOWN AND RH MAIN GEAR APPEARED UP. CREW COMPLETED PARTIAL GEAR UP LANDING CHECKLIST AND LANDED ON RWY 4L. THE AIRCRAFT REMAINED ON CENTER LINE AND CAME TO REST ON THE LH MAIN, NOSE AND RH ENGINE APPROXIMATELY 4200 FEET FROM THE DISPLACED THRESHOLD. THERE WAS NO POST INCIDENT FIRE. A SUCCESSFUL EVACUATION WAS INITIATED WITH THREE MINOR INJURIES REPORTED. THE ONLY NOTABLE DAMAGE TO THE AIRCRAFT APPEARED TO BE TO THE UNDERSIDE OF THE RH ENGINE AND THE LH AND RH INBOARD LANDING GEAR DOORS WHICH REMAINED OPEN DURING THE LANDING AND CONTACTED THE RUNWAY. IT APPEARS THE LANDING GEAR FAILED TO EXTEND BECAUSE THE RH MAIN GEAR INBOARD DOOR FAILED TO OPEN COMPLETELY. THE DOOR FAILED TO OPEN COMPLETELY BECAUSE OF AN AS YET UNSPECIFIED INTERNAL FAILURE OF THE DOOR ACTUATOR. THE LANDING GEAR SYSTEM OPERATES SUCH THAT ALL GEAR DOORS MUST BE COMPLETELY OPEN BEFORE THE LANDING GEAR IS COMMANDED TO EXTEND. THE GRAVITY EMERGENCY EXTENSION WAS EFFECTIVE ON THE LH MAIN AND NOSE GEAR, BUT WAS INEFFECTIVE ON THE RH MAIN BECAUSE IT HIT THE PARTIALLY OPEN INBOARD DOOR WHICH PREVENTED IT FROM FULLY EXTENDING. THE MATTER IS CURRENTLY UNDER INVESTIGATION BY THE VARIOUS MANUFACTURERS INVOLVED AND THE NTSB. SHOULD A DEFINITIVE CAUSE FOR THE FAILURE OF THE RH MLG DOOR ACTUATOR BE DETERMINED, THIS FORM WILL BE AMENDED.IT IS WORTHY OF NOTE THAT DURING THE EVACUATION THE R1 DOOR EMERGENCY ESCAPE SLIDE FAILED TO DEPLOY. A PRELIMINARY INVESTIGATION OF THE FAILURE INDICATES THAT ALL CONDITIONS FOR THE SLIDE TO DEPLOY WERE MET; HOWEVER, THE SLIDE NEVER COMPLETELY LEFT THE BUSTLE WHICH THEN BECAME TRAPPED BY THE DOOR HINGE PREVENTING DEPLOYMENT. INSPECTION BY THE MANUFACTURER AT THEIR FACILITY CONFIRMED THAT THE SLIDE WAS PACKED CORRECTLY AND A FLAT FIRE TEST SHOWED NORMAL INFLATION. THIS MATTER CONTINUES TO BE INVESTIGATED BY THE VARIOUS MANUFACTURERS INVOLVED AND THE NTSB. SHOULD A DEFINITIVE CAUSE FOR THE FAILURE OF THE SLIDE BE DETERMINED, THIS FORM WILL BE AMENDED.

UPON INTERVIEWING AN EYEWITNESS AND FIRST RESPONDER TO THE CRASH HE NOTED THAT THE AIRCRAFT SEEMED TOO HIGH AND FAST AND THAT IT WAS STILL AIRBORNE APPROXIMATELY TWO- THIRDS DOWN THE 2,579 FOOT STRIP. HE ALSO SAW THE AIRCRAFT TURN TO THE LEFT AND IMPACT THE SNOW BANK. HE ALSO STATED THAT HE SAW VERY LARGE SKID MARKS DOWN THE RUNWAY AND IT WAS VERY APPARENT THAT THE LEFT BRAKE WAS MORE ENGAGED THAN THE RIGHT BRAKE. WHEN THE EYEWITNESS ASKED THE PILOT WHAT HAD HAPPENED THE PILOT STATED HE WAS A LITTLE HIGH AND A LITTLE FAST AND THAT HE TRIED TO SAVE THE LANDING. THE PILOT ALSO SAID THAT HE HAD TALKED TO A MECHANIC ABOUT A BRAKE PROBLEM FROM THE DAY BEFORE BUT FLEW THE AIRCRAFT ANYWAY. AT THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENT THE EYEWITNESS NOTED THE WEATHER TO BE WINDS OUT OF THE WEST FAVORING RUNWAY 29. SKY WAS CLEAR AND RUNWAY WAS DRY.  ANOTHER FIRST RESPONDER WAS INTERVIEWED AND HEARD THE PILOT SAY THAT HE WAS HARD ON THE BRAKES AND ALL OF THE SUDDEN THE LEFT BRAKE CAUGHT.  A WRITTEN REPORT WAS OBTAINED DURING THE INVESTIGATION FROM THE PILOT. IN THE REPORT THE PILOT WRITES THAT THE WINDS WERE LIGHT AND VARIABLE WITH AN OCCASIONAL GUST AND A FEW BUMPS ON FINAL. HE CONTINUES TO WRITE THAT THE WINDS WERE SHIFTING AND THAT HE HAD A PUSH FROM THE REAR ALSO ON FINAL. HE TRANSCRIBES THAT HE LANDED BEYOND THE NUMBERS AND STILL A LITTLE FAST. HE CONTINUES IN HIS REPORT THAT HE STEPPED FIRMLY ON THE BRAKES, FELT SOME CHATTERING BUT WAS STRAIGHT AT THE TIME OF TOUCHDOWN AND THAT ALL THE SUDDEN THE AIRCRAFT SWERVED TO THE LEFT. HE STATES HE DID NOT WANT TO OVERCORRECT TO PREVENT A FLIP AND SAW THE SNOW BANK APPROACHING. HE CONTINUES TO WRITE THAT HE THINKS THE BRAKES LOCKED UP AND THAT THE RIGHT RELEASED AND THAT THE LEFT STAYED ON A LITTLE LONGER WHICH STEERED THE AIRCRAFT OFF THE RUNWAY. UPON FURTHER INVESTIGATIONS THE SKID MARKS WERE MEASURED TO SHOW TWO PARALLEL SYMMETRIC SKIDS ON THE CENTER OF THE RUNWAY STARTING 733 FEET FROM THE END OF THE RUNWAY LASTING APPROXIMATELY 260 FEET. THEN THE LEFT SKID MARK VEERING LEFT OFF THE RUNWAY AND INTO THE SNOW. THE AIRCRAFT CONTINUED FOR ANOTHER 141 FEET AND CAME TO REST APPROXIMATELY 375 FEET FROM THE END OF THE NUMBERS OF 29 AT THE END OF THE RUNWAY.   THE RIGHT WING TIP HIT THE SNOW BANK AT A VERY LOW ANGLE, BOTH MAIN WHEEL MARKS IN THE SNOW DISAPPEARED, AND THE AIRCRAFT TURNED 90 DEGREES RIGHT.  THE NOSE WHEEL LEFT A CONTINUOUS MARK IN THE SNOW.  UPON EXAMINATION OF THE AIRCRAFT IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE RIGHT WING TIP HAD IMPACTED THE SNOW BANK AND/OR GROUND, AND THE NOSE GEAR STRUT ASSEMBLY WAS BENT TO THE LEFT.  A FUNCTIONAL CHECK OF THE TOE BRAKES AND PARKING BRAKE PROVED SATISFACTORY.  THE BRAKING SYSTEM EXHIBITED NO HYDRAULIC LEAKS, AND THE BRAKE LININGS WERE SATISFACTORY.  THE VISUAL INSPECTION OF THE FUSELAGE AND RIGHT WING REVEALED THAT THE FORE AND AFT SPARS WERE DAMAGED, APPARENTLY WHEN THE RIGHT WING TIP IMPACTED THE SNOW BANK.  THE FLAPS WERE FOUND IN THE DOWN POSITION, AND WERE NOT ABLE TO BE RETRACTED DUE TO THE RIGHT WING TRAILING EDGE BEING JAMMED AGAINST THE FUSELAGE.  BOTH PROPELLER BLADES WERE FOUND TO BE BENT FROM IMPACT WITH THE GROUND AND/OR SNOW BANK.

THE ONLY RECOGNIZABLE PORTION OF THE AIRCRAFT WAS THE EMPENNAGE SECTION.  THE REMAINDER OF THE AIRCRAFT WAS LARGELY LOCATED IN ONE AREA WITH THE ENGINE IMBEDDED FOUR FEET INTO THE FIELD SO THAT THE FIREWALL WAS LEVEL WITH THE SURFACE OF THE GROUND.  THE INDIANA STATE POLICE WAS ON SCENE AT THE TIME OF OUR ARRIVAL AND PROVIDED LOGISTICAL ASSISTANCE.  PRIOR TO OUR ARRIVAL, THE BODY OF THE PILOT HAD BEEN REMOVED BY THE JEFFERSON COUNTY CORONER. THE AIRCRAFT THEN CONTINUED TO FLY IN A NNW DIRECTION AFTER WHICH THE AIRCRAFT THEN BANKED SLIGHTLY TO THE LEFT, AND BEGAN A HARD PULL-UP WHILE BANKING TO THE RIGHT.  USING A MODEL AIRPLANE, ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ DEMONSTRATED THAT THE AIRCRAFT CONTINUED THE RIGHT TURN TO A "WINGOVER" AND THEN TO A "SPLIT S" RESULTING IN JUST ABOUT A 180 DEGREE COURSE REVERSAL BEFORE IMPACTING THE GROUND.  DURING INTERVIEWS OF SEVERAL CLOSE FRIENDS, ACQUAINTANCES AND RELATIVES OF THE PILOT, THERE WERE STATEMENTS MADE THAT PILOT HAD NOT BEEN ACTING LIKE "HIMSELF".  ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^, A VERY CLOSE FRIEND TO THE PILOT, AND A PILOT HIMSELF, SAID THAT ON THE SATURDAY NIGHT BEFORE THE ACCIDENT (LESS THAN 48 HOURS), THE PILOT APPEARED LUCID AND FINE DURING THEIR TWO HOUR VISIT.  HOWEVER, ON SUNDAY, APRIL 18, 2010 (LESS THAN 24 HOURS BEFORE THE ACCIDENT), ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^, HAD TO PROVIDE ASSISTANCE TO THE PILOT TO OPERATE THE FUEL PUMP, SOMETHING THAT THE PILOT HAD DONE MANY TIMES BY HIMSELF.  FURTHER, SEVERAL COMMENTS WERE HEARD THAT THE PILOT HAD A SMALL STROKE JUST TEN DAYS BEFORE THE ACCIDENT.  THIS MEDICAL INFORMATION COULD NOT BE SUBSTANTIATED DUE TO FEDERAL PRIVACY LAWS.  INVESTIGATION OF THE AIRCRAFT AND THE AIRCRAFT MAINTENANCE RECORDS DO NOT INDICATE THAT THERE WERE ANY AIRWORTHINESS ISSUES THAT CONTRIBUTED TO THE ACCIDENT.  THE PILOT DID HAVE A CURRENT MEDICAL (SEE ATTACHMENT) AND DID HAVE A BIENNIAL FLIGHT REVIEW (SEE LOG BOOK ATTACHMENT)."

THE PILOT QUICKLY REDUCED POWER AND RAISED THE NOSE IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE AIRPLANE'S PILOT INFORMATION MANUAL. THIS STOPPED THE VIBRATION, WHICH LASTED A TOTAL OF ABOUT 3 TO 5 SECONDS. THE PILOT STATED THAT HE WAS BETWEEN 155 AND 160 MPH AT THE TIME OF THE TURBULENCE ENCOUNTER. THE MAXIMUM STRUCTURAL CRUISING AIRSPEED FOR THIS MODEL VARIANT OF THE BEECH 35 SERIES (VNO OR VC, AND THE BEGINNING OF THE YELLOW CAUTION ARC) IS 161 MPH, AND THE MANEUVERING AIRSPEED (VA) IS 131 MPH. BY DEFINITION, MAXIMUM MANEUVERING SPEED (VA) IS THAT SPEED AT WHICH FULL AND ABRUPT CONTROL SURFACE DEFLECTION OR ANY TURBULENCE ENCOUNTER WILL RESULT IN AN AERODYNAMIC STALL BEFORE THE STRUCTURAL LIMIT LOAD WILL BE EXCEEDED AND DAMAGE WILL OCCUR. ABOVE VA IT IS POSSIBLE TO INCUR STRUCTURAL DAMAGE WITH MANEUVERING INPUTS AND/OR SIGNIFICANT TURBULENCE ENCOUNTERS. THE PILOT WAS FLYING ABOVE VA BUT WITHIN THE GREEN AIRSPEED ARC WHEN THE AIRPLANE ENCOUNTERED THE TURBULENCE; HOWEVER, HE WAS NOT FLYING IN THE YELLOW ARC ABOVE VC/VNO AND HAD NO REASON TO BELIEVE THAT THE AIRPLANE WOULD ENCOUNTER TURBULENCE."

MECHANIC STATEMENT:I REMOVED THE LEFT MAIN LANDING GEAR ACTUATOR FROM ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ YAK 3.USING SHOCK AIR, OPERATION OF THE ACTUATOR APPEARED TO BE NORMAL.THERE WERE NO INTERNAL OR EXTERNAL LEAKS. ON SCENE AT THE ACCIDENT SITE IT WAS NOTED THAT THE AIRCRAFT WAS FACING NOSE DOWN TO A STONE WALL NEXT TO A LARGE TREE. THE AIRCRAFT WAS VERTICAL AND PARALLEL NEXT TO THE IMPACT TREE. THE LEFT SEAT OCCUPANT WAS GEORGE FORTIN WHO WAS WEARING A SEATBELT BUT THE AIRPLANE WAS NOT EQUIPPED WITH SHOULDER HARNESSES. THE RIGHT SEAT OCCUPANT WAS ANATOLE KALINUK. HE TOO WAS WEARING THE SEATBELT.WITH RESPECT TO THE FLIGHT, THE PILOT (GEORGE) DEPARTED LIMINGTON HARMON AIRPORT (63B) ABOUT 0830 AND FLEW TO MAPLE RIDGE AIRPORT (03ME) WHICH IS A PRIVATE AIRFIELD, WITH NO FLIGHT PLAN FOUND ON FILE AND WEATHER BRIEFING INFORMATION IS UNKNOWN. IT WAS DETERMINED THAT VISUAL METEOROLOGICAL CONDITIONS EXISTED ON SATURDAY AND SUNDAY. AT 03ME, MR. KALINIK ENTERED THE AIRPLANE WHERE ONLY ONE TAKEOFF WAS REPORTED. THE FLIGHT THEN DEPARTED THE AIRFIELD AREA AND WHEN FLYING OVER LONG LAKE, A WITNESS WHO IS A HARBOR MASTER SAW THE AIRPLANE FLYING IN A NORTHERLY DIRECTION WHEN HE HEARD A "POP" SOUND, FOLLOWED BY ENGINE SILENCE. THE WITNESS REPORTED THE AIRPLANE TURNED EAST THEN WENT OUT OF SIGHT. LATER WE WERE INFORMED THAT TWO ADDITIONAL WITNESSES REPORTED SEEING THE AIRPLANE FLYING IN A NORTHERLY DIRECTION THEN HEARD SPUTTERING SOUNDS, FOLLOWING BY ENGINE SILENCE. THESE WITNESSES REPORTED THE AIRPLANE TURNING TO THE EAST THEN WENT OUT OF SIGHT. THE AIRCRAFT CONTACTED SEVERAL TREE TOPS, DESCENDED AND CONTACTED A LARGE TREE WITH THE RIGHT WING APPROXIMATELY 30-40 FEET UP, DESCENDED VERTICALLY DOWN AND IMPACTED A STONE WALL. FIRST OVER VIEW IS THE PROPELLER WAS NOT UNDER POWER ON IMPACT, THERE WAS NO SMELL OF FUEL, THE RIGHT WING FUEL TANK WAS COMPROMISED AND EMPTY, THE RIGHT WING TANK SHUT-OFF VALVE WAS IN THE OFF POSITION, AND ENGINE CASE WAS IN TACK AND WILL NEED FURTHER INVESTIGATION FOR POSSIBLE CAUSE. WE FOUND PIECES OF THE RIGHT NAVIGATION LIGHT 30 TO 40 YARDS NORTH OF THE ACTUAL CRASH SITE. THIS WOULD INDICATE THE AIRCRAFT CONTACTED THE TREES PRIOR TO CONTACTING THE LARGE TREE. THE ELT DID NOT ACTIVATE BUT WAS FOUND IN THE CABIN AREA WITH THE SWITCH IN THE OFF POSITION.THE AIRCRAFT ANNUAL INSPECTION WAS COMPLETED ON 09-03-2009 @ TACH TIME OF 674.7 HOURS AS UN-AIRWORTHY FOR NO AIRWORTHINESS CERTIFICATE. EXAMINATION OF THE FAA RECORDS INDICATES A REPLACEMENT AIRWORTHINESS CERTIFICATE WAS ISSUED ON 9-16-2009 BY EA-FSDO-65. THE AIRCRAFT TOTAL TIME AT THE INSPECTION WAS 2054.7 HOURS. THE TACH TIME AT THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENT IS 683.5 AND TOTAL TIME OF 2063.5 HOURS. THE CONTINENTAL ENGINE WAS OVERHAULED ON 10-02-1986 AND INSTALLED 06-20-1989 @ TACH TIME 469.0 HOURS.

VISUAL METEOROLOGICAL CONDITIONS (VMC) PREVAILED AT THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENT; JABARA AIRPORT (KAAO) AUTOMATED SURFACE OBSERVATION SYSTEM (ASOS) WAS REPORTING THE WINDS AS 020 DEGREES AT 4 KNOTS.  THE AIRMAN REPORTED THE WINDS AT THE DERBY-COOK AIRPORT TO BE LIGHT AND VARIABLE, FAVORING A LANDING ON RUNWAY 35.  UPON BEING ESTABLISHED ON FINAL FOR RUNWAY 35 AND CONFIGURED FOR LANDING WITH 20 DEGREES OF APPROACH FLAP, THE AIRMAN NOTED THAT THE AIRCRAFT WAS FLYING APPROXIMATELY 5-10 MPH FASTER THAN NORMAL.  THE AIRCRAFT'S APPROXIMATE AIRSPEED ON FINAL WAS 90 MPH; THE AIRMAN INDICATED THAT THE NORMAL LANDING CONFIGURATION AND SPEED WOULD BE 20 DEGREES OF FLAPS AND 80 MPH.  PER THE AIRMAN, DURING THE LANDING PHASE, THE AIRCRAFT BALLOONED AND FLOATED, AND SUBSEQUENTLY LANDED JUST PRIOR TO THE MID-POINT OF RUNWAY 35; RUNWAY 17/35 IS 2,507 FT IN LENGTH AND 40 FT IN WIDTH.  UPON TOUCHDOWN, THE AIRMAN STATED THAT MAXIMUM BRAKING WAS APPLIED AS THE AIRCRAFT WAS QUICKLY APPROACHING THE END OF THE RUNWAY.  DUE TO THE EXCESSIVE SPEED, THE AIRMAN WAS UNABLE TO STOP THE AIRCRAFT PRIOR TO ITS DEPARTURE FROM THE RUNWAY SURFACE.  PER THE AIRMAN, A GO-AROUND WAS NOT ATTEMPTED AT ANY TIME.  PRIOR TO THE AIRCRAFT EXITING THE RUNWAY, THE AIRCRAFT BEGAN VEERING RIGHT OF CENTERLINE; EXCESSIVE BRAKING CAUSED A PERFORATION IN THE RIGHT TIRE EXACERBATING THE AIRCRAFT'S DEPARTURE FROM RUNWAY CENTERLINE.  THE AIRCRAFT SUBSEQUENTLY ROLLED DOWN A SMALL EMBANKMENT AT THE END OF THE RUNWAY AND IMPACTED AN AIRPORT BOUNDARY BARRIER CONSISTING OF HORIZONTALLY LAID TELEPHONE POLES AND CONCRETE CYLINDERS.  UPON IMPACT, THE AIRCRAFT'S RIGHT MAIN GEAR AND NOSE WHEEL WERE SHEERED OFF; THE LEFT MAIN WHEEL WAS ATTACHED TO THE AIRCRAFT BY A BRAKE LINE ONLY.  THE AIRCRAFT SUSTAINED SUBSTANTIAL DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE FIREWALL AS A DIRECT RESULT OF IT IMPACTING THE AIRPORT BOUNDARY BARRIER.  NO INJURIES WERE REPORTED BY EITHER THE AIRMAN OR PASSENGER.

I THEREFORE ELECTED TO USE RUNWAY 10.I TAXIED TO INTERSECTION A3, HOLDING SHORT OF THE RUNWAY, WHERE I THEN PERFORMED A RUNUP AND CONTROL CHECK.  SINCE THE AIRCRAFT HAD NOT FLOWN FOR A FAIRLY LONG TIME, I PERFORMED A FULL-POWER RUNUP AGAINST THE BRAKES, ENSURING THAT THE ENGINE WAS PERFORMING CORRECTLY.  ALL CHECKED OUT PERFECTLY, SO I BEGAN MY TAXI ROLL ONTO RUNWAY 10.  AS I HEADED TO THE CENTERLINE, THE NOSEWHEEL IMPACTED A 5" (WIDE AND DEEP) LATERAL CRACK ACROSS THE RUNWAY CAUSING A NOTICEABLE AND SHARP "WIGGLE" THROUGH THE FOOT CONTROLS.  NO OTHER EFFECT WAS IMMEDIATELY APPARENT.  I THEN LINED UP ON THE RUNWAY CENTERLINE (IMPACTING ANOTHER CRACK), APPLIED THE BRAKES AND BROUGHT THE ENGINE TO FULL POWER.  ONCE THE ENGINE HAD SPOOLED UP, I RELEASED THE BRAKES AND BEGAN THE TAKEOFF ROLL.  THE TAKEOFF ROLL ON THIS AIRCRAFT IS USUALLY 250-400 FEET, DEPENDENT ON LOAD AND DENSITY ALTITUDE.  THE AIRCRAFT WAS LIGHTLY LOADED BUT THERE WAS NO WIND, SO I WAS EXPECTING A 300-350 FOOT ROLL BEFORE ROTATION.JUST AT ROTATION (AT 35MPH INDICATED), THE NOSEWHEEL IMPACTED ANOTHER LATERAL CRACK IN THE RUNWAY, CAUSING ANOTHER SHARP "WIGGLE" THROUGH THE FOOT CONTROLS.  IMMEDIATELY AFTER THAT, THE TRIKE BEGAN VEERING TO THE RIGHT.  I APPLIED RIGHT FOOT INPUT (TRIKE FOOT CONTROLS ARE "PUSH LEFT TO GO RIGHT, PUSH RIGHT TO GO LEFT") TO COUNTER THE VEER, BUT THE CONTROL INPUT HAD NO EFFECT.  I APPLIED FULL LEFT STEER, BUT AGAIN, TO NO EFFECT.  AT THAT POINT, THE TRIKE UNIT ROLLED TO THE LEFT, PULLING THE WING INTO THE RUNWAY SURFACE.   THE ENGINE SUDDENLY STOPPED AND THE AIRCRAFT SLID APPROXIMATELY 15 FEET TO A STOP, RESTING ON ITS LEFT SIDE.  I TURNED OFF THE ELECTRICAL MASTER AND THE MAG SWITCHES, REACHED BACK AND SHUT OFF THE FUEL (WHICH WAS DRIPPING FROM THE BREATHER PIPE), RELEASED MY SEATBELT, REMOVED MY HELMET AND EXTRICATED MYSELF FROM THE COLLAPSED WING.THERE WAS AN AIRCRAFT IN THE PATTERN, SO MYSELF AND THREE FRIENDS (USING A PICKUP TRUCK) ROLLED THE AIRCRAFT ONTO ITS WHEELS AND RECOVERED IT FROM THE RUNWAY AND BACK TO HANGAR #3.  AS WE ROLLED THE AIRCRAFT UPRIGHT, WE NOTICED THAT THE NOSEWHEEL RIM WAS IN PIECES, WITH THE LEFT SIDE OF THE RIM PUSHED INTO THE FRONT SUSPENSION FORK.  WE RECOVERED THE SEPARATED PIECES. AFTER LANDING THERE WAS NO EMERGENCY EVACUATION AND THE ARFF DETERMINED THAT THERE WAS NO HEAT COMING FROM THE AFT CARGO COMPARTMENT, AND DEPLANING OF PASSENGERS AND CREW WAS ACCOMPLISHED VIA PEOPLE MOVERS.  SUBSEQUENT OFFLOADING AND SEARCHING OF AFT CARGO BAGS DETERMINED THAT A FLASHLIGHT HAD BEEN INADVERTENTLY SWITCHED ON INSIDE A PASSENGERS BAG.  THE FINDINGS FROM THE FAA SECURITY AND HAZARDOUS MATERIALS OFFICE AND THE NTSB INDICATE THAT THE CAUSE OF THE FIRE AND SMOKE WAS DUE TO A SPORTSMAN'S WAREHOUSE BRAND (ITEM # 1139424) 12 VOLT HIGH INTENSITY XENON FLASHLIGHT THAT WAS ON INSIDE A PASSENGERS PACKED BAG. THE HALOGEN LIGHT BULB HEATED UP ENOUGH TO IGNITE A MAP THAT WAS STOWED IN THE SAME POCKET AS THE FLASHLIGHT AND BURN A HOLE IN THE BAG CAUSING THE AFT CARGO HOLD SMOKE DETECTOR LIGHT TO ILLUMINATE.  THE AALA CMO WAS NOIFIED OF THIS INCIDENT ON 11/12/2010 AND A SERVICE DIFFICULTY REPORT (SDR) WAS SUMITTED ON 11/15/2010.  FAA SECURITY AND HAZARDOUS MATERIALS FIELD OFFICE HAS COMPLETED THEIR REPORT AND SUBMITTED IT TO WASHINGTON HEADQUARERS FOR REVIEW AND CORRECTIVE ACTION. THERE WERE NO OPERATIONAL OR AIRWORTHINESS ISSUES INVOLVED IN THIS INCIDENT. SEE NTSB REPORT NO. DCA11SA005.THIS REPORT IS CLOSED.

THE AIRCRAFT WAS ON A  14CFR PART 91 REPOSITION FLIGHT BACK TO FXE.  THE PILOT, THE SOLE OCCUPANT ON THE AIRCRAFT,  REPORTED A NORMAL LANDING.  HOWEVER, WHEN HE TAPPED ON THE BRAKES THE RT MLG COLLAPSED AND AT THE SAME TIME THE RT WING CONTACTED THE GROUND.  THE AIRCRAFT WAS REMOVED FROM THE ACTIVE RUNWAY AT APPROXIMATELY 2330 HRS. THE AIRCRAFT SUFFERED THE FOLLOWING DAMAGE UPON IMPACTING THE GROUND: RT PROPELLER BLADES WERE CURLED AFT AT THE TIP OF THE BLADES, RT WING TIP WAS DENTED/SCRATCHED,  RT WING AILERON AND FLAP WITH MINOR DENTS, RT "TIE DOWN" LOOP BENT, AND RT ENGINE AIR INTAKE SCOOP DAMAGED.  AFTER THE AIRCRAFT WAS REMOVED FROM THE RUNWAY AND SECURED AN INSPECTION OF THE RT MLG WAS CONDUCTED. THE INSPECTION REVEALED THAT THE FAILURE OF THE RT MLG WAS DUE TO A BROKEN RT MLG DRAG BRACE.  THE DRAG BRACE BROKE AT ABOUT THREE INCHES FROM THE BOTTOM HINGE WHERE ATTACHES TO THE RT MLG STRUT. IT APPEARS THAT OVER THE YEARS THE DRAG BRACE DEVELOPED AN INTERNAL CRACK WHICH CAUSED THE STRUCTURE OF THE DRAG BRACE TO WEAKEN CAUSING THE RT MLG TO COLLAPSE.THE INSPECTION OF THE DRAG BRACE REVEALS THE FOLLOWING DISCREPANCIES:- THE BOTTOM HINGE GREASE FITTING WAS LOOSE. THE HINGE BUSHING WAS FROZEN IN-PLACE AND SHOWED SIGNS OF CORROSION ON THE INSIDE WALLS OF THE BUSHING.  THE BUSHING BOLT WAS WORN DUE TO SPINNING WITHIN THE BUSHING.- THE TOP HINGE BUSHING HAD MINOR SCORING CORROSION WITHIN THE INSIDE WALLS OF THE BUSHING.- THE DRAG BRACE TUBE SHOWS SIGNS OF CORROSION ALL ALONG THE INSIDE WALLS OF THE TUBE.AFTER FURTHER ANALYZING ALL OF THE FACTS MENTIONED ABOVE THIS OCCURRENCE IS CONSIDERED A MINOR INCIDENT.  THE AIRCRAFT SPARS/RIBS WERE NOT DAMAGED AND NO PILOT INJURIES WERE INVOLVED.

20101218054602A	ON DECEMBER 18, 2010, SOUTHWEST AIRLINES (SWA) FLIGHT 3944 (N650SW) RECEIVED CLEARANCE FROM PHL RAMP CONTROL 2 FOR PUSHBACK FROM GATE E-11 AT 1103 EST.  IT WAS SUBSEQUENTLY PUSHED ONTO THE CENTERLINE FOR THE EAST TAXIWAY BETWEEN TERMINALS E & F AND DISCONNECTED FROM THE PUSHBACK TUG.  AT 11:06 EST, SWA FLIGHT 2592 (N913WN) CALLED FOR AND RECEIVED PUSH CLEARANCE FROM GATE E-9 FROM PHL RAMP CONTROL 2.   AIRCRAFT N650SW WAS POSITIONED ON THE TAXIWAY CENTERLINE BEHIND GATE E-9 WITH BOTH ENGINES RUNNING, PARKING BRAKE SET AND CALLED RAMP 2 FOR TAXI CLEARANCE AT 11:06 EST (APPROXIMATELY 30 SECONDS AFTER N913WN'S CALL FOR PUSH CLEARANCE).  AS N913WN WAS BEING PUSHED IN A TURN TO ALIGN WITH THE CENTERLINE OF THE TAXIWAY WITH #2 ENGINE RUNNING, ITS AFT LEFT WING STUCK THE RIGHT WINGLET OF N650SW.  THE LOWER LEFT HORIZONTAL STABILIZER OF N913WN ALSO CONTACTED THE TOP OF THE RIGHT HORIZONTAL STABILIZER OF N650SW.  THE STABILIZER DAMAGE APPEARED TO CONSIST MOSTLY OF PAINT TRANSFER.  THE DAMAGE TO N650SW APPEARED TO BE CONFINED TO THE WINGLET.  THE DAMAGE TO N913WN WAS SUBSTANTIAL AND RESULTED IN A BREACH OF THE FUEL SURGE TANK AND SUBSTANTIAL DAMAGE TO THE REAR SPAR OF THE LEFT WING.  THERE WERE NO REPORTED INJURIES ON EITHER AIRCRAFT TO THE PASSENGERS. THE TAPES FROM RAMP 2 RECORDED THE CLEARANCE GIVEN TO THE FLIGHT CREW OF N913WN AS "PUSH APPROVED, CALL FOR TAXI."  THE FLIGHT CREW CONVEYED THIS INFORMATION TO THE PUSH CREW.  DURING INTERVIEWS WITH BOTH ON-SCENE WITNESSES AND THE PUSH CREW FOR N913WN, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THERE WAS LOSS OF COMMUNICATION AND/OR VISUAL CONTACT BETWEEN THE TUG DRIVER AND WING WALKER.  THE WING WALKER WAS AWARE OF THE AIRCRAFT IN THE ALLEY BEHIND N913WN AND WAS SIGNALING FOR THE TUG DRIVER TO STOP THE PUSH. THE TUG DRIVER STATED THAT WHILE HE KNEW THE APPROXIMATE POSITION OF AIRCRAFT IN THE ALLEY, HE COULD NOT SEE THE AIRCRAFT FROM HIS POSITION AND HE COMMENCED HIS PUSH ONCE HE RECEIVED THE PUSH CLEARANCE FROM THE FLIGHT CREW.  THE BREAKDOWN IN THIS VITAL LINK BETWEEN THE WING WALKER AND THE TUG DRIVER CONTRIBUTED TO THE COLLISION OF THESE TWO AIRCRAFT.  THERE WAS NO REPORT OF THE COLLISION TO PHL OPERATIONS, RAMP 2 OR ANY REQUESTS MADE FOR PHILADELPHIA FIRE AND RESCUE RESPONSE.  APPROXIMATELY 1 HOUR AFTER THE COLLISION, THE AIRCRAFT WERE TOWED APART AND BACK TO THE GATE WITH PASSENGERS ON-BOARD.  THIS ACCIDENT HIGHLIGHTS SEVERAL CONCERNS OVER POST-ACCIDENT PASSENGER SAFETY PROCEDURES AND POSSIBLE BREAKDOWNS IN NOTIFICATION AND COMMUNICATION PROCEDURES.   THESE ITEMS WILL BE FORWARDED TO THE APPROPRIATE ORGANIZATIONS FOR THEIR REVIEW AND ACTION. SEE RELATED ATQA# AEA1710036 FOR N650SW

20110214002129I	NEARING THE COMPLETION OF A PRODUCTION TEST FLIGHT, THE AIRCRAFT WAS ESTABLISHED INSIDE THE FINAL APPROACH FIX FOR RUNWAY 30.  WITH FLAPS SET TO 20 DEGREES, THE CREW EXTENDED THE LANDING GEAR.  SHORTLY THEREAFTER, THE "LEFT HYDRAULIC QUANTITY LOW" ANNUNCIATOR ILLUMINATED.  THE CREW SELECTED THE HYDRAULIC SYNOPTIC PAGE AND NOTICED THAT THE LEFT SYSTEM HYDRAULIC QUANTITY WAS DECREASING.  NEXT, THE "LEFT HYDRAULIC SYSTEM FAIL" ANNUNCIATOR ILLUMINATED.  SINCE THE AIRCRAFT WAS ALREADY IN A LANDING CONFIGURATION BELOW 1,000 FEET AGL, THE CAPTAIN ELECTED TO CONTINUE THE APPROACH TO A LANDING.  THE CREW STATED THAT SINCE THE AUXILIARY HYDRAULIC SYSTEM RESERVOIR STILL CONTAINED FLUID AND THAT THE EMERGENCY/PARKING BRAKE ACCUMULATOR WAS CHARGED TO 3,000 PSI, THE EXPECTATION WAS TO HAVE FULL HYDRAULIC SYSTEM CAPABILITY EXCEPT FOR LEFT ENGINE THRUST REVERSE AFTER LANDING.  UPON TOUCHDOWN, HOWEVER, THE CAPTAIN DISCOVERED THAT NORMAL BRAKING WAS INOPERATIVE.  BECAUSE OF THE POSSIBILITY OF TIRE BLOWOUT (NO ANTI-SKID CAPABILITY), THE CAPTAIN STATED THAT HE DID NOT UTILIZE THE EMERGENCY BRAKES.  WITH APPROXIMATELY 3,000 FEET OF RUNWAY REMAINING, THE CAPTAIN INITIATED A GO AROUND BY ADVANCING THE THROTTLES TO TAKEOFF POWER.  THE FIRST OFFICER, WHO FELT THAT THE AIRCRAFT WAS NOT SUFFICIENLY ACCELERATING TO EFFECT A SAFE TAKEOFF, RETARDED THE THROTTLES TO IDLE.  THE AIRCRAFT DEPARTED THE DEPARTURE END OF RUNWAY 30 WHILE TRAVELING AT 95 KNOTS.  THE AIRCRAFT CAME TO A STOP APPROXIMATELY 2,000 FEET OFF THE RUNWAY END AND SLIGHTLY RIGHT OF THE EXTENDED RUNWAY CENTERLINE.  THE LEFT MAIN LANDING GEAR COLLAPSED.  ALL THREE OCCUPANTS EXITED THE AIRCRAFT THROUGH THE MAIN CABIN ENTRY DOOR.   THE INVESTIGATION SHOWED THAT UPON LANDING GEAR EXTENSION, THE NOSE LANDING GEAR SWIVEL ASSEMBLY CRACKED WHICH ALLOWED THE LEFT AND AUXILIARY SYSTEM HYDRAULIC FLUID TO BE PUMPED OVERBOARD.  WHEN THE CREW WAS FIRST MADE AWARE OF THE PROBLEM ON FINAL APPROACH TO RUNWAY 30, THE AUXILIARY HYDRAULIC SYSTEM RESERVOIR STILL CONTAINED FLUID AND SHOULD HAVE ALLOWED FOR NORMAL BRAKING CAPABILITY UPON LANDING.  HOWEVER, IN THE RELATIVELY SHORT PERIOD OF TIME BETWEEN SAID DISCOVERY AND TOUCHDOWN, THE REMAINING AUXILIARY RESERVOIR FLUID WAS PUMPED OVERBOARD WHICH RENDERED THE NORMAL BRAKES INOPERATIVE.  ACCORDING TO THE GULFSTREAM G550 "LEFT SYSTEM AND AUXILIARY HYDRAULIC SYSTEM LOSS OF FLUID" CHECKLIST, THE AIRCRAFT SHOULD BE LANDED ON A RUNWAY THAT IS AT LEAST 7,000 FEET LONG AND 150 FEET WIDE WITH A CROSSWIND COMPONENT OF LESS THAN 5 KNOTS.  THE AIRPLANE CAN THEN BE BROUGHT TO A STOP WITH THE USE OF RIGHT THRUST REVERSE, SPEED BRAKES, AND THE APPLICATION OF EMERGENCY BRAKES.  RUNWAY 30 AT ATW IS 6501 FEET LONG BY 150 FEET WIDE AND THE WIND AT THE TIME OF THIS INCIDENT WAS 340 DEGREES AT 10 KNOTS.

WHEN LANDING WAS IMMINENT HE PULLED THE MIXTURE TO CUT OFF, FUEL SELECTOR WAS PLACED TO OFF POSITION, THE IGNITION WAS TURNED TO THE OFF POSITION AND UNLATCHED THE DOORS. ONCE ON FINAL HE ADDED FLAPS AND TURNED THE BATTERY MASTER OFF. AFTER TOUCH DOWN HE STATES, THE AIRCRAFT DECELERATED PRETTY QUICKLY AND AT ALMOST A COMPLETE STOP THE AIRCRAFT HIT A WASH TEARING THE NOSE GEAR OFF THE AIRCRAFT, STOPPING IMMEDIATELY THERE AFTER. DAMAGE TO THE AIRCRAFT EXHIBITED, THE NOSE GEAR SHEARED OFF, FIREWALL DAMAGE, LOWER ENGINE COWLING, AND EXHAUST STACK. THERE WAS NO EVIDENCE OF A PROPELLER STRIKE OR FIRE. THE CFI AND STUDENT SUSTAINED NO INJURIES.ON FEBRUARY 16, 2011 AN INSPECTION OF THE AIRCRAFT ON SCENE BY THE SDL-FSDO REVEALED NO OBVIOUS DEFECTS WITH THE ENGINE. THE FUEL TANKS EXHIBITED SUFFICIENT FUEL. THE LEFT FUEL TANK HAD A VISUAL FUEL CAPACITY TO THE BOTTOM OF THE FILLER NECK. THE RIGHT FUEL TANK HAD A VISUAL CAPACITY APPROXIMATELY ? OF AN INCH BELOW THE FILLER NECK. FUEL WAS STRAINED FROM THE LEFT AND RIGHT WINGS SUMPS AND FUEL STRAINER. NO WATER OR CONTAMINANTS WERE EXHIBITED. THE CONTENT WAS BLUISH IN COLOR AND SMELLED LIKE AVGAS. POSITION OF THE ENGINE CONTROL EXHIBITED THE THROTTLE ? FULL, MIXTURE WAS FULL RICH AND CARBURETOR HEAT WAS ON. THE FUEL SELECTOR WAS IN THE OFF POSITION. THE FUEL WAS DRAINED BY ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL FROM THE LEFT WING TANK AND MEASURED APPROXIMATELY 15 US GALLONS, THE RIGHT WING TANK MEASURED APPROXIMATELY 17 US GALLONS. ON FEBRUARY 23, 2011 INSPECTOR FROM THE SDL-FSDO PERFORMED A DETAILED ENGINE INSPECTION. NO OBVIOUS DEFECTS WITH THE ENGINE WERE NOTED. THE AIRCRAFT WAS RIGGED WITH AN EXTERNAL FUEL SUPPLY AND THE ENGINE WAS GROUND RUN. THE ENGINE WOULD RUN AND IDLE FOR A BRIEF AMOUNT OF TIME AND WOULD NOT ACCELERATE WITH THROTTLE. HE ALSO SAID "THE ONLY THING THAT SEEMED TO MAKE A DIFFERENCE IN ENGINE PERFORMANCE WAS PUMPING THE THROTTLE."  EVERY TIME THE THROTTLE WAS PUSHED IN, THE ACCELERATOR PUMP WOULD GIVE THE ENGINE A SHORT BURST OF POWER.  GETTING ONLY ENOUGH POWER TO SLOW THE DESCENT RATE TO 100 FEET PER MINUTE, HE REALIZED HE WAS NOT GOING TO MAKE IT BACK TO THE AIRPORT. THE CAR IMPACTED THE AIRCRAFT ON ITS RIGHT SIDE, BREAKING THE WING STRUT AND DAMAGING THE RIGHT SIDE OF THE FUSELAGE. THE TWO VEHICLES REMAINED IN CONTACT WITH EACH OTHER AS THEY LEFT THE RIGHT SIDE OF THE ROAD, CROSSED THE DITCH AND CAME TO A STOP AFTER HITTING A FENCE.  THE ACCIDENT CAUSED SUBSTANTIAL DAMAGE TO THE FUSELAGE, ENGINE FIREWALL AND RIGHT WING AS WELL AS DESTROYING THE PROPELLER, DAMAGING THE RIGHT HORIZONTAL STABILIZER, BREAKING THE ENGINE MOUNTS AND SHEARING OFF THE NOSE STRUT AND RIGHT MAIN LANDING GEAR.FAA INSPECTORS EXAMINED THE AIRCRAFT THE FOLLOWING MORNING. AFTER ENSURING THE ENGINE WAS GETTING AIR, FUEL AND IGNITION SPARK, THEY REMOVED THE MUFFLER AND FOUND THE STARBOARD BAFFLE HAD BROKEN ITS WELD AND WAS BLOCKING THE EXHAUST PIPE. THE CAPTAIN THEN VERBALLY DIRECTED THE LEAD FLIGHT ATTENDANT TO EVACUATE OUT THE MAIN CABIN DOOR, HOWEVER, PASSENGERS AT THE EXIT ROWS BEGAN TO EXIT THE AIRCRAFT THROUGH THE OVER WING EXITS. THREE PASSENGERS FROM THE OVER WING EXITS EGRESSED TO THE RAMP AND OTHER PASSENGERS WERE ON THE LEFT AND RIGHT WINGS. THE AFT FLIGHT ATTENDANT DECIDED TO USE THE TAIL CONE EMERGENCY EXIT, BUT IT WAS NOT OPERABLE. IN HER STATEMENT, SHE INDICATED THAT SHE ATTEMPTED TO USE THE FORWARD AND AFT RELEASE HANDLES (LOCATED IN THE TAIL CONE AREA) BUT TO NO AVAIL. THE REAR STAIRS WERE LOWERED (PRESUMABLY BY GROUND PERSONNEL) AND ONE PASSENGER WAS ABLE TO WALK DOWN TO THE RAMP PRIOR TO THE FLIGHT ATTENDANT BLOCKING THE EXIT AS UNUSABLE. AT SOME POINT, THE REAR TAIL CONE JETTISONED WITH THE REAR ESCAPE SLIDE INFLATING. IT IS STILL UNCLEAR WHY THE TAIL CONE AND SLIDE DEPLOYED LATE, THEREFORE, AN INVESTIGATION CONTINUES TO DETERMINE THE REASON FOR THE MALFUNCTION. THE CAPTAIN HALTED THE EVACUATION WHEN HE DETERMINED THE FIRE WAS OUT. THE PASSENGERS ON THE WINGS WERE BROUGHT BACK INTO THE AIRCRAFT THROUGH THE EMERGENCY EXITS, AND DEPLANED NORMALLY. BASED ON AN ON SCENE INVESTIGATION BY AN FAA INSPECTOR FROM THE DAL ATL CMU, IT APPEARS THAT THERE WAS INTENSE HEAT FROM ARCING IN THE EXTERNAL POWER RECEPTACLE, BUT NO FIRE. THE AIRCRAFT RECEIVED DAMAGE TO THE ALUMINUM STRUCTURE AROUND THE EXTERNAL POWER RECEPTACLE AS WELL AS THE RECEPTACLE ITSELF. A PERTINENT MAINTENANCE DISCREPANCY WAS NOTED ON FEBRUARY 4, 2011 WHEN MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL REPLACED THE EXTERNAL POWER MONITOR.  THIS INCIDENT WAS REPORTED TO THE NTSB PURSUANT TO PART 830. THERE WERE NO INJURIES REPORTED.

20110418020509I	AN ANONYMOUS CALL WAS RECEIVED AT THE WICHITA FLIGHT STANDARDS DISTRICT OFFICE ON JUNE 14, 2011. THE COMPLAINANT STATED THAT HE WAS SCHEDULED TO FLY A RENTAL AIRCRAFT BASED AT THE WESTPORT AIRPORT, WICHITA, KS, AND UPON THE PREFLIGHT, IT WAS NOTED THAT THE LEFT WINGTIP WAS DAMAGED. BY REFERENCE TO THE SCHEDULE BOOK IN THE MAINTENANCE OFFICE, IT WAS NOTED THE LAST ENTRY DATED APRIL 18, 2011, SHOWED THE PILOT'S NAME. THE COMPLAINANT INFORMED INSPECTORS THAT HE KNEW THE PILOT AND HE PROVIDED A PHONE NUMBER. INSPECTORS WERE DISPATCHED TO WESTPORT AIRPORT TO EXAMINE THE AIRCRAFT. PHOTOGRAPHS WERE TAKEN AND THE DAMAGE ON THE LEFT WINGTIP VERIFIED. PHOTOGRAPHS OF THE TACHOMETER AND HOBBS METER READINGS WERE ALSO TAKEN AND A COPY OF THE SCHEDULE BOOK WAS OBTAINED.IN A TELEPHONE INTERVIEW WITH THE PILOT, SHE STATED THAT SHE WAS RECEIVING PRACTICAL EXAM FOR THE PRIVATE AIRMAN CERTIFICATE FROM A LOCAL DESIGNATED PILOT EXAMINER, AND WAS PERFORMING A SOFT FIELD TAKEOFF FROM RUNWAY 17 AT WELLINGTON MUNICIPAL AIRPORT, WELLINGTON, KS (EGT), WHEN THE TAIL TIE DOWN POINT CONTACTED THE RUNWAY, WHICH REQUIRED THE EXAMINER TO TAKE CONTROL OF THE AIRCRAFT. THE AIRCRAFT WAS SUBSEQUENTLY LANDED AND EXAMINED FOR DAMAGE. THE PILOT FURTHER STATED THAT THE ONLY DAMAGE ON THE AIRCRAFT WAS A SCRAPE ON THE TAIL TIE DOWN POINT. THE AIRCRAFT WAS THEN FLOWN BACK TO WESTPORT AIRPORT AND TIED DOWN. WHEN THE PILOT WAS INFORMED THAT THE TACHOMETER AND HOBBS METER TIMES ENTERED IN THE SCHEDULE BOOK MATCHED THOSE ON THE INSTRUMENTS IN THE AIRCRAFT AND IT APPEARED SHE WAS THE LAST PERSON TO FLY THE AIRCRAFT, SHE ADAMANTLY RESPONDED THAT SHE DID NOT KNOW HOW THE AIRCRAFT DAMAGE OCCURRED, BECAUSE IT WAS NOT DAMAGED WHILE SHE HAD IT. A TELEPHONE INTERVIEW WITH THE EXAMINER NETTED SIMILAR RESULTS. HIS STATEMENTS WERE VERY SIMILAR TO THE PILOT'S AND ADDED THAT THE DAMAGE TO THE AIRCRAFT ABSOLUTELY DID NOT OCCUR ON THEIR FLIGHT.USING THE SCHEDULE BOOK AS A BASIS, THE MOST LIKELY PERSON OPERATING THE AIRCRAFT AT THE TIME OF THE DAMAGE WAS THE PILOT WHILE TAKING A CHECK RIDE FROM AN EXAMINER. HOWEVER, BOTH ADAMANTLY DENY THAT THE AIRCRAFT WAS DAMAGED ON THAT FLIGHT. THE TIME INTERVAL FROM THE LAST LOGGED FLIGHT AND FAA KNOWLEDGE OF THE DAMAGE WAS ALMOST TWO MONTHS, AND IT IS TECHNICALLY POSSIBLE TO DISABLE THE RECORDING TACHOMETER AND HOBBS HOUR METER, SO THE POSSIBILITY EXITS THAT THE AIRCRAFT WAS FLOWN AND THE TIME NOT SHOWN ON THOSE INSTRUMENTS. CONSEQUENTLY, IT CANNOT BE CONCLUSIVELY PROVEN WHO WAS OPERATING THE AIRCRAFT AT THE TIME IT WAS DAMAGED.

HE PARKED FACING EAST BETWEEN A CHAIN LINK FENCE AND A ROW OF AIRPLANES.  HE COULD SEE THAT THE PARKING AREA WAS A CUL-DE-SAC, WITH AN OPEN AREA AHEAD WHICH EXTENDED TO THE LEFT PAST A CHAIN LINK FENCE (WHICH TOOK A 90 DEGREE TURN TO PROCEED).  AFTER PICKING UP THE PASSENGER, HE STARTED ENGINES AND TAXIED FORWARD TO CLEAR THE FENCE ON THE LEFT SO HE COULD SWING LEFT TO MAKE A 180 DEGREE TURN TO THE RIGHT AND EXIT THE WAY HE CAME IN.  THE PILOT WAS OBSERVING THE CLEARANCE TO THE RIGHT IN ORDER TO MISS THE AIRCRAFT PARKED THERE.  WHEN HE LOOKED TO THE LEFT TO CHECK THE CLEARANCE OF THE FENCE HE SAW THAT HE WAS CLEAR AND TURNED TO THE LEFT, WHICH  HAD THE EFFECT OF PIVOTING THE WINGTIP BACKWARDS.  THE CLEARANCE WAS NOW GONE, BECAUSE WHEN HE STARTED TAXING FORWARD THE AIRCRAFT CONTACTED THE FENCE POST AND DAMAGED THE WINGTIP.  HE STOPPED THE AIRCRAFT TO SEE THE DAMAGE.   A MECHANIC APPROACHED AND  THE PILOT ASKED HIM, WHAT HE THOUGHT OF THE DAMAGE, I.E., COULD THE AIRCRAFT FLY  SAFELY?  THE MECHANIC REPLIED THAT "IT WOULD BE THE PILOTS CALL."  THE PILOT SURVEYED THE DAMAGE AND DETERMINED VISUALLY THAT THE AIRCRAFT HAD NO STRUCTURAL DAMAGE, ONLY WHAT THE PILOT CONSIDERED TO BE COSMETIC DAMAGE TO THE METAL OF THE WINGTIP.  HE USED HIS JUDGEMENT OF 42 YEARS EXPERIENCE AS A PROFESSIONAL PILOT AND OVER 15,000 HOURS FLIGHT TIME TO DETERMINE THAT IT COULD FLY SAFELY UNTIL REPAIRS COULD BE PERFORMED.

THE TROUBLESHOOTING OF THE AIRCRAFT PINPOINTED A DISCREPANCY WITH A HYDRAULIC HOSE.  THIS HOSE (STRATOFLEX, P/N 111417-4S-160) IS CONNECTED TO THE INPUT SIDE OF THE LEFT LANDING GEAR ACTUATOR.  THE HOSE MALE FITTING (NIPPLE) BECAME DISCONNECTED FROM THE SOCKET ALLOWING THE HYDRAULIC FLUID TO LEAK OUT PREVENTING THE LANDING GEAR HYDRAULIC SYSTEM FROM DEVELOPING THE PRESSURE REQUIRED TO BRING THE LANDING GEAR TO THE DOWN AND LOCK POSITION.  A "MALFUNCTION OR DEFECT REPORT" WAS FILED, REPORT NUMBER 2011FA0000304.

20110526013449A	ON MAY 26TH, 2011, AT APPROXIMATELY 1445 LOCAL TIME (1945 UTC), AN AIRLINE TRANSPORT PILOT WAS INVOLVED IN AN AIRCRAFT ACCIDENT WHILE ATTEMPTING TO CONDUCT A RUN-ON LANDING FOLLOWING AN INTENTIONAL AUTOROTATION; THIS FLIGHT OPERATION WAS IN CONJUNCTION WITH A MAINTENANCE EVALUATION OF THE ROTOR TRACK AND BALANCE.  THE ACCIDENT OCCURRED 6.1 NAUTICAL MILES (NM) NORTHWEST OF THE NEWTON CITY COUNTY AIRPORT (KEWK), NEWTON, KANSAS; ACTUAL LOCATION OF THE ACCIDENT SITE IS IN CLOSE PROXIMITY TO WALTON, KANSAS.   THE AIRCRAFT INVOLVED IN THIS ACCIDENT IS OWNED AND OPERATED BY A TITLE 14 CODE OF FEDERAL REGULATIONS (CFR) PART 135 ON-DEMAND HELICOPTER EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES (HEMS) OPERATOR.  VISUAL METEOROLOGICAL CONDITIONS (VMC) PREVAILED AT THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENT; CLEAR SKIES, 10 STATUE MILES OF VISIBILITY AND NORTHEASTERLY WINDS AT 8 KNOTS WERE REPORTED VIA THE NEWTON CITY COUNTY AIRPORT AUTOMATED WEATHER OBSERVATION SYSTEM.  PER THE AIRMAN'S STATEMENT, THE HELICOPTER WAS CONDUCTING A MAINTENANCE FLIGHT TO COMPLETE A TRACK AND BALANCE CHECK; THIS WAS THE EIGHTH (8TH) MAINTENANCE FLIGHT OF THIS PARTICULAR DAY.  PER THE OPERATOR, IN ORDER TO COMPLETE THE REMAINING TRACK AND BALANCE CHECK, AN AUTOROTATION WAS PLANNED WITH A POWERED RECOVERY.  THE AUTOROTATION, PER THE AIRMAN, WAS INITIATED AT APPROXIMATELY 3,000 FT. MSL BY REDUCING THE POWER AND DOWN COLLECTIVE; A FIELD WAS CHOSEN IN THE EVENT OF AN EMERGENCY LANDING.  UPON INITIATING THE AUTOROTATION, THE HELICOPTER WAS FLYING AT APPROXIMATELY 60 KNOTS; INITIAL ENGINE INDICATIONS WERE NORMAL.  AT APPROXIMATELY 500 FT AGL, THE AIRMAN STATED THAT HE ELECTED TO INITIATE THE POWERED RECOVERY BY SLOWLY ADDING POWER.  AS THE HELICOPTER WAS DESCENDING THROUGH 300 FT AGL, THE AIRMAN INDICATED THAT THE LOW ROTOR RPM ANNUNCIATOR LIGHT ILLUMINATED, AND AN AUDIBLE WARNING HORN WAS HEARD.  THE AIRMAN STATED THAT THE ROTOR RPM INDICATED 80 %.  ADDITIONAL DOWN COLLECTIVE WAS APPLIED AND POWER WAS SLOWLY ADDED TO INITIATE THE POWERED RECOVERY; HOWEVER, BASED UPON THE HELICOPTER'S CURRENT ALTITUDE AND DESCENT RATE, HE ELECTED TO CONDUCT A RUN-ON LANDING IN THE FIELD.   THE HELICOPTER'S APPROACH TO THE DOWN-SLOPING, TERRACED WHEAT FIELD WAS IN A NORTH-NORTHWESTERLY DIRECTION; APPROXIMATE HEADING WAS 340 DEGREES MAGNETIC.  THE HELICOPTER'S SKIDS INITIALLY CONTACTED THE WHEAT FIELD AND TRAVELED APPROXIMATELY 63 FEET PRIOR TO THE FRONT RIGHT SKID, IMPACTING THE TERRACED, SOFT GROUND.  UPON THE RIGHT SKID IMPACTING THE GROUND, THE HELICOPTER FIRMLY LANDED; THE RESULTANT TOUCHDOWN CAUSED THE TAIL SECTION TO BE SEPARATED FROM THE FUSELAGE BY THE MAIN ROTOR BLADE.  THE HELICOPTER'S SUBSEQUENT NOSE-LOW ATTITUDE CAUSED THE LOW-MOUNTED WIRE CUTTER TO PENETRATE INTO THE SOFT EARTH, ULTIMATELY CAUSING THE HELICOPTER TO ROLL INVERTED, RESTING APPROXIMATELY 21 FEET FROM THE INITIAL SKID IMPACT POINT.  AN INSPECTION OF THE WRECKAGE REVEALED THAT ALL FLIGHT CONTROL SURFACES AND ENGINE CONTROLS WERE OPERATING PROPERLY, WITH CONTINUITY TO EACH SYSTEM ESTABLISHED.  SEVERAL ATTACHMENT POINTS AND ROTOR TRANSMISSION PARTS DISPLAYED OVERLOAD INDICATIONS.  THE HELICOPTER'S MAIN ROTOR REMAINED ATTACHED WITH MINIMAL LEADING EDGE DAMAGE.  INITIAL INVESTIGATION INDICATES THAT THERE WERE NO AIRCRAFT MAINTENANCE ISSUES PRIOR TO THE ACCIDENT.  UPON RECOVERY, 31 GALLONS OF JET A FUEL WERE STRAINED FROM THE HELICOPTER'S FUEL TANK; ADDITIONAL FUEL REMAINED WITHIN THE HELICOPTER'S MAIN FUEL BLADDER.  A FUEL SAMPLE WAS RETRIEVED FROM THE HELICOPTER'S FUEL SYSTEM FOR ADDITIONAL TESTING.  ADDITIONAL TESTING OF THE HELICOPTER'S ENGINE BY THE MANUFACTURER DID NOT REVEAL THE PRESENCE OF ANY ANOMALY THAT WOULD HAVE CONTRIBUTED TO, OR WOULD HAVE BEEN INDICATIVE OF, AN ENGINE FAILURE.  THE AIRMAN AND THE AIRFRAME & POWERPLANT MECHANIC ON-BOARD THE HELICOPTER SUSTAINED MINOR INJURIES AS A RESULT OF THE ACCIDENT.

THE AIRPORT MANAGER WHO RESPONDED TO THE ACCIDENT INDICATED THAT HE LOOKED IN THE COCKPIT WHEN HE ARRIVED ON THE SCENE AND TOOK PHOTOGRAPHS AND HE OBSERVED THE GEAR HANDLE IN WHAT HE DESCRIBES AS A MID POSITION, NEITHER ALL THE WAY UP OR DOWN.THE AIRCRAFT WAS RECOVERED FROM THE RUNWAY BY LIFTING IT ONTO A TRAILER AND SUPPORTED BY OLD AUTO TIRESAND PLACED IN THE FBO HANGAR.THIS INSPECTOR ARRIVED AT THE FBO HANGAR AND BEGUN AN INVESTIGATION OF THE AIRCRAFT AND THE DAMAGE TO IT AS WELL AS TROUBLESHOOTING THE MAIN LANDING GEAR FAILURE TO RETRACT ISSUE.THE AIRCRAFT WAS LIFTED OFF THE TRAILER USING AIRCRAFT JACKS AND THE TRAILER WAS REMOVED. A MORE DETAILED EXAMINATION OF THE DAMAGE WAS THEN CONDUCTED RESULTING IN THE FINDINGS OF STRUCTRUAL DAMAGE THEREBY CLASSIFYING THIS AS AN ACCIDENT. THE AICRAFT WAS POWERED UP AND THE LANDING GEAR WAS SELECTED TO THE DOWN POSITION, THE ONLY REACTION TO THE GEAR BEING SELECTED DOWN WAS THE AUDIBLE SOUND OF THE SOLENOID ENGAGING BUT THE GEAR DID NOT MOVE NOR DID THE GEAR PUMP OPERATE. AN INSPECTION WAS MADE OF THE GEAR MOTOR WHICH SHOWED THAT THE MOTOR BRUSHES WE COMPLETELY DESTROYED, ALL THAT REMAINED WAS DUST AND DEBRIS FROM THE BRUSHES.AT THIS POINT THE GEAR EMERGENCY LEVER WAS ACTUATED AND ALL THREE LANDING GEAR DEPLOYED SMOOTHLY AND RAPIDLY INTO THE DOWN AND LOCKED POSITION WITH A VISUAL INDICATION OF THREE IN THE GREEN IN THE COCKPIT.THE AIRCRAFT WAS THEN LOWERED TO ITS GEAR AFTER DOUBLE CHECKING THE GEAR FOR SECURITY. AN INTERVIEW WITH THE PILOT WAS CONDUCTED BEFORE AND AFTER THE ACTUAL WORK ON THE AIRCRAFT AND THE PILOT STATED THAT HE DID NOT FOLLOW THE CHECK LIST, WHICH WAS ON BOARD, NOR DID HE THINK TO TRY THE EMERGENCY GEAR HANDLE BEFORE COMMITING TO LANGING WITH THE GEAR UP. THE AIRCRAFT WAS IN CURRENT ANNUAL INSPECTION AND HIS REGULATORY PILOT RECURRENT EVENTS WERE MET.

20110724017639A	N164BF, AN EXPERIMENTAL, AMATEUR BUILT RV-6 AIRCRAFT LOST ENGINE POWER AND GLIDED TO LAND ON THE NATCHUR PARKWAY IN KY. THE AIRCRAFT TOUCHED DOWN ON THE NORTHBOUND LANES. TO AVOID IMPACTING VEHICLES THAT THE AIRCRFT WAS APPROACHING, THE PILOT MOVED THE AIRCRAFT CLOSE TO THE CENTER MEDIAN. DURING DECELERATION, THE AIRCRAFT VEERED SHARPLY TO THE LEFT, CROSSING THE MEDIAN, DAMAGING THE RIGHT MAIN LANDING GEAR AND RESPECTIVE ENGINE MOUNT. THE AIRCRAFT THEN STRUCK A GUARDRAIL AT APPROXIMATELY 30 TO 35 KNOTS AND STOPPED. THE FIREWALL WAS BUCKLED, AND THERE WAS DAMAGE TO THE UNDERSIDE OF THE RIGHT WING, RIGHT WING AILERON AND TAILWHEEL. THE PILOT STATED THAT HE RUNS AUTOMOTIVE GAS IN THE RIGHT MAIN TANK AND BOTH AUXILIARY TANKS, AND 100LL AVGAS IN THE LEFT MAIN TANK.  AUX TANKS ARE ONLY USED ON LONG TRIPS. THEY HAD NOT BEEN USED FOR APPROXIMATELY 8 - 9 MONTHS BEFORE THE ACCIDENT TRIP. THE PILOT STATED THAT HE THOUGHT HE HAD DRAINED THE AUX TANKS COMPLETELY, BUT HE STATED THERE IS A CHANCE THE RIGHT SIDE WAS NOT COMPLETELY EMPTY.  FOR THE FIRST TIME IN 8 - 9 MONTHS, THE AUX TANKS WERE TOPPED OFF FOR THE ACCIDENT TRIP.  THE PILOT STATED THAT HE DEPARTED AND CLIMBED TO ALTITUDE, UTILIZING 100LL FUEL OUT OF THE LEFT MAIN FUEL TANK AS NORMAL. ONCE REACHING ALTITUDE, THE PILOT STATED THAT HE SWITCHED THE FUEL SELECTOR TO AUX TANKS. HE STATED THAT THE AIRCRAFT RAN FOR A LITTLE BIT AND THEN "STUMBLED." HE PUT THE ELECTRIC BOOST PUMP ON AND DID NOT GET FUEL PRESSURE INDICATION.  HE SWITCHED BACK TO THE LEFT MAIN TANK AND WAS UNABLE TO GET THE ENGINE RUNNING AGAIN. INVESTIGATION REVEALED CONTAMINATION COMPLETELY BLOCKING THE FUEL INLET SCREEN TO THE CARBURETOR. AN OILY SUBSTANCE THAT APPEARED LIKE VARNISH FROM OLD AUTO GAS WAS FOUND IN FUEL LINES, ELECTRIC BOOST PUMP AND ELECTRIC FUEL PUMP SCREEN.  THE FUEL SMELLED OF VARNISH. INDICATIONS OF THE SUBSTANCE WERE TRACED FROM THE CARBURETOR INLET BACK THROUGH THE SYSTEM TO THE RIGHT AUXILIARY TANK. VISUAL INSPECTION OF THE RIGHT AUXILIARY TANK REVEALED THE VARNISH TYPE SUBSTANCE IN A DRIED STATE ON THE BOTTOM OF THE FUEL TANK. WHEN AUX TANKS WERE SELECTED DURING CRUISE FLIGHT, CONTAMINATION FROM THE RIGHT AUXILIARY TANK MAY HAVE BEEN PUSHED THROUGH THE SYSTEM, CLOGGING THE FUEL SCREENS, PREVENTING THE POSSIBILITY OF RESTART.  COUNSELING OF PILOT ON FUEL PROCEDURES HAS BEEN COMPLETED. A SAFETY RECOMENDATION WILL BE SUBMITTED FOR THIS EVENT.

THERE WERE NO REPORTED INJURIES TO ANY OF THE PASSENGERS. THAT INSPECTOR RESPONDED TO THE INCIDENT REPORT BY TRAVELING TO THE SCENE TO CONDUCT AN INVESTIGATION. ON ARRIVAL AT THE CHICAGO O'HARE E-TERMINAL GATES, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT DELTA AIRLINES, MD-88 AIRCRAFT, REGISTRATION NUMBER N970DL, FLIGHT NUMBER 1777, ORD TO ATL WITH 76 PASSENGER AND 5 CREW MEMBERS HAD BEEN PUSHED BACK FROM GATE E-13  INTO DELTA AIRLINES A-319 AIRCRAFT, REGISTRATION NUMBER N332NB, FLIGHT NUMBER 2207 WITH 129 PASSENGERS AND 5 CREWMEMBERS. DURING THE COURSE OF THIS INVESTIGATION IT WAS DETERMINED THAT AIRCRAFT N332NB HAD BEEN PUSHED BACK FROM TERMINAL GATE E-15 AND HAD REQUESTED TAXI INSTRUCTIONS FROM GROUND CONTROL. GROUND CONTROL GAVE TAXI INSTRUCTIONS BUT BEFORE AIRCRAFT N332NB WAS ABLE TO MOVE AWAY FROM THE E-15 GATE AREA, AIRCRAFT N970DL WAS PUSHED INTO ITS RIGHT WING TIP. MD-88 AIRCRAFT N970DL HAD REQUESTED PUSH BACK FROM GATE FROM GATE E-13 AND WAS INFORMED BY GROUND CONTROL THAT THEY COULD PUSH BACK ONCE THEY WERE CLEARED OF COMPANY AIRCRAFT. THE CREW OF N970DL ASSUMED THAT THEY WERE CLEAR OF COMPANY AIRCRAFT AND REQUESTED PUSH BACK FROM THE TUG OPERATOR. THE TUG OPERATOR THEN INITIATED PUSH BACK WITHOUT WAITING FOR CLEARANCE FROM THE RAMP WING WALKERS.    AIRCRAFT N970DL SUSTAINED DAMAGE TO THE LEFT AFT UPPER PORTION OF THE UNPRESSURIZED FUSELAGE ABOVE THE AIRSTAIR AREA AND TO THE TAILCONE ASSEMBLY. THAT DAMAGE INCLUDED A FUSELAGE PUNCTURE ABOUT 10 INCHES IN LENGTH AND OTHER SURFACE DISTORTION. AIRCRAFT N332NB SUSTAINED DAMAGE TO THE RIGHT WING TIP FAIRING OR WINGLET. DELTA AIRLINES MAINTENANCE REMOVED THE DAMAGED RIGHT WING FAIRING (WINGLET) FROM N332NB AND DEFERRED IT PER THE CDL. THE AIRCRAFT DEPARTED IN REVENUE SERVICE THE FOLLOWING MORNING. THE MD-88 AIRCRAFT, N970DL WAS TAKEN TO THE OLD NORTHWEST HANGAR TO AWAIT A MAINTENANCE CREW.THE DELTA AIRLINES TUG OPERATOR WAS SUBSEQUENTLY TESTED FOR DRUGS AND ALCOHOL. THE RESULTS OF THOSE TEST WERE NEGATIVE. AT THE PRESENT TIME DELTA AIRLINES CONTINUES WITH THEIR INTERNAL INVESTIGATION OF THIS INCIDENT AND HAVE NOT FORMULATED A CORRECTIVE ACTION PLAN.THE DELTA AIRLINES MAINTENANCE TEAM THAT ARRIVED AT ORD SHORTLY AFTER THIS INCIDENT COMPLETED THE REPAIRS TO AIRCRAFT N970DL ON AUGUST 8, 2011. THEY REPAIRED THE DAMAGE TO THE LEFT AFT FUSELAGE AREA PER (ERA) ENGINEERING REPAIR AUTHORIZATION NUMBER 494957-14 AND MD-88 DRAWING 9911842. ALL WORK WAS DOCUMENT ON NON ROUTINE LOG FORMS AND ALL OPERATIONAL AND FUNCTIONAL CHECK WERE ACCOMPLISHED. IN ADDITION THE (RII) REQUIRED INSPECTIONS WERE ACCOMPLISHED AND THE AIRCRAFT WAS RELEASED FOR SERVICE AND FERRIED OUT OF ORD ON AUGUST 9, 2011.

THIS CORRELATES TO ABOUT FIFTEEN GALLONS OF FUEL IN EACH FUEL TANK.  HE CALCULATED THAT WITH A 9.5 GALLONS OF FUEL PER HOUR HE HAD ABOUT THREE HOURS OF FLIGHT TIME REMAINING.  AFTER THE PREFLIGHT AND THE ENGINE RUN UP WERE CONDUCTED, THE AIRCRAFT DEPARTED THE NORTH PERRY AIRPORT (HWO) RUNWAY 9 LEFT AT ABOUT 1815 HOURS.  THE PILOT CONTACTED THE MIAMI APPROACH CONTROL AND WAS ASSIGNED TRANSPONDER CODE 0150 AND WAS CLEARED TO PROCEED ON A EASTERLY HEADING TOWARD THE MIAMI SHORE LINE.   UPON REACHING THE OCEAN REEF AIRPORT, MIAMI APPROACH CONTROL CONTACTED THE PILOT AND WAS ASSIGNED TRANSPONDER CODE 1200.  AT THIS TIME, THE FUEL SELECTOR WAS CHANGED TO THE RIGHT FUEL TANK.  THE PILOT PROCEEDED ON A SOUTH WEST HEADING UNTIL REACHING THE CITY OF TAVERNIER.  AT THIS TIME, THE PILOT TURNED TO A NORTHERLY HEADING.  WHEN THE PILOT REACHED THE EVERGLADE COASTLINE, AGAIN, HE CHANGED THE FUEL SELECTOR TO THE LEFT FUEL TANK.  HE CONTACTED THE MIAMI APPROACH CONTROL AND WAS ASSIGNED TRANSPONDER CODE 4346.  AS HE CONTINUED ON A NORTHERLY HEADING, HE PASSED THE TMB AIRPORT AT 1,500 FEET.  AT THIS TIME, THE ENGINE STARTED TO CUT OFF AND HE IMMEDIATELY APPLIED FULL RICH MIXTURE, FUEL PUMP, AND CHANGED THE FUEL SELECTOR TO THE RIGHT FUEL TANK.  THE PILOT STATED ON HIS WRITTEN REPORT THAT "THE LEFT FUEL GAUGE WAS ON EMPTY AND WHILE RIGHT FUEL GAUGE WAS IN THE YELLOW BAND".  HE THEN CALLED THE MIAMI APPROACH CONTROL AND NOTIFIED THEM THAT HE WAS DIVERTING TO THE TMB AIRPORT INSTEAD OF CONTINUING TO THE HWO AIRPORT AS HE HAD PLANNED.  HE CONTACTED THE TMB AIRPORT TOWER AND REPORTED HIS POSITION.  THE PILOT STATED ON HIS WRITTEN REPORT THAT " SHORTLY, STILL AT 1,500 FEET ALTITUDE THE ENGINE STARTED TO BECOME IRREGULAR AND LOOSING POWER AGAIN, REPORTED THE SITUATION TO TMB TOWER SUSPECTING FUEL STARVATION".  THE TMB TOWER GAVE HIM PRIORITY AND HE WAS CLEARED TO RUNWAY NINE LEFT.  THE PILOT HAD THE RUNWAY IN SIGHT, HOWEVER, EVEN WITH THE POWER LEVER TO FULL POWER, THE ENGINE POWER WAS BECOMING MORE AND MORE INTERMITTENT AND HE WAS UNABLE TO MAINTAIN ALTITUDE.  DUE TO THE ENGINE COMPLETE LOST OF POWER, THE PILOT MADE AN EMERGENCY LANDING ON A LARGE PLOWED FARM FIELD LOCATED ABOUT A MILE WEST OF THE END OF TMB AIRPORT RUNWAY NINE LEFT. ON AUGUST 22, 2011, PERSONNEL FROM THIS OFFICE INSPECTED THE AIRCRAFT AND NO PHYSICAL DAMAGE TO THE AIRCRAFT WAS NOTICED.  THE LEFT AND RIGHT FUEL TANKS CAPS WERE REMOVED AND NO SIGNS OF FUEL WAS NOTICED INSIDE OF THE FUEL TANKS.  THE LEFT AND RIGHT FUEL TANK MANUAL DRAINS WERE OPENED AND A SMALL AMOUNT OF FUEL WAS DRAINED FROM BOTH LEFT AND RIGHT WING FUEL TANKS.  THE ENGINE GASCOLATOR SUMP WAS OPENED AND NO FUEL CAME OUT.  DURING THE INTERVIEW WITH THE PILOT HE STATED THAT THE AIRCRAFT WAS LAST REFUELED ON JULY 30, 2011 AND ON THE SAME DATE THE AIRCRAFT FLEW 4.0 HOURS PER THE HOBB METER.  ON AUGUST 21, 2011, THE DATE OF THE EMERGENCY LANDING THE AIRCRAFT FLEW 1.6 HOURS BEFORE THE ENGINE STOP RUNNING.  PER THE HOBB METER THE AIRCRAFT FLEW A TOTAL OF 5.6 HOURS WITHOUT BEING REFUELED.  ON AUGUST 23, 2011, THE AIRCRAFT WAS TRANSPORTED FROM THE OFF FIELD LANDING LOCATION TO THE TMB AIRPORT.  AT THE TMB AIRPORT THE AIRCRAFT WAS REFUELED AND IT TOOK 58 GALLONS OF FUEL.  THE AIRCRAFT IS TYPE CERTIFICATED TO HOLD 59.8 GALLONS TOTAL WITH 57.2 USABLE FUEL.  ON AUGUST 24, 2011, THE AIRCRAFT WAS  INSPECTED AND RETURNED TO SERVICE.  THE AIRCRAFT WAS REPOSITIONED FROM TMB AIRPORT TO HWO AIRPORT WITHOUT ANY DISCREPANCY.

20110904020339I	ON SUNDAY, SEPTEMBER 4, 2011, AT 11:34 PACIFIC STANDARD TIME, A DARK GREEN 1983 SIAI-MARCHETTI, N260DP TAXIED ONTO RUNWAY 21 FOR A VISUAL DEPARTURE SOUTHWEST BOUND. DURING THE TAKE-OFF ROLL AT APPROXIMATELY 45 KNOTS THE NOSE GEAR OF THE AIRCRAFT RETRACTED WHILE THE AIRCRAFT'S MAIN WHEELS WERE STILL ON THE RUNWAY. THE AIRCRAFT'S THREE BLADED HARTZEL PROPELLER STRUCK THE RUNWAY SURFACE AND THE AIRCRAFT VEERED TO THE RIGHT SIDE OF THE RUNWAY COMING TO REST ON THE INFIELD APPROXIMATELY 400 FEET FROM THE BEGINNING OF THE TAKE-OFF ROLL ADJACENT TO THE WIND SOCK.THE PILOT WAS UNAWARE THAT THE LANDING GEAR LEVER HAD BEEN ACCIDENTALLY PLACED IN THE UP POSITION AT THE TIME THE AIRCRAFT WAS SERVICED ON SEPTEMBER 1, 2011. THE MECHANIC WHO IS EMPLOYED BY THE OWNER OF THE AIRCRAFT WAS ASKED TO INSPECT AND SERVICE ONE OF THE LANDING GEAR INDICATOR LIGHT BULBS. THE MECHANIC HAD PLACED THE LANDING GEAR LEVER IN THE UP POSITION TO BETTER ACCESS THE INDICATOR RHEOSTAT AND BULB. THE MECHANIC FAILED TO ASSURE THE LANDING GEAR LEVER WAS IN THE DOWN POSITION AT THE COMPLETION OF WORK.ON THE DAY OF THE FLIGHT, THE PILOT FAILED TO POSITIVELY CHECK THE LANDING GEAR CONTROL LEVER DURING THE PRE-FLIGHT OF THE AIRCRAFT.THE LANDING GEAR IS A RETRACTABLE TRICYCLE LANDING GEAR WHICH CONSISTS OF A MAIN LANDING GEAR, AND NOSE LANDING GEAR. THE NOSE LANDING GEAR CONSISTS OF A SINGLE WHEEL MOUNTED ON A SHOCK STRUT AND RETRACTING REARWARD INTO THE FUSELAGE NOSE SECTION. THE LANDING GEAR SYSTEM IS PROVIDED WITH A SAFETY SYSTEM (SQUAT SWITCH) TO PREVENT THE INADVERTENT RETRACTION WHEN ON THE GROUND. HOWEVER, THE AIRCRAFT PILOT OPERATING HANDBOOK (POH) NOTES: "MOVEMENT OF THE AIRCRAFT DURING GROUND RUNS CAN DISACTIVATE THE SAFETY SWITCH." THE SQUAT SWITCH IS LOCATED ON THE LEFT MAIN LANDING GEAR STRUT. WHEN THE MAIN LANDING GEAR STRUT EXTENDS THE SWITCH IS DEPRESSED, THUS CLOSING THE ELECTRICAL CIRCUIT AND ENERGIZING THE SYSTEM. WHEN THE LANDING GEAR LEVER IS IN THE "UP" POSITION WITH THE SWITCH DEPRESSED THE ELECTROMECHANICAL ACTUATOR WILL BEGIN THE RETRACTION CYCLE OF THE LANDING GEAR.DURING THE TAKE-OFF ROLL AS THE AIRCRAFT BEGAN TO ENTER GROUND EFFECT THE AIRCRAFT'S MAIN WHEELS BEGAN TO LIFT FROM THE RUNWAY WHILE THE NOSE WHEEL WAS STILL ON THE RUNWAY. THIS "WHEELBARROW" EFFECT CAUSED THE SAFETY SQUAT SWITCH TO BECOME DEPRESSED DEACTIVATING THE SAFETY SYSTEM AND BEGINNING THE RETRACTION CYCLE OF THE LANDING GEAR. THE COMBINED WEIGHT ON THE NOSE OF THE AIRCRAFT AND THE FORWARD THRUST BEING PRODUCED BY THE PROPELLER CREATED A PITCH DOWN MOMENT. AS THE NOSE BEGAN TO RETRACT IN THE WHEEL WELL THE PROPELLER STRUCK THE RUNWAY. THE PILOT ABORTED THE TAKEOFF AND THE AIRCRAFT VEERED TO THE RIGHT OF THE RUNWAY WITH THE NOSE RETRACTED AND THE TWO MAIN LANDING GEAR STRUTS EXTENDED.

THE AIRCRAFT THEN TRAVELED APPROXIMATELY ANOTHER 146 FEET ON A HEADING OF APPROXIMATELY 120 DEGREES UNTIL A STRAND OF BARBED WIRE THAT HAD BECOME ENTANGLED WITH THE NOSE GEAR WAS STRETCHED FROM THE ATTACHMENT POINT ON A FENCE POST TO THE MAXIMUM LENGTH OF THE WIRE.  SUCH BARBED WIRE ACTUALLY FUNCTIONED AS AN "ARRESTING WIRE" HOOKED TO THE NOSE GEAR, CAUSING THE AIRCRAFT TO MAKE A SHARP PIVOT TO THE LEFT AND COME TO REST ON A HEADING OF APPROXIMATELY 335 DEGREES.  ALL PERSONS ABOARD N9249L EXITED THE AIRCRAFT AND SUSTAINED NO INJURY THROUGHOUT THE EVENT.THE FLIGHT INSTRUCTOR REPORTED NO PRE-ACCIDENT MECHANICAL DEFECTS ASSOCIATED WITH THE OPERATION OF N9249L, AND A POST ACCIDENT INVESTIGATION REVEALED NO PRE-ACCIDENT MECHANICAL ISSUES THAT COULD HAVE CONTRIBUTED TO THE ACCIDENT.  ACCORDINGLY, THE PRIMARY CAUSAL FACTOR ASSOCIATED WITH THE ACCIDENT OF N9249L WAS THE FLIGHT INSTRUCTOR'S FAILURE TO INTERVENE AND ASSUME CONTROL OF THE AIRCRAFT FROM HIS STUDENT BEFORE THE AIRCRAFT DESCENDED AND SLOWED TO AN ALTITUDE AND AIRSPEED THAT WAS NOT RECOVERABLE, THUS ALLOWING THE AIRCRAFT TO STRIKE OBSTACLES ON THE GROUND.
20110921025349I	09/21/2011.  THE STUDENT PILOT AND INSTRUCTOR TAXIED TO RUNWAY 10 VIA TAXIWAY ALPHA AND ECHO.  A DEPARTURE TAKEOFF, FOLLOWED BY A TOUCH-AND-GO LANDING WAS PERFORMED WITHOUT INCIDENT.  ON THE SECOND APPROACH AND LANDING, THE AIRCRAFT TOUCHED DOWN AT THE RUNWAY MARKINGS.  WHEN THE NOSE WHEEL TOUCHED DOWN AT APPROXIMATELY TAXIWAY DELTA, THE STUDENT FLYING THE AIRCRAFT AND THE INSTRUCTOR THOUGHT THAT THE NOSE WHEEL TIRE WAS FLAT.  IN ACTUALITY, THE NOSE GEAR FORK AND TIRE SEPARATED FROM THE NOSE STRUT AT TOUCHDOWN, AND THEY WERE ROLLING OUT ON THE MAIN LANDING GEAR AND THE NOSE GEAR LEG MINUS TIRE/WHEEL.  THE INSTRUCTOR TOOK CONTROL OF THE AIRCRAFT AND LIFTED THE NOSE TO ALLEVIATE INDUCED STEERING ADVERSITY AND REGAIN DIRECTIONAL CONTROL.  WHEN LIFT WAS BLED OFF, THE NOSE GEAR LEG AGAIN CONTACTED THE RUNWAY.  THE INSTRUCTOR MAINTAINED SPEED AS MUCH AS POSSIBLE TO GET THE AIRCRAFT OFF OF THE RUNWAY AND TO EXECUTE A TURN AT TAXIWAY CHARLIE.  AT THE INTERSECTION OF RUNWAY 10 AND TAXIWAY CHARLIE, THE AIRCRAFT SPEED HAD SLOWED CONSIDERABLY.  THE NOSE STRUT ENCOUNTERED IRREGULARITIES IN THE PAVEMENT THAT STOPPED FORWARD MOMENTUM AND CAUSED THE NOSE LANDING GEAR ASSEMBLY (P/N 22-3220-00-00) TO BE DISLODGED FROM THE AIRFRAME.  THE AIRCRAFT PROPELLER CONTACTED THE PAVEMENT AS THE NOSE DROPPED AND WAS DESTROYED.  WHEN THE PILOTS EXITED THE AIRCRAFT THEY NOTED THAT THE NOSE WHEEL FORK (P/N 20-3220-08-00) AND THE TIRE/WHEEL ASSEMBLY WERE MISSING.  INVESTIGATION FOUND THE FORK/TIRE/WHEEL PARTS TO THE LEFT SIDE OF RUNWAY 10 NEAR TAXIWAY DELTA THAT COINCIDE WITH THE TOUCH DOWN AREA.  DURING THE SUBSEQUENT INSPECTION OF THE RUNWAY AND TAXIWAY FOR DEBRIS, SEVERAL ADDITIONAL PARTS WERE FOUND ON TAXIWAY ALPHA, NORTHEAST OF TAXIWAY CHARLIE.  THE PARTS FOUND ARE THOSE OF A DIAMOND AIRCRAFT DA-20, AND WERE NOT PRESENT AT THE AIRCRAFT OR ON THE RUNWAY IN THE AREA THAT THE FORK WAS FOUND.  THE PARTS CONSISTED OF A BROKEN STUD APPROXIMATELY ONE INCH LONG WITH THE CASTELLATED NUT (P/N AN310-6) AND COTTER PIN (P/N MS24665-285) INSTALLED, TWO FLAT WASHERS (P/N AN960-616), TWO BELLEVILLE WASHERS (P/N 680-221), NOSE LANDING GEAR LOWER SPACER (P/N 20-3220-00-24) AND THE NOSE LANDING GEAR STEERING STOP PLATE (P/N 20-3220-00-23).  THE CONCLUSION IS THAT THE FOUND PARTS HAD FALLEN FROM N166SE WHILE TAXIING ON ALPHA EN ROUTE TO RUNWAY 10 PRIOR TO THE FIRST DEPARTURE.  IT REMAINS UNCLEAR WHY THE NOSE FORK DID NOT BECOME DISLODGED AT THIS TIME OR AT ROTATION OF THE FIRST DEPARTURE TAKEOFF WHEN THE AIRCRAFT WEIGHT WAS REMOVED FROM THE NOSE GEAR.  THERE WAS NO DAMAGE TO THE AIRPORT PROPERTY OR SIGNAGE.

AFTER THE ASSEMBLY WAS TORQUED AND A COTTER-KEY WAS INSTALLED, THE INSPECTION AND PINCH-FIT OF THE MECHANISM LED THE MECHANICS TO BELIEVE THAT THE ASSEMBLY WAS ATTACHED PROPERLY. FLIGHT CONTROL MOVEMENTS AND A MAINTENANCE TEST FLIGHT WERE PERFORMED WITH NO INDICATION THAT THE PITCH CHANGE CONTROL TUBE WAS INSTALLED IMPROPERLY. THE INCORRECT INSTALLATION WAS THE RESULT OF INADEQUATE MAINTENANCE INSTRUCTIONS FOR THIS 'FIRST-TIME' INSTALLATION. THIS INSTALLATION WAS INSPECTED BY FOUR DIFFERENT TECHNICIANS, ALL OF WHOM FELT THAT THE INSTALLATION WAS CORRECT. WHILE REPOSITIONING THE AIRCRAFT, WITH TWO MECHANICS ON BOARD, WHILE IN HOVER OVER THE END OF THE RUNWAY, THE TAIL ROTOR PITCH CHANGE CONTROL TUBE CAME FREE FROM THE BELLCRANK. THE PILOT WAS ABLE TO SAFELY LAND.

THE EXTENT OF THE DAMAGE TO THE RIGHT ENTRY DOOR MADE THE DETERMINATION; IF THE RIGHT ENTRY DOOR WAS SECURED PRIOR TO TAKEOFF OR IF THE RIGHT ENTRY DOOR FORWARD LATCH MECHANISM FAILED, VIRTUALLY IMPOSSIBLE TO DETERMINE AS THE CONTROL RODS, WITHIN ENTRY DOOR, WERE BROKEN AND THE REAR DOOR LATCH WAS SEPARATED FROM THE DOOR. BOTH PILOTS INDICATED THAT DOORS WERE SECURED AND WERE CHECKED FOR SECURITY BY PUSHING ON FORWARD AND REARWARD PARTS OF DOOR PRIOR TO TAKEOFF.INSPECTION OF LEFT ENTRY DOOR LATCH MECHANISM REVEALED NO DISCREPANCIES AND OPERATED NORMALLY.  LATCH MECHANISM HAS THE SAME BASIC TYPE OF OPERATION THAT MANY CARS DO.  WHEN THE DOOR IS PULLED CLOSED THE LATCH IS DEPRESSED BY THE DOOR POST, RELEASING A LOCK ALLOWING THE HANDLE TO BE PUSHED FORWARD TO THE LATCHED POSITION.  IF OPERATING PROPERLY, THE HANDLE CANNOT BE PUSHED TO THE LATCHED POSITION, UNLESS THE LATCHES HAVE BEEN ENGAGED BY THE DOOR POSTS, WHICH THEN ALLOWS THE LATCH TO BE SECURED TO THE DOOR POST. CLOSER INSPECTION OF LEFT ENTRY DOOR LATCH MECHANISM REVEALED THAT WHEN DOOR IS CLOSED, AND IN THE LATCHED POSITION, THE LATCH IS BEING HELD TO THE DOOR POST ONLY ON THE VERY BOTTOM PORTION OF THE LATCH.

20111020025619I	THE ROOT CAUSE OF THIS INCIDENT RESULTING IN AN AIRCRAFT ROUTE DEVIATION (WITH NO LOSS OF SEPARATION) WAS THE FLIGHTCREW'S INABILITY TO IDENTIFY AND TO FLY THE REVISED HIGH ALTITUDE JET AIRWAY ROUTING THAT BECAME EFFECTIVE ON THE DATE OF THIS INCIDENT.  THE FLIGHTCREW REFERRED TO A CURRENT, BUT INCORRECT NAVIGATION CHART PRODUCED BY JEPPESSEN AND PROVIDED BY THE COMPANY AS PRIMARY FOR NAVIGATION.THIS CHARTING ERROR COMBINED WITH THE AIRCRAFT'S FLIGHT MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (FMS) DEFERRAL DID NOT PROVIDE THE FLIGHTCREW AN OPPORTUNITY TO ACCURATELY IDENTIFY THE REDEFINED JET AIRWAY AND SUBSEQUENTLY NAVIGATE ALONG THE CLEARED ROUTE.  IF THE FMS HAD BEEN USABLE ON THE DATE OF THE INCIDENT, THE VALID ELECTRONIC DATABASE WOULD HAVE PROVIDED THE FLIGHTCREW WITH THE CORRECT AIRWAY ROUTING AND SUBSEQUENTLY ALLOWED THE CREW TO NAVIGATE ALONG THE REDEFINED JET AIRWAY.  FURTHERMORE, EVENTHOUGH THE FLIGHTCREW FOLLOWED STATED PROCEDURES PERTAINING TO MEL PROVISIONS FOR THIS DEFERRAL, MEL PROVISIONS AS CURRENTLY WRITTEN ARE INADEQUATE TO PREVENT RECURRENCE OF A SIMILAR INCIDENT.  THEREFORE, THE COMPANY IS CURRENTLY EVALUATING BOTH DISPATCH SYSTEM / MEL PROVISIONS FOR RISK IDENTIFICATION AND MITIGATION.

ON NOVEMBER 15, 2011, THE OBV WAS EXAMINED AND THE FRACTURED MUSCLE LINE ATTACHMENT FITTING WAS DETERMINED TO HAVE BEEN CRACKED PRIOR TO THE FAILURE.  THERE HAVE BEEN A NUMBER OF SIMILAR FAILURES AND HONEYWELL IS WORKING WITH THE NTSB TO IDENTIFY A PROBABLE ROOT CAUSE. AT THIS TIME, THE NTSB HAS CUSTODY OF THE RELEVANT PARTS AND THE INVESTIGATION.

THE ADDISON TOWER PERSONNEL OBSERVED THIS DEVIATION AND ALSO NOTED N227TX'S ALTITUDE WAS BELOW THE GLIDESLOPE.  ADDISON TOWER PERSONNEL NOTIFIED N227TX OF HIS LOW ALTITUDE AND OFF COURSE SITUATION.  AT THAT POINT N227TX INITIATED A MISSED APPROACH.  ADDISON TOWER ISSUED A CLEARANCE TO CLIMB TO 2000 FT AND TURN LEFT HEADING 050.  N227TX WAS THEN PASSED BACK TO DALLAS NORTH CONTROLLER FOR VECTORS BACK TO THE RWY 15 ILS FOR A SECOND ATTEMPT.  AT 1131AM N227TX WAS CLEARED BY DALLAS NORTH CONTROLLER FOR THE ILS RWY 15.  WITHIN SECONDS OF TURNING ON COURSE N227TX STATED HE WAS NOT RECEIVING THE LOCALIZER, AND ASKED IF IT WAS WORKING.  AT 1132 N227TX DECLARED AN EMERGENCY.  ATC ISSUED A HEADING OF 150 DEGREES, AND 4 MILES FROM THE AIRPORT.  AT 1133:19AM RADAR DATA INDICATED N227TX BEGAN A LEFT TURN.  AT 1133:54 THE RADAR DATA TAG FOR N227TX WAS LOST FROM THE RADAR SCREEN.FAA INVESTIGATORS ARRIVED ON SCENE AT APPROXIMATELY 1245PM.  AS A RESULT OF THE CRASH SEQUENCE THE RIGHT WING WAS DETACHED FROM THE AIRCRAFT.  THERE WAS NO ODOR OF FUEL ANYWHERE.  THE LEFT WING WAS STILL ATTACHED TO THE AIRCRAFT AND VERTICAL TO THE GROUND.  THERE WAS NO FUEL NOTICED TO BE LEAKING FROM EITHER WING.  WHEN THE CONTINENTAL MOTORS, INC AIR SAFETY INVESTIGATOR INSPECTED THE ENGINE THERE WERE NO SIGNS OF FUEL.  THE PILOT AND FRONT SEAT PASSENGER SURVIVED THE CRASH.  THE PASSENGER IN THE BACK SEAT DID NOT.NUMEROUS ATTEMPTS HAVE BEEN MADE BY THE INVESTINGATING INSPECTOR TO OBTAIN INFORMATION TO COMPLETE BLOCKS 29 AND 31.  HOWEVER PILOT HAS NOT RESPONDED TO ANY REQUESTS.

VISUAL METEOROLOGICAL CONDITIONS PREVAILED AND NO FLIGHT PLAN WAS FILED FOR EITHER FLIGHT. THE LOCAL FLIGHT FOR THE PIPER PA-44-180 ORIGINATED FROM THE MC MINNVILLE MUNICIPAL AIRPORT (MMV), MC MINNVILLE, OREGON, ABOUT 1536, DESTINED FOR THE AURORA STATE AIRPORT, AURORA, OREGON. HE THEN BRIEFED THE PILOT RECEIVING INSTRUCTION ON THE PROCEDURES FOR A SIMULATED EMERGENCY DECENT WHILE CONDUCTING VARIOUS CLEARING TURNS. THE CFI STATED THAT THE PILOT RECEIVING INSTRUCTION THEN EXECUTED THE SIMULATED EMERGENCY DESCENT AND RECOVERED TO CRUISE FLIGHT AT AN ALTITUDE OF ABOUT 4,500 FEET MSL. THE FLIGHT THEN PROCEEDED ON A NORTHERLY HEADING TOWARDS UAO WITH THE INTENT OF ENTERING THE AIRPORT TRAFFIC PATTERN. THE CFI FURTHER REPORTED THAT WHILE MAINTAINING AN ALTITUDE OF 4,500 FEET MSL, HE WAS SCANNING THE AREA FOR TRAFFIC AND OBSERVED A SINGLE-ENGINE AIRPLANE ON A CONVERGENCE COURSE TOWARDS HIS LOCATION THAT APPEARED TO BE IN A SLIGHTLY STEEPER THAN AVERAGE DESCENT. HE INSTRUCTED THE PILOT RECEIVING INSTRUCTION TO INITIATE A LEFT DESCENDING TURN IN AN EFFORT TO AVOID THE OBSERVED TRAFFIC. FOLLOWING AN APPROXIMATE 10 TO 20-DEGREE HEADING CHANGE, THE CFI RE-ESTABLISHED VISUAL CONTACT WITH THE SINGLE-ENGINE AIRCRAFT THAT WAS BEHIND AND ABOVE HIS POSITION. SUBSEQUENTLY, HE FELT A JOLT ALONG WITH A VIOLENT SHUDDER IN THE AIRPLANE FOLLOWED BY AN UN-COMMANDED LEFT ROLL AND YAW. THE CFI IMMEDIATELY TOOK CONTROL OF THE AIRPLANE AND THOUGHT THEY HAD POSSIBLE STRUCK GEESE. HE THEN INITIATED AN EMERGENCY FORCED LANDING TO A NEARBY OPEN FIELD.WITNESSES LOCATED IN VARIOUS AIRCRAFT ADJACENT TO THE ACCIDENT SITE REPORTED THAT PRIOR TO THE COLLISION; THEY OBSERVED THE BEECH V35 ON A NORTHERLY COURSE IN CRUISE FLIGHT.EXAMINATION OF THE ACCIDENT SITE REVEALED THAT THE WRECKAGE OF THE TWO AIRPLANES WAS SCATTERED OVER AN AREA OF ABOUT 2 MILES. DEBRIS FROM BOTH AIRPLANES, INCLUDING THE EMPENNAGE, TAIL CONE, AND REAR SEAT, FROM THE BEECH V35 AND NOSE COWLING FROM THE PIPER PA-44-180 WERE LOCATED ALONG THE DEBRIS PATH, WHICH WAS LOCATED IN CHAMPOEG STATE PARK. THE BEECH V35 CAME TO REST UPRIGHT ABOUT 0.3 MILES NORTH OF THE CHAMPOEG STATE PARK AND WAS MOSTLY CONSUMED BY FIRE. THE PIPER PA-44-180 CAME TO REST UPRIGHT IN AN OPEN FIELD ABOUT 1.5 MILES WEST OF CHAMPOEG STATE PARK. THE WRECKAGES OF BOTH AIRCRAFT WERE RECOVERED TO A SECURE FACILITY AWAITING FURTHER EXAMINATION.

20111027029219I	ON 10/27/2011 ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ WHILE CONDUCTING AN INSTRUCTIONAL FLIGHT AND ACTING AS PILOT IN COMMAND OF A GREAT LAKES BI-PLANE, REGISTRATION NUMBER N6075L, DID LOSE CONTROL DURING LANDING RESULTING IN A PARTIAL GROUND LOOP AND MINOR DAMAGE TO THE WING FABRIC ON THE RIGHT WING LOWER SKIN. 10/31/2011 DURING A TELEPHONE DISCUSSION WITH ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^, HE INDICATED THAT THE TAIL WHEEL DEVELOPED A SIGNIFICANT SHIMMY DURING LANDING. ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ EXPLAINED THAT HE MADE THREE ATTEMPTS TO "UNLOAD AND RELOAD" THE FLIGHT CONTROLS IN AN EFFORT TO MINIMIZE OR ELIMINATE THE SHIMMY. AFTER EACH ATTEMPT AND AS THE AIRCRAFT SLOWED DOWN THE SHIMMY INCREASED IN INTENSITY. ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ EXPLAINED THAT AFTER THE THIRD ATTEMPT, THE AIRCRAFT EXITED THE RUNWAY TO THE LEFT, RESULTING IN THE PARTIAL LOOP.10/31/2011 DISCUSSION WITH OFFICE AIRWORTHINESS INSPECTORS PERTAINING TO THIS EVENT, IT WAS EXPLAINED  THAT THE "SCOTTS" TAIL WHEEL ASSEMBLY IS PRONE TO THIS BEHAVIOR IF NOT PROPERLY SERVICED DUE TO SMALL RETAINING LUGS THAT TEND TO WEAR OUT.  FURTHER INVESTIGATION REQUIRED.11/01/2011 DURING A TELEPHONE CONVERSATION WITH ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^, CHIEF PILOT, HE STATED HE HAD FLOWN THAT SAME AIRCRAFT THE AFTERNOON OF THE PREVIOUS DAY AND EXPERIENCED NO TAIL WHEEL SHIMMY. ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ ALSO STATED THAT HE FELT ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ MAY NOT BE COMFORTABLE WITH BRAKING DURING LANDINGS AND THAT THEY WERE PLANNING TO FLY TOGETHER TO WORK ON BRAKING AS A LAST OPTION FOR AIRCRAFT CONTROLLABILITY DURING LANDINGS. THREE-INCH-DEEP GROUND DISRUPTIONS OF SIMILAR SHAPE AND LENGTH TO BOTH WINGS, AND THE VERTICAL STABILIZER, WERE NOTED 4-FEET NORTHWEST OF THE CRATER.  FRAGMENTS OF GREEN LENS MATERIAL WERE LOCATED AT THE TIP OF THE NORTHEAST GROUND DISRUPTION CORRESPONDING TO THE RIGHT WING, WITH RED LENS FRAGMENTS NOTED AT TIP OF THE SOUTHWEST GROUND DISRUPTION, CORRESPONDING TO THE LEFT WING.  FRAGMENTS OF RED LENS MATERIAL, AS WELL AS THE TAIL-MOUNTED VOR ANTENNA WERE LOCATED AT THE TIP OF THE NORTHWEST DISRUPTION.A DEBRIS FIELD CONTAINING CABIN ITEMS, SEAT FRAGMENTS AND SECTIONS OF AIRFRAME SKIN, EMANATED FROM THE INITIAL IMPACT. THE ENTIRE SECTION HAD SUSTAINED THERMAL DAMAGE, CONSISTENT WITH POST-ACCIDENT FIRE. THE DEBRIS PATH WAS ORIENTED OPPOSITE THE PRESUMED DIRECTION OF TRAVEL.

THE PIC STATED THAT IT WAS A ROLLING TAKEOFF - HE DID NOT IMMEDIATELY BRING THE POWER TO THE TO POSITION, BUT ADVANCED THE THROTTLES SMOOTHLY AS THE AIRCRAFT BEGAN TO ROLL DOWN THE RUNWAY.  THE SIC STATED THAT AT APPROXIMATELY 80 TO 85 KIAS, AN AURAL 'NO TAKEOFF' WAS HEARD.  HE CHECKED THE FLAPS (AT 15 DEGREES) AND SPEED BRAKES (STOWED).  HE THEN CALLED 'ABORT, ABORT' AND THE PIC BEGAN THE ABORTED TAKEOFF PROCEDURE AROUND 110 KIAS.  THE PIC STATED THAT THE ABORT PROCEDURE WAS BEGUN BETWEEN 80 AND 90 KIAS, PRIOR TO V1.THE AIRCRAFT CAME TO A STOP WITH APPROXIMATELY 10 FEET OF THE END OF THE 4300 FT RUNWAY AND THEY TRIED TO TAXI OFF.  THEY GOT THE AIRCRAFT OFF THE RUNWAY, BUT NOT ACROSS THE HOLD LINE.  THEY DID NOT REALIZE THAT BOTH MAIN TIRES HAD BLOWN OUT DURING THE ABORTED TAKEOFF.  A TUG WAS CALLED OUT TO TOW THE AIRCRAFT OFF THE RUNWAY.THE AIRCRAFT HAD TO HAVE BOTH MAIN TIRES, WHEELS, AND BRAKE ASSEMBLIES REPLACED DUE TO DAMAGE FROM HEAT.ACCORDING TO THE PIC, CESSNA HAS DETERMINED THAT THE 'NO TAKEOFF' WARNING WAS DUE TO A MIS-TRIM CONDITION WITH THE TRIM BEING LESS THAN 1% OUTSIDE THE TAKEOFF RANGE FOR THE AIRCRAFT.  HOWEVER, THE ASSOCIATED ANNUNCIATOR DID NOT ILLUMINATE.THE CESSNA AIRCRAFT REPRESENTATIVE CONTACTED STATED THAT THE ARES DATA TAKEN FROM THE AIRCRAFT INDICATED THAT THE PIC WAS MANUALLY TRIMMING THE PITCH DURING THE TAKEOFF ROLL.  THE PITCH TRIM WAS CHANGED FROM 2.5 DEGREES NOSE UP AT THE START OF THE TAKEOFF ROLL TO 1 DEGREE NOSE DOWN PITCH.  THE 1 DEGREE NOSE DOWN PITCH IS THE TAKEOFF TRIM LIMIT.  THE TRIM REACHED THIS LIMIT AT THE SAME TIME THE AIRCRAFT REACHED THE 80 KIAS THRESHOLD.  EXCEEDING THE TRIM LIMIT CAUSED THE 'NO TAKEOFF' AURAL MESSAGE BUT THE 80 KIAS KEPT THE CAS MESSAGE FROM APPEARING.  THE CESSNA REPRESENTATIVE CONFIRMED THAT THE AURAL MESSAGE DID OCCUR AT 80 KIAS BUT THE AIRCRAFT REACHED A MAXIMUM SPEED OF 135 KIAS DURING ITS TAKEOFF ROLL BEFORE THE ABORT PROCEDURE WAS BEGUN.INSPECTOR DAN WITHERS OF THE ACO ALSO PROVIDED ADDITIONAL DATA AND INFORMATION FROM CESSNA ON THIS INCIDENT.THE BALANCED FIELD LENGTH FOR THE AIRCRAFT ON THE DAY OF THE INCIDENT SHOULD HAVE BEEN 2370 FEET OR 2550 IF NO WIND EXISTED.  THE APPROPRIATE V SPEEDS SHOULD HAVE BEEN V1=94 KIAS, VR=97 KIAS, V2=111 KIAS, AND VENROUTE = 140 KIAS.  THE BALANCED FIELD LENGTH DATA ASSUMES BRAKES ARE APPLIED AT V1 AND MAXIMUM BRAKING.ADDITIONAL DATA FROM CESSNA AIRCRAFT WAS THAT THE EMERGENCY BRAKES WERE USED DURING THE ABORT PROCEDURE.  THIS FACT WAS NOT MENTIONED BY EITHER CREW MEMBER DURING THEIR INTERVIEWS.  THE PIC STATED THAT BOTH CREWMEMBERS WERE 'ON THE BRAKES HARD', BUT NEVER MENTIONED THE USE OF EMERGENCY BRAKES.BASED ON THIS INFORMATION, THE AURAL WARNING WAS SOUNDED WELL BELOW THE V1 SPEED BUT THE AIRCRAFT EXCEEDED V2 BEFORE THE ABORT PROCEDURE WAS BEGUN.

(SWOOPING IS A MANEUVER IN WHICH THE SKYDIVER OPERATES HIS CANOPY SO AS TO ACCELERATE HIS VERTICAL DESCENT SPEED PRIOR TO LANDING. THIS ALLOWS THE ENERGY BUILT UP IN DESCENT TO TRANSLATE INTO FORWARD SPEED AT THE TIME OF FLAIR WHICH PROPELS THE SKYDIVER FORWARD JUST ABOVE THE GROUND, IF TIMED CORRECTLY.) THIS JUMP WAS A PRACTICE JUMP TO FOR A SWOOPING COMPETITION WHICH WAS TO BE HELD THE NEXT WEEKEND. KE DEPLOYED HIS MAIN CANOPY WITHOUT INCIDENT AND WAS OPERATING / FLYING A FULLY DEPLOYED, PROPERLY OPERATING CANOPY ALL THE WAY TO THE GROUND. WITNESSES STATED THAT HE PERFORMED A 270 DEGREE LEFT HAND TURN TO FINAL AT THE APPROPRIATE ALTITUDE. HE WAS FOCUSING ON ENTERING A "GATE" AREA WHILE ON SHORT FINAL AND FAILED TO FLAIR THE CANOPY PRIOR TO IMPACTING THE GROUND. THE SKYDIVER LANDED IN A HIGH SPEED DESCENT WITH HIS LEGS PULLED UP AND HIT ON HIS BUTTOCKS. HE IMPACTED WITH SUFFICIENT FORCE TO BOUNCE BACK INTO THE AIR SEVERAL FEET AND THEN CAME TO REST NEAR A PACKING STRUCTURE ON THE SOUTH EAST CORNER OF THE LANDING ZONE.^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ SUSTAINED A BROKEN LEG AND BACK AND WAS AIR EVACED TO THE HOSPITAL. (CONSIDERED TO BE AN EXPERT LEVEL WING LOADING CANOPY). ACCORDING TO THE DROP ZONE SAFETY OFFICER KE HAD BEEN RECEIVING "CANOPY PILOTING" TRAINING AND DID A LOT OF SOLO CANOPY ORIENTED JUMPS. THE DZ SAFETY OFFICE ALSO STATED THAT HE AND KE HAD DISCUSSED THE RIG EARLIER IN THE DAY REGARDING THE MODIFICATIONS WHICH HAD BEEN DONE TO THE CANOPY, AS WELL AS THE HIGH INCIDENCE OF MALFUNCTIONS WHICH HAD BEEN PLAGUING HIM.THE CANOPY AND RIG ARE BEING EXAMINED BY A MASTER RIGGER AT THIS TIME TO DETERMINE WHETHER THERE ARE ANY ABNORMALITIES WHICH WOULD AFFECT THE ABILITY TO FLAIR THE CANOPY.

THE UPPER SPARK PLUGS WERE REMOVED, AND THE ELECTRODES WERE INTACT, AND ASHEN IN COLOR. A BORESCOPE EXAMINATION OF ALL SIX CYLINDERS REVEALED NORMAL WEAR, AND NO ABNORMAL DEPOSITS. BOTH MAGNETOS WERE REMOVED, AND THE RIGHT MAGNETO PRODUCED SPARK AT ALL SIX TOWERS. THE LEFT MAGNETO WAS IMPACT DAMAGED, AND COULD NOT BE ROTATED. DISASSEMBLY REVEALED THAT THE MAGNETO DRIVESHAFT WAS BENT BY IMPACT.  THE OIL PUMP DISPLAYED NORMAL FUNCTION WHEN THE ENGINE CRANKSHAFT WAS ROTATED. EMERGENCY MANUAL EXTENSION OF THE LANDING GEAR WAS NOT POSSIBLE BY THE PILOT DUE TO THE "JAMMED" CONDITION OF THE CONTROL RODS AT THE ACTUATOR. 20120323004189A	MARCH 23, 2012SYNOPSIS OF LANDING INCIDENT WITH N840JC BY ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ON THE MORNING OF MARCH 23, 2012 I PREPARED FOR A FLIGHT FROM KALISPELL, MONTANA (GPI) TO CONRAD, MONTANA (S01), SHELBY, MONTANA (SBX) AND A FINAL DESTINATION OF CUTBANK, MONTANA (CTB).  I CHECKED THE LOCAL AREA WEATHER AND NOTAMS TO INCLUDE CONRAD, CUTBANK, SHELBY, GREAT FALLS AND MISSOULA, MONTANA.   THERE WAS SNOW IN THE AREA BUT VISIBILITY WAS 2 MILES OR BETTER AT CUTBANK.  THE CEILING WAS BROKEN TO OVERCAST, WITH BROKEN LAYERS VARYING BETWEEN 500 AND 800 FEET AND AN OVERCAST LAYER ABOVE THAT.  I ALSO CHECKED THE CONRAD SUPER AWOS, A TEST SITE, AND IT WAS REPORTING THE SAME INFORMATION.   I FILED AN IFR FLIGHT PLAN FROM KALISPELL TO CONRAD, FOLLOWED BY FLIGHT PLANS TO SHELBY AND CUTBANK.  I RECEIVED AN IFR CLEARANCE FROM SALT LAKE CENTER WHILE ON THE GROUND IN KALISPELL FOR THE FLIGHT TO CONRAD.  WE WERE ENROUTE AT 15,000 FEET MSL, WITH A DECENT TO 12,000 FEET, FOLLOWED BY THE APPROACH CLEARANCE INTO CONRAD WITH THE INSTRUCTIONS TO MAINTAIN 8,000 UNTIL ESTABLISHED ON THE APPROACH.  I ALSO RECEIVED A THRU CLEARANCE TO SHELBY WITH THE INSTRUCTIONS TO MAINTAIN 9,000 FEET ON DEPARTURE.  I EXECUTED THE GPS RWY 24 APPROACH IN CONRAD.  AFTER THE PROCEDURE TURN INBOUND AT AROUND 5,000 FEET MSL I BROKE OUT OF THE CLOUDS AND HAD THE CONRAD AIRPORT IN SITE.  AT THIS POINT I WAS APPROXIMATELY 4 MILES FROM THE AIRPORT AND WAS CONFIGURED WITH GEAR DOWN, FLAPS 20 AND INDICATING 120 KTS.  AT APPROXIMATELY THREE MILES FROM THE RUNWAY I NOTICED THAT THE SNOW PLOW WAS ON THE RUNWAY AND HAD MADE SEVERAL PASSES DOWN BOTH SIDES OF THE CENTER OF THE RUNWAY, ALTHOUGH THE EDGES WERE NOT CLEARED.  I NOTICED THAT THE SNOWPLOW  WAS EXITING THE END OF THE RUNWAY.  I MADE POSITION CALLS ON THE UNICOM FREQUENCY, BUT I WAS NOT IN CONTACT WITH THE SNOW PLOW.  AT THIS POINT THE SNOWPLOW WAS CLEAR OF THE RUNWAY SO I SELECTED FLAPS 40, SLOWED TO 100 KTS, AND CONTINUED A NORMAL APPROACH TO LANDING.  I OBSERVED THAT THE RUNWAY APPEARED WET, BUT I DIDN'T NOTICE ANYTHING THAT WOULD BE A PROBLEM WITH MY LANDING.  I BEGAN MY FLARE AND AS I TOUCHED DOWN THE AIRCRAFT BEGAN TO SLIDE TO THE LEFT.  AT THIS POINT THE AIRCRAFT WAS NOT ALIGNED WITH THE RUNWAY SO I DECIDED NOT TO APPLY POWER FOR A GO AROUND AS I FELT THIS WOULD PROPEL ME OFF OF THE SIDE OF THE RUNWAY.  INSTEAD I APPLIED RUDDER PRESSURE TO ATTEMPT TO STRAIGHTEN OUT THE AIRCRAFT SO I COULD ATTEMPT THE GO-AROUND.  I WAS UNABLE TO ALIGN MYSELF SUFFICIENTLY WITH THE DIRECTION OF THE RUNWAY AS THE AIRCRAFT BEGAN TO SLIDE TO THE RIGHT.  I WAS NEVER ABLE TO GET THE AIRCRAFT ALIGNED WITH THE RUNWAY SO THAT I WOULD HAVE FELT COMFORTABLE APPLYING POWER TO EXECUTE THE GO-AROUND, SO I CONTINUED WITH RUDDER PRESSURE, ATTEMPTING TO KEEP THE AIRCRAFT ON THE RUNWAY.  WE CONTINUED TO SLIDE DOWN THE RUNWAY UNTIL THE AIRCRAFT FINALLY SLID OFF THE NORTH SIDE OF THE RUNWAY.  THE AIRCRAFT TURNED APPROXIMATELY 150 OR 160 DEGREES AS IT WAS SLIDING TO THE NORTH OF THE RUNWAY.  THERE WAS A SMALL BERM/DITCH TO THE NORTH OF THE RUNWAY THAT THE AIRCRAFT SLID THRU.  I BELIEVE THIS WAS WHEN THE LEFT GEAR COLLAPSED.  AS WE WERE SLIDING, I PULLED THE CONDITION LEVERS TO CUTOFF/FEATHER AND SELECTED FUEL EMERGENCY SHUT OFF.  I THEN TURNED OFF THE BATTERY AND ANY ADDITIONAL SWITCHES THAT WERE ON.  ALL OF THE PASSENGERS STATED THEY WERE OKAY WITH NO INJURIES.  THE EMERGENCY EXIT WINDOW CAME OUT SOMETIME DURING THE SLIDE, AND WAS LYING ON THE FLOOR.  I WAS ABLE TO MOVE THE WINDOW AND THE MAIN CABIN DOOR OPENED AND ALL PASSENGERS WERE ABLE TO EXIT THE AIRCRAFT ON THEIR OWN POWER.EXTERNAL OBSERVATION OF THE AIRCRAFT SHOWED THE NOSE GEAR HAD COLLAPSED, THE LEFT MAIN LANDING GEAR LOWER EXTENSION TUBE HAD BUCKLED AND THE WHEEL WAS LAYING 90 DEGREES ON THE GROUND.  IT APPEARED IT MAY HAVE BEEN STILL PARTIALLY ATTACHED.  THE LEFT PROP WAS FEATHERED BUT THE BLADES WERE BENT, THE LEFT WINGTIP HAD DUG INTO THE GROUND AND THE WING TIP FAIRING WAS DISPLACED.
