WHILE EN-ROUTE TO KJEF, THE AIRMAN STATED THAT THE RIGHT LOW FUEL ANNUNCIATOR LIGHT ILLUMINATED IN THE AIRCRAFT, INDICATING THAT THE FUEL IN THAT TANK WAS BELOW FIVE (5) GALLONS REMAINING.  THE AIRMAN, UNSURE AS TO HOW TO RESOLVE THIS ISSUE, ELECTED TO SEEK ADDITIONAL GUIDANCE FROM THE FLIGHT INSTRUCTOR VIA A TEXT MESSAGE.  WHEN A RESPONSE WAS NOT RECEIVED, THE AIRMAN SWITCHED TO THE LEFT FUEL TANK AND CONTINUED ON TO THE DESTINATION; AIRMAN STATED THAT A DIVERSION TO AN ALTERNATE AIRPORT WAS NEVER CONSIDERED.  UPON ARRIVAL, 12 GALLONS OF FUEL, 6 GALLONS PER SIDE, WERE ADDED TO THE AIRCRAFT. THE AIRMAN WAS ADVISED TO BUY 10 GALLONS OF FUEL AS THIS SHOULD BE SUFFICIENT; HOWEVER, 12 GALLONS WERE PURCHASED.  APPROXIMATELY 30-40 MILES WEST OF KJEF, THE AIRMAN STATED THAT THE RIGHT LOW FUEL ANNUNCIATOR, ONCE AGAIN, BECAME ILLUMINATED.  A SECOND ATTEMPT WAS MADE TO CONTACT THE FLIGHT INSTRUCTOR VIA TEXT MESSAGE; HOWEVER, NO RESPONSE WAS RECEIVED.  THE AIRMAN SUBSEQUENTLY SELECTED THE LEFT FUEL TANK AND CONTINUED ON TOWARDS THE DESTINATION. ONCE AGAIN, THE AIRMAN STATED THAT A DIVERSION TO ANOTHER AIRPORT WAS NOT CONSIDERED.  IN THE VICINITY OF ALTA VISTA, KANSAS, THE AIRMAN STATED THAT THE ENGINE FAILED; THE AIRMAN'S RADIO TRANSMISSION TO THE AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL FACILITY PROVIDING FLIGHT FOLLOWING INDICATED THAT THE AIRCRAFT HAD RUN OUT OF FUEL.  THE AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL FACILITY ATTEMPTED TO DIRECT THE AIRCRAFT TO THE NEAREST AIRPORT; HOWEVER, THE AIRMAN INDICATED THAT THE AIRCRAFT WOULD NOT REACH THAT LOCATION.  THE ENGINE FAILURE CHECKLIST WAS INITIATED BY THE AIRMAN; HOWEVER WAS NOT COMPLETED.  ACCORDING TO THE AIRMAN, THE MIXTURE WAS INCREASED TO FULL RICH AND THE FUEL SELECTOR WAS CHANGED FROM THE, "LEFT," TANK TO THE, "BOTH," POSITION.  UPON ESTABLISHING THE AIRCRAFT'S BEST GLIDE SPEED, THE AIRMAN CIRCLED A TERRACED WHEAT FIELD, IN WHICH AN EMERGENCY LANDING WAS ACCOMPLISHED.  THE AIRCRAFT DID NOT SUSTAIN ANY DAMAGE DURING THE OFF-AIRPORT EMERGENCY LANDING; THE PILOT, THE SOLE OCCUPANT ON-BOARD WAS UNINJURED.  DURING THE POST-INCIDENT INSPECTION, APPROXIMATELY 7-8 GALLONS OF AVIATION GASOLINE WAS RECOVERED; ALL FUEL-RELATED AIRCRAFT SYSTEMS WERE INSPECTED AND FULLY FUNCTIONAL.  FUEL QUANTITY INDICATORS SHOWED THE LEFT TANK AT 0 GALLONS; AIRCRAFT WAS OPERATING ON THE LEFT FUEL TANK EXCLUSIVELY PRIOR TO THE ENGINE FAILURE.  THE AIRCRAFT WAS INSPECTED BY THE DIRECTOR OF MAINTENANCE, RETURNED TO SERVICE, AND FLOWN BACK TO ITS BASE OF OPERATIONS.  SUBSEQUENT REVIEW OF THE AIRMAN'S CROSS-COUNTRY NAVIGATION LOGS REVEALED THAT MINIMUM FUEL REQUIREMENTS FOR THIS FLIGHT, INCLUDING VFR FUEL RESERVES, WERE NOT PROPERLY CALCULATED.  NAVIGATION LOGS AND FUEL CALCULATIONS INDICATE THAT THE AIRCRAFT DEPARTED ON THE RETURN FLIGHT WITH ONLY 3 GALLONS OF FUEL REMAINING.

SINCE THE DATE OF THE INCIDENT, THE AIRCRAFT COULD NOT BE LOCATED. THE AIRCRAFT MAINTENANCE LOG BOOKS CANNOT BE REVIEWED AND TO DATE ARE PRESUMED LOST. RECOVERY WAS ACCOMPLISHED BY AIR-N-SEA RECOVERY OUT OF FT. PIERCE, WITH THE ASSISTANCE OF DIVERS ASSOCIATED WITH BLUE POINT MARINE. WITNESS'S STATED THE AIRCRAFT ALTHOUGH 3 MILES OFFSHORE WAS OPERATING AT AN ESTIMATED ALTITUDE OF 12-15 FEET ABOVE THE SURFACE, CONTRARY TO THE PILOT STATEMENT. THE SEARCH FOR THE AIRCRAFT RESUMED THE NEXT DAY WITH UNSUCCESSFUL RESULTS. THE AIRCRAFT WAS FINALLY RECOVERED AND TRANSPORTED BY BARGE ON 05/09/2012. DURING MY INITIAL CURSORY INSPECTION FOUND THE AIRCRAFT HAD EXTENSIVE CORROSION ALREADY SETTING IN WHEREAS,MY INTENT WAS TO ESTABLISH FLIGHT CONTROL CONTINUITY. THIS DEEMED DIFFICULT DUE TO SAND & MUD DEPOSITS IN AND AROUND THE PEDALS,THE CONNECTING RODS,BELLCRANKS AND PUSH/PULL TUBES,AS WELL THE EXTENUATING DAMAGE IN THE TAIL SURFACE AREA CAUSED WHEN LIFTING THE AIRCRAFT FROM THE OCEAN FLOOR. THE SALVAGE COMPANY WAS TO PREP THE AIRCRAFT FOR INSPECTION UPON TRANSFER. DURING MY INSPECTION TO OBTAIN CONTINUITY I EXAMINED THE ENTIRE SYSTEM IN WHICH IS NOTHING MORE THAN A SERIES OF PUSH/PULL TUBES,LIFT STRUTS,THREE BELLCRANKS AND FOR THE FLAPERONS CONSIDERED A MIXER ASSEMBLY. AS STATED,IN THE LOSS OF ELEVATOR CONTROL, THE SYSTEM A SINGLE PUSH/PULL TUBE ATTACHED TO A CONTROL COLUMN, THEN TO AN IDLER BELLCRANK, FROM THERE ANOTHER PUSH/PULL TUBE AND APPROXIMATELY MID WAY WAS AN ELEVATOR TUBE BEARING IN BETWEEN THE MID FUSELAGE TUBE BEFORE CONNECTING TO THE CONTROL HORN. GIVEN THE LENGTH OF TIME THE AIRCRAFT WAS EXPOSED TO SALTWATER,PRIOR DAMAGE TO THE BEARING COULD NOT BE SUBSTANTIATED. HOWEVER THE FREEDOM OF MOVEMENT IN THE FWD & AFT DIRECTION WAS ACCEPTABLE WITHOUT RESTRICTION. ALTHOUGH NOT REPORTED WE DID FIND A LOSS IN RUDDER CONTINUITY AND CANNOT ESTABLISH IF DIRECTLY RELATED TO THE IMPACT. THE AIRCRAFT EQUIPPED WITH RUDDER TRIM,WAS ALSO QUESTIONABLE AS TO WHY IT WAS TRIMMED FULL RIGHT. THE PEDALS ALSO NON-RELATED WERE RESTRICTED WITHIN MOVEMENT. THE FLAPERONS HAD FREEDOM OF MOVEMENT BUT,THEY WERE SEPARATED AT THE SEAM,AS THE PILOT STATED EARLIER THEY WERE OPERATING NORMAL. FINAL INSPECTION WHEN REMOVING THE STICK BOOTS,FOUND A LEATHER GLOVE AND A 6-7 INCH PLASTIC ALLIGATOR CLIP JUST BEHIND THE PILOT'S CONTROL STICK. IT APPEARS THEY MAY HAVE BEEN PREVIOUSLY USED AND LEFT WITHOUT NOTICED AND COULD BE A CONTRIBUTING FACTOR TO THE STICK BINDING INITIALLY. THESE ITEMS ALONG WITH THE CAMERA EQUIPMENT INSTALLED AND OTHER MISCELLANEOUS EQUIPMENT BROUGHT ON BOARD BY THE OPERATOR,ALL THIS STORED ON AND AROUND THE SEAT AREA TOGETHER MAY HAVE INHIBITED FULL TRAVEL OF THE CONTROL STICK,SINCE THE DUAL STICK AIRCRAFT SOLELY RELIES ON A SINGLE TORQUE TUBE OR CONTROL COLUMN ASSEMBLY,IN WHICH TIES BOTH CONTROL STICKS TOGETHER WITHOUT THE ABILITY TO LOCK ONE OUT.

THE COURSE WAS CLOSED AT THE TIME, AND THERE WERE NO INJURIES OR DAMAGE FROM THE DOOR REPORTED.  THE DOOR AND SOME COMPONENTS WHICH HAD LANDED NEARBY, WERE SECURED AND DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING MORNING TO THE BOMBARDIER FACILITY AT FLL, WHERE THE AIRCRAFT HAD BEEN SECURED PENDING AN INVESTIGATION.THE MANUFACTURER, UPON LEARNING OF THE EVENT, CONTACTED THE NTSB AND REQUESTED TO BE A PARTY TO THE INVESTIGATION.  THE IIC WAS INFORMED THAT NTSB INVOLVEMENT WOULD BE LIMITED IN NATURE.  WITH THE CONCURRENCE OF THE NTSB, THE IIC ACCEPTED THE REQUEST AND INVITED THE MANUFACTURER TO SERVE AS A TECHNICAL ADVISOR AND PARTY TO THE INVESTIGATION.THE FOLLOWING FINDINGS WERE SIGNIFICANT:1. THE HINGE FOR THE MAIN PASSENGER DOOR WAS RELATIVELY INTACT, REMAINED ATTACHED TO THE AIRFRAME, AND OPERATED SMOOTHLY.  THE DOOR SEPARATED FROM THE HINGE ALONG THE RIVET LINE WHICH SECURED THE DOOR TO THE HINGE. 2. THE MAIN PASSENGER DOOR UPPER HALF WAS FOUND CRUSHED FROM WHAT IS BELIEVED TO BE GROUND IMPACT. 3. THE LOWER FORWARD AND AFT DOOR ROLL LATCHES WERE FOUND IN THE UNLOCKED POSITION WITH NO DAMAGE, AND OPERATED SMOOTHLY. 4. THE UPPER FORWARDED AND AFT DOOR ROLL LATCHES WERE FOUND IN THE UNLOCKED POSITION WITH NO DAMAGE AND OPERATED SMOOTHLY. 5. NO DAMAGE WAS OBSERVED TO ANY OF THE FUSELAGE MOUNTED DOOR LOCKING STRUCTURE, NOR WAS ANY DAMAGE FOUND ON THE FORWARD AND AFT FUSELAGE MOUNTED DOOR PROXIMITY SENSORS. 7. THE CONTROL ROD CONNECTING THE UPPER AND LOWER ROLL LATCHES WAS FOUND CRUSHED INSIDE THE AIR STAIR STRUCTURE. DENTS ON THE UPPER AND LOWER SURFACES OF THE CONTROL ROD CORRESPONDED WITH INTERNAL DOOR STRUCTURE, AND THE LOCATION OF THE DENTS CORRESPONDED WITH THE POSITION THE ROD WOULD BE AT IF THE DOOR LOCKING MECHANISM WAS IN THE UNLOCKED POSITION AT THE TIME THE DOOR IMPACTED THE GROUND.8. THE FUSELAGE BENEATH THE DOOR HINGE WAS FOUND TO HAVE A PENETRATION ALIGNED WITH THE EXTERNAL DOOR ASSIST HANDLE. 9. THE EXTERNAL DOOR "T" HANDLE WAS FOUND DEPLOYED, AND IN THE UNLOCKED POSITION. 10. THE FUSELAGE IMMEDIATELY BENEATH THE DOOR HAD AN IMPRESSION SIMILAR TO THE "T" HANDLE, AND WAS AT AN ANGLE ALIGNED TO THE POSITION THAT THE "T" HANDLE WOULD BE IN WHEN THE DOOR IS UNLOCKED. 11.  THE CIRCUIT BREAKERS FOR THE DOOR WARNING SYSTEM, LOCATED ON THE COPILOT'S B OUTBOARD (#160) AND D (#17) CIRCUIT BREAKER PANELS WERE OPEN.

20120524010689I	ON MAY 24, 2012, AT APPROXIMATELY 1145 LOCAL TIME (1645 UTC), A PRIVATE PILOT WAS INVOLVED IN AN AIRCRAFT INCIDENT THAT OCCURRED DURING THE LANDING ROLL-OUT AT THE FORT SCOTT MUNICIPAL AIRPORT (KFSK), FORT SCOTT, KANSAS.  THE AIRCRAFT INVOLVED IN THIS INCIDENT IS A CESSNA P-210-N, WHICH IS OWNED AND OPERATED BY THE PILOT-IN-COMMAND; THE PASSENGER ON BOARD THIS AIRCRAFT IS THE HOLDER OF AN AIRLINE TRANSPORT PILOT CERTIFICATE; HOWEVER, THIS INDIVIDUAL WAS NOT DESIGNATED AS THE PILOT-IN-COMMAND.  VISUAL METEOROLOGICAL CONDITIONS (VMC) EXISTED AT THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT; PITTSBURG ATKINSON MUNICIPAL AIRPORT (KPTS) AUTOMATED WEATHER OBSERVATION SYSTEM (AWOS), LOCATED 21 NAUTICAL MILES DUE SOUTH OF KFSK, REPORTED THE SURFACE WINDS AT 210 DEGREES AT 14 KNOTS, GUSTING TO 20 KNOTS.  ACCORDING TO THE AIRMAN'S VERBAL AND WRITTEN STATEMENT, PRIOR TO DEPARTURE, AN EXTERIOR PRE-FLIGHT INSPECTION OF THE AIRCRAFT WAS CONDUCTED.  A PRE-FLIGHT OF THE AIRCRAFT'S LANDING GEAR SYSTEM WAS ALSO PERFORMED PER THE PILOT'S OPERATING HANDBOOK (POH), INCLUDING THE ASSOCIATED LIGHTS AND AURAL WARNING HORN; NO ANOMALIES WERE NOTED.  AFTER TAKEOFF, THE PILOT STATED THAT NORMAL GEAR RETRACTION WAS PERFORMED.  DUE TO THE SURFACE WINDS AND RELATIVE AIRCRAFT POSITION TO THE LANDING RUNWAY, A STRAIGHT-IN APPROACH TO RUNWAY 18 WAS CONDUCTED.  UPON BEING ESTABLISHED ON A THREE (3) NAUTICAL MILE FINAL APPROACH TO RUNWAY 18, THE AIRMAN STATED THAT THE LANDING GEAR WAS EXTENDED; THE EXTENSION OF THE MAIN GEAR WAS VISUALLY CONFIRMED BY THE PILOT-IN-COMMAND AND PASSENGER, IN ADDITION TO THE ILLUMINATION OF THE, "GREEN," GEAR LIGHT.  THE AIRMAN STATED THAT THE LANDING GEAR AURAL WARNING SYSTEM WAS NOT AUDIBLE, NOR WAS A, "RED," UNSAFE GEAR INDICATION OBSERVED.  A SHORT FIELD APPROACH AND LANDING WAS PLANNED, AND AS PER THE POH, FULL FLAPS WERE SELECTED.  ACCORDING TO THE AIRMAN, IMMEDIATELY UPON TOUCHDOWN, AS STATED IN THE POH, THE FLAPS WERE RETRACTED TO PROVIDE GREATER AERODYNAMIC BRAKING AND A REDUCTION IN THE TOTAL LANDING DISTANCE ROLL-OUT; AIRMAN VERBALLY STATED THAT THIS IS A STANDARD PROCEDURE FOR LANDING.  AS THE AIRCRAFT DECELERATED, THE AIRMAN STATED THAT THE NOSE CONTINUED TO LOWER UNTIL SUCH TIME AS THE PROP STRUCK THE RUNWAY SURFACE.  A POST-INCIDENT INSPECTION BY THE PASSENGER, AS PROVIDED IN A WRITTEN STATEMENT, INDICATED THAT UPON RE-ENTRY INTO THE CABIN, IT WAS VISUALLY OBSERVED THAT THE FLAP HANDLE WAS STILL IN THE FULL-DOWN POSITION WITH THE WING FLAPS EXTENDED, AND THE LANDING GEAR HANDLE WAS IN THE UP OR RETRACTED POSITION.  THE AIRMAN, IN SUBSEQUENT COMMUNICATION, STATED THAT IT WAS APPARENT THAT THE LANDING GEAR HANDLE WAS INADVERTENTLY RAISED DURING THE LANDING ROLL-OUT IN LIEU OF THE FLAP HANDLE.  ACCORDING TO THE AIRMAN, THE AIRCRAFT IS CONVENTIONALLY CONFIGURED WITH THE LANDING GEAR HANDLE ON THE LEFT SIDE OF THE POWER QUADRANT, AND THE FLAP HANDLE IS POSITIONED ON THE RIGHT.  ADDITIONALLY, THE REPOSITIONING OF THE LANDING GEAR HANDLE REQUIRES THE AIRMAN TO PULL THE HANDLE OUT OF A DETENT BEFORE IT CAN BE RAISED OR LOWERED.  A POST-INCIDENT INSPECTION OF THE LANDING GEAR SYSTEM WAS PERFORMED BY A CERTIFIED AIRCRAFT MECHANIC.  THIS INSPECTION, AS STATED IN THE MECHANIC'S WRITTEN STATEMENT, DOCUMENTED THAT IT APPEARED AS THOUGH THE NOSE WHEEL WAS NOT DOWN AND LOCKED UPON TOUCHDOWN (DID NOT COLLAPSE); NORMAL NOSE GEAR EXTENSION WAS OBSERVED UPON THE OPENING OF THE NOSE GEAR DOORS THAT WERE DAMAGED UPON CONTACT WITH THE RUNWAY SURFACE.  THE AIRCRAFT SUSTAINED MINOR DAMAGE UPON TOUCHDOWN; BOTH THE PILOT-IN-COMMAND AND PASSENGER WERE UNINJURED.

WHEN THE RIGHT ENGINE AIRFRAME FUEL BOOST PUMP WAS TURNED ON FUEL WAS OBSERVED LEAKING OUT OF THIS HOSE/FITTING ASSEMBLY AT THE ENGINE COOLING BAFFLING LOCATION. THERE WAS ANOTHER FITTING THAT THREADS INTO THE FUEL METERING SERVO ON THE RIGHT ENGINE THAT WAS SAFETIED BUT ALSO LOOSE. NO FUEL WAS OBSERVED LEAKING FROM THIS FITTING. NO FUEL WAS OBSERVED IN THE LEFT AUXILIARY FUEL TANK, THE LEFT MAIN FUEL TANK HAD 3 INCHES OF FUEL SHOWING, THE RIGHT AUXILIARY FUEL TANK HAD 1 INCH OF FUEL SHOWING AND THE RIGHT MAIN FUEL TANK HAD 3 INCHES OF FUEL SHOWING. ALL AILERON, ELEVATOR, AND RUDDER CONTROL SYSTEMS, TO INCLUDE TRIM SYSTEMS WERE CHECKED FOR CONTINUITY AND FOUND TO INDICATE PROPER FUNCTIONALITY.

20120810027359A	DURING TAKEOFF ROLL OF A SELF LAUNCHING  GLIDER, THE GLIDER PILOT DID NOT ABORT HIS TAKEOFF, RAN OUT OF TAXIWAY AND WENT INTO A DITCH AND BACK UP THE OTHER SIDE. THE GLIDER WAS NOT DAMAGED EXTERNALLY BUT INTERNALLY. THE LANDING GEAR BOX SEPERATED FROM THE FUSELAGE DUE TO THE ROUGH TERRAIN IN THE DITCH.  THE TAXIWAY WAS BEING USED FOR LAUNCHING.DURING RUN UP, PRIOR TO LAUNCH, THE BRAKES ARE SET BY PULLING BACK ON A LEVER THAT ALSO CONTROLS THE SPEED BRAKES. ONCE THE ENGINE POWERS UP, THE PILOT RELEASES THE LEVER AND LOCKS IT IN PLACE, IN THE FORWARD POSITION. IF THE LEVER IS NOT LOCKED THE SPEED BRAKES WILL DEPLOY, PREVENTING THE GLIDER FROM REACHING TAKE OFF SPEED. THIS IS WHAT KEPT THE GLIDER FROM BECOMING AIRBORNE. THE PILOT WAS NOT INJURED.

ONCE THE AIRCRAFT WAS NOSE DOWN AND FUEL AND FUEL WEIGHT ON THE VENT TUBE COULD HAVE LIKELY DISOLVED AND OBSTRUCTION, ALLOWING FUEL TO ONCE AGAIN FLOW AS WITNESSED 45 MINUTES AFTER THE ACCIDENT.

VISIBLE DAMAGE WAS AS FOLLOWS:  - BENT PROPELLOR, CRACKED/BROKEN R&L WHEEL FAIRING, CRACKED/BROKEN ENGINE COWLING, L WING LEADING EDGE DAMAGE, R WING TRAILING EDGE DAMAGE TO REAR SPAR AT AILERON, UPPER WING DAMAGE FROM IMPACT OF FLIPPING OVER, VERTICAL STAB IMPACT DAMAGE FROM FLIPPING OVER, ENGINE MOUNT TORN/BROKEN IN NUMEROUS DIFFERENT LOCATIONS, REAR OIL FILTER ATTACH POINT BROKEN, PROPELLOR SPINNER BROKEN, RIGHT WING STRUT BENT.11/15/12: MET WITH ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ AND NTSB INVESTIGATORS AT AIR SALVAGE OF DALLAS (ASOD) FOR ENGINE RUN AND ANALYSIS. THE ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ INFORMED US THAT HE DID A FUEL FLOW TEST THE PREVIOUS NIGHT, AND NOTED THAT HE WAS ONLY GETTING 1 QT PER 3 MINUTES. THIS EQUATES TO ROUGHLY 5 GAL/HOUR FUEL FLOW. ENGINE ANALYSIS WAS AS FOLLOWS: #3 SPARK PLUG HAD FOREIGN MATTER IN THE ELECTRODE, SHORTING IT OUT; ONE MAGNETO WAS WELL WORN, CAUSING ENGINE TIMING TO BE OFF FACTORY SETTING. A NEW PLUG WAS INSERTED AND ENGINE RUN WAS SUCCESFUL. ENGINE TIMING WAS RESET TO FACTORY SETTING WITH A RESULT OF A SMOOTHER RUNNING ENGINE. FUEL FLOW WAS THEN RESTRICTED TO 5 GAL/HR TO APPROXIMATE ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ OBSERVATION. THE ENGINE RAN FINE AT IDLE AND RUNUP SPEEDS. HOWEVER, AT TAKEOFF POWER SETTINGS, THE ENGINE BECAME FUEL STARVED AND QUIT AFTER 15 SECONDS. ACCORDING TO ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^, HE WOULD HAVE BEEN AIRBORNE AND AT APPROXIMATELY 200 FEET AFTER 15 SECONDS. THIS CLOSELY RESEMBLES THE EVENTS AND TIMELINE OF THE ACCIDENT.11/16/12: MET WITH THE ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ OF N848Z, THIS MORNING  AT HIS HANGAR. THE PURPOSE OF THIS MEETING WAS TO CONDUCT A FUEL FLOW RATE TEST AS A FOLLOW UP TO THE ENGINE RUN RESULTS FROM YESTERDAY AT AIR SALVAGE OF DALLAS (ASOD). USING A GRADUATED CONTAINER, I OBSERVED THE OWNER OPEN THE FUEL VALVE OF N848Z AND ALLOW FUEL TO FLOW FROM THE MAIN FUEL TANK INTO THE CONTAINER THROUGH THE FLEX TUBING, WHICH IS THE SAME TUBING THAT CONNECTS TO THE CARBURETOR. I STARTED A STOPWATCH AND TIMED THE FUEL FLOW UNTIL REACHING THE 16OZ. MARK ON THE CONTAINER. THE TIME TO 16 OZ. WAS 1MINUTE, 15 SEC. THIS WOULD EQUATE TO APPROXIMATELY 7.5 GAL/HOUR FUEL FLOW, CONSISTENT WITH THE ENGINE RUN TEST YESTERDAY AT ASOD.NEXT, THE ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ REMOVED THE FLEX TUBING, AND REPLACED IT WITH A CLEAR PLASTIC TUBING WHICH SLIPPED OVER THE FITTING. UPON OPENING THE FUEL VALVE, SOME KIND OF RED RTV TYPE MATERIAL FLOWED THROUGH THE TUBING AND INTO THE CONTAINER. THE FLOW OF FUEL DRAMATICALLY IMPROVED WHEN USING THE CLEAR PLASTIC TUBING. THE ORIGINAL FLEX TUBING WAS BLOWN OUT WITH COMPRESSED AIR, AND SOME MORE FOREIGN MATERIAL RESIDUE EXITED ONTO THE WORKBENCH. ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^, THEN DRAINED THE FUEL TANK AND REMOVED THE FORWARD AND AFT FUEL SCREENS. THE REAR SCREEN CONTAINED THE SAME FOREIGN MATERIAL THAT WAS FOUND IN THE FLEX LINE. IN ADDITION, BOTH FUEL SCREENS WERE OF A SIZE THAT CAN ALLOW LARGE PARTICLES TO PASS THROUGH AND ENTER THE FUEL LINES, LARGE ENOUGH TO RESTRICT OR INHIBIT FUEL FLOW. FURTHER INVESTIGATION SHOWS RTV WAS USED AS A GASKET FOR AN IN-TANK FUEL GAUGE INSTALLATION THAT HAD DETERIORATED.CONCLUSION: IT IS APPARENT THAT THE OBSTRUCTION FOUND IN THE FUEL LINES WAS SUFFICIENT ENOUGH TO REDUCE THE FLOW OF FUEL TO THE ENGINE SO THAT THE ENGINE COULD NOT MAINTAIN FULL POWER AFTER APPROXIMATELY 15 SECONDS. ONCE THESE OBSTRUCTIONS WERE REMOVED, FUEL FLOW RETURNED TO NORMAL. ENGINE POWER LOSS CAUSED BY FUEL FLOW RESTRICTION BY FOREIGN MATERIAL IN THE FUEL LINE.INVESTIGATION CLOSED.

THE AIRCRAFT LANDED ON HIGHWAY 69, NORTH BOUND AND SUSTAINED MINOR DAMAGE TO THE LEFT MAIN LANDING GEAR. THE PROPELLER WAS INTACT AND ABLE TO BE ROTATED THE ENGINE WITH NO MECHANICAL RESTRICTION WITHIN THE ENGINE.  ON NOVEMBER 20, 2012 DURING A DETAIL ENGINE INSPECTION IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE ENGINES SECONDARY COIL WIRE THAT PROVIDES ENGINE ELECTRICAL IGNITION FAILED. THE WIRE FAILURE STEMMED FROM CONTINUOUS MOISTURE INTRUSION INTO THE COILS CONTACT POINT DUE TO NON STANDARD WIRE ROUTING PRACTICES/STRESS CORROSION. THE WIRE FAILURE RESULTED IN AN IN-FLIGHT ENGINE IGNITION, ATA-74 SYSTEM FAILURE.A MALFUNCTION OR DEFECT REPORT, FAA FORM 8110-4 DATED NOVEMBER 26, 2012 HAS BEEN SUBMITTED BY THE AIRCRAFT OWNER.THIS MATTER DOES NOT REQUIRE FURTHER INVESTIGATION AND IS CLOSED, REFERENCE PTRS ID SW15201303506 AND SW15201303508.

20121116026509A	PILOT WAS ENROUTE FROM DURANGO, CO. TO NOGALES, AZ. WHEN HE EXPERIENCED A LOSS OF ENGINE POWER. PILOT STATED HE WAS IN CONTACT WITH ALBUQUERQUE CENTER (ZAB) AND WAS CLIMBING FROM 12,000 TO 14,000 FT MSL WHEN HE HEARD A "POP" SOUND FROM THE ENGINE AREA. HE THEN EXPERIENCED A DROP IN MANIFOLD PRESSURE (MP) AND THE ENGINE BEGAN RUNNING ROUGH. HE REACTED BY LEANING THE MIXTURE CONTROL AND REDUCING THE THROTTLE. HE STATED HE THOUGHT HE HAD LOST THE SUPERCHARGER DRIVE BELT AS THIS HAD HAPPENED ONCE BEFORE DURING A FLIGHT. INITIALLY HE WAS NOT CONCERNED ABOUT THE LOSS OF MP AS HE KNEW HE COULD FLY THE AIRCRAFT WITHOUT THE SUPERCHARGER AND IT WOULD SIMPLY GO BACK TO A NORMALLY ASPIRATED CONDITION ONCE THE ENGINE WAS PROPERLY LEANED. HE THEN CONTACTED ZAB TO NOTIFY THEM HE HAD A PROBLEM, BUT THAT IT WAS NOT AN EMERGENCY. HE DISENGAGED THE AUTOPILOT AND CORRECTED HIS CLIMB TO LEVEL OFF AT 14K. A MINUTE OR TWO LATER THE ENGINE MONITOR HAD A BLINKING AMBER LIGHT INDICATING LOW OIL PRESSURE. THE PILOT CHECKED THE OIL PRESSURE AND NOTED OIL PRESSURE WAS 47 LBS AND DECLINING. HE CALLED ZAB AND DECLARED AN EMERGENCY. ZAB GAVE HIM A STEERING FOR SHOW LOW (SOW) WHICH HE TURNED TO AND SET THE AIRSPEED UP FOR BEST GLIDE. ZAB ANNOUNCED THAT HE WAS GETTING READY TO BE LOST ON RADAR BECAUSE OF HIS DECLINING ALTITUDE. AT THAT POINT THE PILOT STATED THAT HE WAS NOT GOING TO BE ABLE TO MAKE THE SOW AIRPORT. HE TOLD ZAB THAT HE WAS GOING TO STEER FOR AN OPEN FIELD AND FIRE HIS PARACHUTE. HE ASKED THEM TO CALL FOR HELP. ONCE THE PARACHUTE WAS POPPED THE PILOT STATED THAT HE WAS UNDER THE CANOPY FOR ABOUT 3 SWINGS WHEN THE AIRCRAFT CONTACTED THE LANDING AREA. DURING THE TIME HE WAS DESCENDING UNDER THE CANOPY THE PILOT STATED THAT HE TURNED THE AIRCRAFT POWER OFF AND OPENED THE CANOPY DOOR IN ANTICIPATION OF THE LANDING. THE LANDING WAS VERY HARD AND KNOCKED THE BREATH OUT OF HIM, BUT HE WAS ABLE TO IMMEDIATELY EGRESS THE AIRCRAFT.THE PILOT WAS TAKEN TO THE HOSPITAL AFTER THE RESCUE AND FOUND THAT HE HAD A FRACTURED VERTEBRA, BUT NO OTHER MEDICAL PROBLEMS.THE AIRCRAFT SUFFERED SUBSTANTIAL DAMAGE WHEN IT CONTACTED THE GROUND UNDER CANOPY. THE LANDING GEAR WAS TORN FROM THE AIRCRAFT. INVESTIGATION OF THE AIRCRAFT AT THE SCENE DETERMINED THAT THERE WAS OIL RESIDUE FROM THE ENGINE COMPARTMENT DOWN THE LEFT HAND SIDE OF THE AIRCRAFT AND BELLY. ONCE THE ENGINE COWLING WAS REMOVED IT WAS APPARENT THAT THE OIL LINE FITTING TO THE SUPERCHARGER HAD FAILED AND ALLOWED ENGINE OIL TO BE PUMPED OVERBOARD.NTSB, FAA, ENGINE, AND AIRFRAME MANUFACTURERS ARE CURRENTLY CONDUCTING FURTHER INVESTIGATION OF THE ENGINE AND ITS COMPONENTS.

THE PALM BEACH COUNTY SHERIFF'S OFFICE (PBSO) HELICOPTER (EAGLE II) LAUNCHED OUT AND FOUND AN AIRCRAFT IN A SUGAR CANE FIELD ABOUT 3-5 MILES S.E. OF THE PAHOKEE (PHK) AIRPORT. NONE OF THE SURROUNDING SUGAR CANE WAS DISTURBED. THE AREA WAS PHOTOGRAPHED AND AN INVENTORY OF THE PARTS THAT ARRIVED AT THE CRASH SITE WAS PERFORMED. THIS INVENTORY ACCOUNTED FOR THE AIRFRAME, EMPENNAGE, TAIL, ELEVATOR AND RUDDER. THE AIRCRAFT WAS LATER TURNED OVER AND THE PILOT WAS UNBELTED AND REMOVED. THE TOP OF THE AIRCRAFT SHOWED SIGNS THAT THE PILOT HAD BEEN INJURED BEFORE THE AIRCRAFT STRUCK THE GROUND. THE AIRCRAFT SUSTAINED MORE IMPACT DAMAGE ON THE LEFT SIDE THEN THE RIGHT. AN IMPACT AND TRANSFER MARK ON THE LEFT WINGS LEADING EDGE INDICATES THAT THE LEFT MAIN LANDING GEAR AND FAIRING STRUCK THE WING. THE AIRCRAFT WAS REMOVED TO AN IMPOUND LOT, WERE THE NTSB CONTINUED EXAMINING THE WRECKAGE.ACCORDING TO RADAR INFORMATION ACQUIRED FROM ATC AND NTSB, IT SHOWS THAT ABOUT 17 MINUTES INTO THE FLIGHT, N118GG ENCOUNTERED TRAFFIC, A BOEING 757, AT BETWEEN 7600'-8000'+/-. N118GG WAS UNABLE TO MAINTAIN A STEADY HEADING AND ALTITUDE, SO HE CLIMBS FROM 7600' UP TO 8400'. AS N118GG CROSSES THE 757'S FLIGHT PATH AGAIN AND DROPS FROM 8200' TO 7300' IN ABOUT 10SECONDS. AT THE NEXT RADAR SWEEP, THE AIRCRAFT SHOWS NO ALTITUDE AND 157KTS AIRSPEED.ON DECEMBER 11, 2012, A PBSO HELICOPTER SURVEYED THE CRASH SITE AND RELOCATED AN AREA IN QUESTION. ALL MAJOR COMPONENTS OF THE AIRPLANE WERE ACCOUNTED FOR AT THE SCENE WITH THE EXCEPTION OF THE BALLISTIC PARACHUTE COVER. BOTH LEFT AND RIGHT FUEL TANKS WERE INTACT AND CAPS WERE INSTALLED. THERE WAS NO SMELL OF FUEL OR EVIDENCE OF ANY LEAKS AT THE SCENE.   THE AIRCRAFT WAS RECOVERED AND TRANSPORTED TO DXR THAT NIGHT. INSPECTION OF THE AIRCRAFT THE FOLLOWING DAY REVEALED THE FOLLOWING: THE FLAPS WERE IN THE FULL UP POSITION, THE THROTTLE WAS IN IDLE AND THE MIXTURE WAS IN CUTOFF.  THE FUEL SELECTOR WAS SET TO THE RIGHT TANK, AND THE BOOST PUMP WAS IN THE OFF POSITION. BATTERY POWER WAS APPLIED TO AIRCRAFT AND BOTH FUEL GAUGES INDICATED ZERO QUANTITY.   ALL EXTERIOR DAMAGED APPEARED TO BE CAUSED BY IMPACT WITH THE TREES AND THE GROUND. ALL PROP BLADES WERE BENT AFT, ALL FOUR ENGINE MOUNTS WERE BROKEN AND THE ENGINE MOVED AFT APPROXIMATELY EIGHT INCHES CAUSING THE OIL FILTER HOUSING TO BREAK OFF WHEN IT IMPACTED THE NOSE STRUT MOUNT.   THE UPPER AND LOWER ENGINE COWLS WERE REMOVED. ALL FUEL HOSES WERE FOUND TO BE INTACT AND UNDAMAGED. ALL WIRING WAS FOUND TO BE INTACT AND CONNECTED. BOTH LEFT AND RIGHT WING FUEL CAP WERE REMOVED AND NO FUEL WAS NOTED IN EITHER TANK. THE ENGINE SUMP AND LEFT AND RIGHT FUEL TANK SUMPS WERE DRAINED FOR A COMBINED TOTAL OF 26 OUNCES OF FUEL.   THE RIGHT MULTI-FUNCTION DISPLAY?S FLASH CARD WAS REMOVED ALONG WITH THE REMOTE DATA MODULE LOCATED ON THE RUDDER SPAR AND SENT TO THE NTSB FOR TESTING.  THERE WERE THREE PERSONS ON BOARD. A PRIVATE PILOT WHO WAS FLYING THE AIRCRAFT LOCATED IN THE LEFT SEAT AND A FLIGHT INSTRUCTOR WAS IN THE RIGHT SEAT. THE PRIVATE PILOT?S BROTHER WAS LOCATED IN THE REAR SEAT. THE PRIVATE PILOT WAS FLYING THE AIRCRAFT, WHEN ABOUT SIX MILES OUT FROM DANBURY AIRPORT, THE ENGINE STARTED RUNNING ROUGH AND THEN STOPPED RUNNING.  AT THIS POINT THE FLIGHT INSTRUCTOR TOOK THE CONTROLS AND WAS ABLE TO RESTART THE ENGINE. AT FOUR MILES FROM THE AIRPORT THE ENGINE STOPPED RUNNING FOR A SECOND TIME. BASED ON A REVIEW OF THE DANBURY AIRPORT AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL TOWER AUDIO RECORDINGS, THE FLIGHT INSTRUCTOR FIRST STATED THAT THEY HAD NO FUEL AND WHEN THE ENGINE QUIT THE SECOND TIME HE STATED THEY WERE OUT OF FUEL.   A LINE PERSON WHO IS EMPLOYED BY RELIANT AIRCRAFT SERVICE WAS INTERVIEWED AND STATED THAT HE FUELED N140PG ON JANUARY 20, 2013. THE FUEL LOAD REQUEST WAS TO FILL TO THE TABS PLUS AN ADDITIONAL EIGHT GALLONS. THAT FUEL LOAD SHOULD HAVE MADE THE TOTAL FUEL QUANTITY 43 GALLONS. THERE IS NO OTHER RECORD OF THE AIRCRAFT BEING FUELED AGAIN FROM THAT TIME TO THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENT.   RECORDS SHOWED THAT N140PG FLEW FOR 2.7 HOURS BEFORE THE ACCIDENT FLIGHT DEPARTED. THE TACH TIME WAS OBTAIN FROM THE AIRCRAFT AFTER THE ACCIDENT AND IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE ACCIDENT FLIGHT LASTED 1.1 HOURS.

20130302003659I	THE AIRCRAFT WAS BEING FLOWN ON AN INSTRUMENT CHECK RIDE AND WAS ON A PRACTICE APPROACH TO SDL WHEN THE AIRCRAFT ENGINE BEGAN SURGING AND RUNNING ROUGH. THE CFI/PILOT EXAMINER TOOK THE CONTROLS AND ATTEMPTED TO GET ENGINE RUNNING AGAIN BY SWITCHING TANKS, ADJUSTING MIXTURE, ETC. NONE OF THESE ACTIONS IMPROVED THE POWER FROM THE ENGINE. THE ENGINE QUIT AND WAS THEN RESTARTED SEVERAL TIMES BUT IT WOULD NOT PRODUCE POWER OR CONTINUE TO RUN ON ITS OWN AT A RPM HIGHER THAN IDLE. THE CFI CONTACTED SDL TOWER AND DECLARED AN EMERGENCY AND REQUESTED TO LAND ON RWY 03. THE AIRCRAFT WAS CLEARED TO THE RUNWAY AND LANDED WITHOUT INCIDENT. THERE WAS NO DAMAGE TO THE AIRCRAFT AND NO INJURY TO EITHER PILOT. AS THE AIRCRAFT TURNED OFF THE RUNWAY THE ENGINE WAS ABLE TO RUN WITH SUFFICIENT POWER TO TAXI. THE CFI TAXIED TO PARKING AND THEN PERFORMED AN ENGINE RUN-UP ATTEMPTING TO TROUBLESHOOT THE PROBLEM. IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE ENGINE WOULD RUN AT LOW RPM, BUT AS THE THROTTLE WAS ADVANCED THE FUEL PRESSURE WOULD DROP BELOW THE LOWER REDLINE. THIS HAPPENED WHETHER THE ELECTRIC FUEL PUMP WAS ENGAGED OR NOT. THE AIRCRAFT WAS PARKED AT SDL UNTIL COMPANY MAINTENANCE COULD MAKE A DETERMINATION OF THE PROBLEM. ONCE MAINTENANCE PERFORMED TROUBLESHOOTING IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE AIRCRAFT ELECTRIC FUEL PUMP HAD SOME KIND OF BLOCKAGE WHICH WOULD ONLY ALLOW A DRIBBLE OF FUEL INTO THE ENGINE FUEL SYSTEM. THE ELECTRIC FUEL PUMP WAS REMOVED AND REPLACED WITH A NEW FUEL PUMP. THE ENGINE WAS TEST RUN AND PRODUCED NORMAL POWER THROUGHT ITS PERFORMANCE PARAMETERS. THE AIRCRAFT WAS THEN RETURNED TO SERVICE.  THIS AIRCRAFT HAS BEEN OPERATING NORMALLY SINCE THE REPLACEMENT OF THE ELECTRIC FUEL PUMP.  MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL LATER OPENED THE ELECTRIC DRIVEN FUEL PUMP TO DETERMINE WHY FUEL FLOW WAS BEING RESTRICTED. DURING TEARDOWN IT WAS NOTED THAT THE VALVE SEAT ON THE INTAKE SIDE OF THE PUMP WAS MISSING PART OF THE METAL (BRASS) VALVE SEAT AND THE PLUNGER WAS COCKED  SIDEWAYS. UPON FURTHER INSPECTION IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE VALVE PLUNGER WAS STUCK TO ITS SEAT. IT APPEARS THAT THE PLUNGER WAS JAMMED AND WOULD NOT ALLOW FUEL TO FLOW FREELY INTO THE VALVE BODY.  THE MAINTENANCE PROVIDER HAS SUBMITTED A SDR REPORT.  A REVIEW OF THE MAINTENANCE RECORDS FOR THIS AIRCRAFT INDICATES THE FUEL PUMP HAS NEVER BEEN CHANGED SINCE THE AIRCRAFT WAS CERTIFICATED. FURTHER INVESTIGATION WILL BE CONDUCTED TO DETERMINE WHETHER PARTS WITHIN THE PUMP NEED TO BE ASSESSED FOR WEAR.

THE 48 PASSENGERS AND SIX CREW MEMBERS (INCLUDING TWO DEADHEADING CREW MEMBERS) WERE EVACUATED WHILE ON RUNWAY 12L FROM THE AIRCRAFT'S FRONT AIR-STAIR DOOR AND TRANSPORTED TO THE TERMINAL.  NO INJURIES WERE REPORTED.   THE PILOTS DID NOT VISUALLY CONFIRM AN ENGINE FIRE.  HOWEVER, THE FLIGHT ATTENDANTS NOTICED "A BALL OF FIRE ON THE RIGHT ENGINE" AND HORIZON AIR GROUND PERSONNEL REPORTED THE RIGHT ENGINE COWLING WAS SCORCHED.  AVIATION SAFETY INSPECTORS FROM THE SAN JOSE FLIGHT STANDARDS DISTRICT OFFICE (WP-15) WERE IMMEDIATELY DISPATCHED TO THE AIRCRAFT AFTER IT LANDED TO PERFORM AN ON-SITE INVESTIGATION.    THE AIRCRAFT WAS TOWED TO A SECURED HANGAR FOR FURTHER EXAMINATION.  LATER IN THE DAY, HORIZON AIR SENT A MAINTENANCE TEAM TO SJC TO INSPECT THE DAMAGE TO THE AIRCRAFT.    ON MARCH 6, 2013 FIELD SERVICE REPRESENTATIVES FROM BOTH THE AIRCRAFT MANUFACTURER (BOMBARDIER, INC.) AND ENGINE MANUFACTURER (PRATT & WHITNEY CANADA) WERE ON-SITE AND PROVIDED TECHNICAL SUPPORT.  IN ADDITION, ENGINEERS (STRUCTURES AND SYSTEMS) FROM THE ENGINE AND AIRCRAFT MANUFACTURER CONDUCTED AN EVALUATION AND DAMAGE ASSESSMENT.   ON MARCH 15, 2013 THE NTSB STRUCTURES ENGINEER DETERMINED (VIA DAMAGE ASSESSMENT) THAT THE ENGINE FIRE DAMAGE WAS NOT LIMITED TO THE ENGINE, BUT AFFECTED THE NACELLE AND STRUT STRUCTURE.  ACCORDING TO THE NTSB ENGINEER, VIRTUALLY EVERY ENGINE STRUT HAD HEAT/BURN DAMAGE THAT COMPROMISED THE MATERIAL PROPERTIES.  SOME OF THE STRUT ATTACHMENT BRACKETS, FRAMES, ENGINE MOUNT FITTINGS AND FIREWALLS WERE ALSO DAMAGED.  THE STRUCTURE IN QUESTION IS ALL CLASSIFIED AS PRIMARY STRUCTURE PER THE AIRCRAFT MANUFACTURER'S STRUCTURAL REPAIR MANUAL.  THE VAST MAJORITY OF THE STRUCTURE MUST BE REPLACED PER A DAMAGE SURVEY PROVIDED BY BOMBARDIER, INC.  THE DAMAGE QUALIFIES AS SUBSTANTIAL AS DEFINED IN NTSB 49 CFR 830.2.   PER THE DAMAGE ASSESSMENT, THIS EVENT HAS BEEN CLASSIFIED AS AN ACCIDENT BY THE NTSB INVESTIGATOR-IN-CHARGE.  ON JULY 8, 2013, AN E-MAIL MESSAGE SENT BY THE NTSB IIC STATED THAT A STRUCTURAL EXAMINATION OF THE NACELLE STRUTS REVEALED NO DEGRADATION OF THE MATERIAL PROPERTIES.  AN NTSB STRUCTURES ENGINEER REPORTED THE DAMAGE TO THE AIRCRAFT WAS ONLY TO THE SECONDARY STRUCTURE AND WOULD NOT AFFECT THE STRUCTURAL STRENGTH, PERFORMANCE, OR FLIGHT CHARACTERISTICS OF THE AIRCRAFT.  THEREFORE, IT CANNOT BE CLASSIFIED AS SUBSTANTIAL DAMAGE UNDER NTSB RULES.  THIS EVENT HAS BEEN RECLASSIFIED FROM AN ACCIDENT TO AN INCIDENT, PER NTSB 830.2.  THE NEW NTSB CASE NUMBER IS WPR13IA14

MAY 08, 2013  THE FOLLOWING EFCB WAS POSTED FOR THE 757/767-300 FLEET.   SUBJECT: MANUAL SPEEDBRAKE DEPLOYMENT                                              SOURCE: 757/767-300 FLEET TEAM                                                 EFFECTIVE DATE: 08MAY13    EXPIRATION DATE: 30JUN13      PRIORITY BULLETIN: N  BULLETIN TEXT:                     BULLETIN-ID: MA-76713-0006                    RECENT TAIL STRIKES HIGHLIGHT THE NEED FOR BETTER PILOT AWARENESS OF MANUAL SPEEDBRAKE DEPLOYMENT ON LANDING. THE 757/767 MDM STATES THE FOLLOWING FOR AUTO SPEEDBRAKE INOPERATIVE: . CAUTION:DEPLOYING SPEEDBRAKES MANUALLY BEFORE NOSEWHEEL TOUCHDOWN MAY CAUSE PRONOUNCED NOSE PITCH UP. . IN ADDITION, THE 757 QRH AUTO SPEEDBRAKE INOP PROCEDURE STATES:  NOTE:NOSE WHEEL MUST BE ON THE GROUND PRIOR TO DEPLOYING SPEEDBRAKES MANUALLY.  . BE FAMILIAR WITH THE GUIDANCE IN THE MDM/QRH. IT IS IMPORTANT TO UNDERSTAND THAT MANUALLY DEPLOYING THE SPEEDBRAKES WILL CAUSE A SIGNIFICANT PITCH UP MOMENT NOT EXPERIENCED WHEN SPEEDBRAKES ARE AUTOMATICALLY DEPLOYED. ***CONTINUED*** .   THE AUTOMATIC SYSTEM DELAYS DEPLOYMENT OF SOME OF THE SPOILER PANELS. THIS IS NOT THE CASE IF SPEEDBRAKES ARE DEPLOYED MANUALLY. ALL PANELS IMMEDIATELY DEPLOY CAUSING AN ADDITIONAL PITCH UP MOMENT. . FINALLY, THE ABOVE INFORMATION SHOULD BE APPLIED TO ANY SITUATION WHERE THE SPOILERS DO NOT DEPLOY AUTOMATICALLY ON LANDING.       THIS INVESTIGATION IS CLOSED.

HE TOUCHED DOWN ON THE CENTER LINE AT APPROX. 12:55. HE MADE A SOFT LANDING BECAUSE OF THE TAIL WHEEL BRIEFING AND ONCE THE TAIL WHEEL WAS DOWN HE BROUGHT THE CONTROL STICK FULLY BACK AND LET THE AIRCRAFT DECELERATE. AS THE AIRCRAFT DECELERATED IT TRACKED TO THE LEFT. HE MADE SMALL CORRECTIONS ATTEMPTING TO GET BACK TO THE CENTERLINE. AS HE MADE THIS INPUT OF RIGHT RUDDER, THE NOSE STARTED TO MOVE TO THE RIGHT AND THE TAIL SUDDENLY DROPPED SEVERAL INCHES. THE NOSE THEN QUICKLY CAME LEFT AND THE AIRCRAFT EXITED THE LEFT SIDE OF THE RUNWAY JUST WEST OF TAXIWAY D7.    THE GROUND BETWEEN THE RUNWAY AND TAXIWAY SLOPES DOWN INTO A GULLY FOR WATER DRAINAGE IN THIS AREA. THE RIGHT WING TOUCHED THE GROUND AND THE AIRCRAFT STOPPED BETWEEN 22R AND TAXIWAY D.   HE STOPPED THE ENGINE, INFORMED THE TOWER HE WAS OK AND THAT HE WANTED TO TAKE A LOOK AT THE AIRCRAFT. HE COULD SEE THE SCUFF MARKS UNDER THE RIGHT WING TIP AND A CREASE MARK IN THE RIGHT AILERON WHICH HE ASSUMED HAD MADE MOST CONTACT WITH THE ROUGH GROUND. THE PROPELLER AND ENGINE SHOWED NO SIGNS OF DAMAGE SO WITH THE HELP OF TWO GUYS SENT OUT BY THE TOWER, THE AIRCRAFT WAS PUSHED ONTO THE TAXIWAY AND HE REQUESTED TO TAXI BACK TO THE CAF RAMP VIA TAXIWAY D.   ONCE THE AIRCRAFT WAS IN THE HANGER, A WALK AROUND SHOWED THE RIGHT AILERON WAS SLIGHTLY BENT, SCUFF MARKS UNDER THE RIGHT WING TIP. THE TAIL WHEEL WAS LEANING TO THE LEFT. WHEN CAF MEMBER ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^, WHO OWNS TWO STEARMANS, STOOD ON THE REAR FUSELAGE HANDLE, THE TAIL WHEEL BANGED DOWN SEVERAL INCHES ON ITS SUSPENSION AND DID NOT SPRING BACK UP WHEN HE STEPPED OFF, IT DID COME BACK UP AND STAYED UP WHEN THE TAIL WAS LIFTED BY THE REAR HANDLES. THE TAIL WHEEL STRUT WAS NOT DAMAGED BY THE LANDING.  HE HAVE HEARD SINCE THE PT-17 FLIGHT THE SEVERAL PEOPLE IN THE FLIGHT DEPARTMENT WERE NOT HAPPY THAT THE AIR/OIL TAIL STRUT HAD BEEN INSTALLED. APPARENTLY IT WAS STICKING AS DESCRIBED ABOVE PRIOR TO MY FLIGHT AND WOULD NOT DEPRESS VERY EASILY, UNLIKE THE SPRING SUSPENSION PREVIOUSLY USED ON N47964 AND CURRENTLY INSTALLED ON THE OTHER TWO STEARMANS IN THE MUSEUM.   DURING THE MAINTENANCE INSPECTION AFTER THE ACCIDENT IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE TAIL AIR/OIL STRUT HAD FAILED AND THE STRUT HAS BEEN REPLACED. THE RIGHT LOWER WINGS SPAR WAS ALSO  CRACKED IN SEVERAL PLACES AND IS ON ORDER FOR REPLACEMENT.  AMEND. 6/3/2013 TO ADD NTSB REPORT NUMBER.

AIRMAN STATEMENT OF INFLIGHT PROPELLER LOSS, ERCOUPE 415C, N87114, MESQUITE, NEVADA APRIL 14, 2013:  I, ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^, HAD COMPLETED A VFR FLIGHT FROM LAKE HAVASU, AZ (KHII) TO MESQUITE, NV (67L), ARRIVING AT 0839 PDT. IFILED A FLIGHT PLAN WITH LOCKHEED-MARTIN FLIGHT SERVICE FOR MY NEXT LEG TO ELY, NV (KELY) WITH A PRESUMED DEPARTURE TIME OF 0915 (THERE IS NO RADIO CONTACT WITH FSS FROM THE GROUND AT 67L). I HAD THE TANKS FILLED WITH 9.9 GALLONS OF 100LL FOR FULL TANKS PRIOR TO MY DEPARTURE. GROUND RUN-UP WAS NORMAL, AS WAS THE TAKE-OFF AND INITIAL CLIMB. THE AIRCRAFT WAS CLIMBING AT ABOUT 500 FPM AT 2300 RPM WITH OIL PRESSURE, CHT'S AND EGT IN NORMALPARAMETERS. ABOUT 5 MINUTES INTO THE FLIGHT, IFELT A "LOW-FREQUENCY" VIBRATION WHICH IESTIMATE PERSISTED FOR ABOUT 10 SECONDS.  ISCANNED THE ENGINE INSTRUMENTS, CHECKED THE CANOPY, AND DECIDED THAT PERHAPS IHAD AN RPM-RELATED 'HARMONIC'.  AS IREACHED TO ADJUST THE THROTTLE, THE ENGINE SUDDENLY SURGED WITH THE TACH PASSING 4,000 RPM.  IQUICKLY RETARDED THE THROTTLE AND REALIZED THAT I WAS PRODUCING NO THRUST AND COULD NOT SEE THE PROP MOVEMENT.  AT FIRST, ICOULD NOT BELIEVE THAT THE PROPELLOR WASN'T THERE,BUT WHEN IADVANCED THE THROTTLE IT AGAIN SURGED TO VERY HIGH RPM.  I WAS AT ABOUT 4,200 MSL. AS THE AIRSPEED DECAYED, IRECOGNIZED THAT THE CONTROLS WERE GETTING 'SLOPPY' DUE TO A SHIFT OF THE CG. IPUSHED THE NOSE DOWN TO MAINTAIN ABOUT 85 MPH AND TURNED SOUTH TOWARD 67L.  IMADE TWO 'MAYDAY' CALLS ON 122.8 (CTAF AT 67L) AND ANNOUNCED MY POSITION.  ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^, PILOT OF A CESSNA 172, HEARD THESE CALLS AND RELAYED THEM TO FSS. REALIZING THAT IWOULD BE UNABLE TO GLIDE BACK TO THE AIRPORT, ISCANNED FOR SUITABLE TERRAIN FOR A FORCED LANDING... BUT THIS IS AN AREA OF ROUGH BADLANDS.  IN AN EFFORT TO REDUCE MY LANDING SPEED, IT TURNED BACK NORTH INTO A 10-15 KNOT WIND.  I SPOTTED TWO 'JEEP' TRAILS AND A MODERATELY LEVEL RIDGE AND BEGAN MY DESCENT.  EACH TIME ITRIED TO REDUCE MY AIRSPEED THE AIRCRAFT BECAME NEARLY UNCONTROLLABLE.  THE TRAILS APPEARED VERY ROUGH, AND IHAD LOST TOO MUCH ALTITUDE TRYING TO MAINTAIN CONTROLTO MAKE THE LEVEL RIDGE.  I ELECTED TO TRY FOR A 'WASH' WITH SLOPING SIDES THAT WAS RISING TOWARD THE RIDGE.  MY 'SHORT FINAL' WAS AT ABOUT 75 MPH, AND I'FLARED' AT ABOUT 30 FEET AGL. THIS RESULTED IN SIGNIFICANTLY DEGRADED CONTROLRESPONSE AS THE AIRCRAFT GOT 'NOSE HIGH' AND HIT ON BOTH MAIN GEAR, CONTINUING UP THE 'WASH' FOR ABOUT 80-100 FEET.  THE NOSE GEAR COLLAPSED AS THE AIRCRAFT PROGRESSED UP THE SLOPE AT THE HEAD OF THE WASH, HITTING A JOSHUA TREE WITH THE LEFT WING AT AN ESTIMATED 20 MPH. ISHUT OFF THE MASTER SWITCH AND QUICKLY EXITED THE AIRCRAFT, AS BOTH WING TANKS HAD RUPTURED DURING THE ROLL-OUT. THE 121.5 ELT HAD BEEN TRIGGERED, AND ITRIED TO CALL MESQUITE UNICOM ON MY HANDHELD RADIO.  WHEN THAT FAILED, ICALLED FSS ON MY CELLPHONE. RESPONSE WAS QUICK AS I WAS ONLY ABOUT 3 MILES NORTH OF 67L.  THE BEAVER DAM FIRE DEPARTMENT ACTED AS A RELAY, WITH ME DIRECTING A MEDI-FIIGHT HELICOPTER TO MY LOCATION... THE HELICOPTER LED SEARCH AND RESCUE PERSONNEL TO ME. THEY ARRIVED WITH A JEEP AND PICK-UP TRUCK WITHIN 45 MINUTES.  I THEN REMOVED THE COVER OF THE BATTERY CASE AND DISCONNECTED THE POSITIVE CABLE TO PRECLUDE ANY CHANCE OF ELECTRICAL ARCING. SEARCH AND RESCUE TOOK ME TO THE PAVED ROAD WHERE A MOJAVE COUNTY, AZ SHERIFF'S DEPUTY (BRIAN BINKNEY) WAS WAITING.  ISUFFERED ONLY A SLIGHT CONTUSION WHEN THE LEFT CANOPY SLIDER HIT MY BALL CAP, FORCING MY GLASSES AGAINST MY LEFT CHEEK.  IREQUIRED NO MEDICAL ATTENTION. ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^

20130424012379A	AMENDMENT TO ORIGINAL REPORT: ON JULY 25, 2013 THE NTSB RECEIVED A TEARDOWN REPORT FROM COVINGTON AIRCRAFT IN OKMULGEE, OK. THE SUPERCHARGER UNIT WAS SENT TO AND INSPECTED BY COVINGTON AIRCRAFT.  THE FINDING IN THE TEARDOWN REPORT STATE THAT THE REAR BEARING FAILED AND WAS FRAGMENTED.  THE REAR BEARING BALLS WERE PLASTICIZED, THE PHENOLIC RING SEPARATED FROM THE BEARING AND SMALL FRAGMENTS WERE NOTED THROUGHOUT THE BLOWER.  THE OUTER RACE REMAINED INTACT.  THE MIDDLE BEARING PHENOLIC RING WAS FRAGMENTED AND PIECES RECOVERED IN THE IMMEDIATE VICINITY OF THE BEARING.  THE FLAT SPOTS CONSISTENT WITH RUBBING WERE NOTED ON THE BEARING BALLS. THE OUTER RACE CONTAINED METAL FRAGMENTS.  BOTH THE INNER AND OUTER RACE REMAINED INTACT.  THE FRONT BEARING CONTAINED METAL AND PHENOLIC FRAGMENTS BETWEEN THE OUTER RACE, PHENOLIC RING, INNER RACE, AND THE BALLS.  THE BEARING WOULD NOT ROTATE BUT WAS EXTERNALLY UNREMARKABLE.  BASED ON THIS REPORT NO RECOMMENDATION BY THE FAA IIC ARE BEING CONSIDERED AT THIS TIME.  IN AN INITIAL TELEPHONE INTERVIEW THE PILOT STATED THAT THE "ENGINE ROLLED BACK" AT ABOUT 200-300 HUNDRED FEET ABOVE THE RUNWAY SURFACE.  HE LANDED IN AN UNPLOWED CROP FIELD ABOUT 1500 FEET PAST THE AIRPORT/RUNWAY.  THE AIRPLANE ROLLED OVER ON ITS BACK.  THE PILOT STATED THAT HE WAS NOT INJURED.  IN A SECOND PHONE CONVERSATION ON THE SAME DAY THE PILOT STATED THAT THE AIRPLANE WAS, AT THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENT, BEING INSPECTED FOR ITS ANNUAL INSPECTION BUT WASN'T FINISHED. HE SAID THAT HE WANTED TO FLY IT AROUND TO WARM UP THE OIL BEFORE THE OIL CHANGE.  IN A FACE-TO-FACE INTERVIEW THE PILOT WAS ASKED HOW MUCH GAS THE TANKS HAD AND HE SAID HE BELIEVED ABOUT 35 GALLONS. THE GAS WAS JUST PUT IN THE TANKS SO IT WASN'T FROM LAST YEAR.  THE FIVE DAYS AFTER THE ACCIDENT AND AFTER THE AIRPLANE WAS RELOCATED TO A HANGAR ON THE AIRPORT THE FAA IIC  LOOKED IN BOTH WING GAS TANKS AND SAW GAS IN THEM. THE PILOT PROVIDED A WRITTEN STATEMENT STATING THAT "THE AIRPLANE WAS WASHED. THE ENGINE WAS WASHED DOWN AND INSPECTED".  AFTER 15 MINUTES OF RUN TIME ON THE ENGINE TO WARM IT AND THE OIL TEMPS UP HE TAXIED TO RUNWAY 31.  THE ENGINE WAS RUN UP TO 30" MANIFOLD PRESSURE, PROP WAS CYCLED, MAGNETOS WERE CHECKED AND THE CARBURETOR HEAT WAS CHECKED BEFORE TAKEOFF.  AT THE FIRST POWER REDUCTION AFTER TAKEOFF THE ENGINE CONTINUED TO LOSE POWER SUCH THAT FLIGHT WAS NOT SUSTAINABLE.  THE PILOT CHOSE TO LAND STRAIGHT AHEAD IN A CROP FIELD.  THE FIELD CONDITIONS WERE WET AND SOFT.  THE LANDING WHEELS (BOTH) BROKE OFF OF THE MAIN GEAR STRUTS CAUSING THE STRUTS TO DIG INTO THE EARTH AND THE AIRPLANE THEN FLIPPED OVER COMING TO REST IN AN INVERTED POSITION.  THE PILOT SECURED THE AIRCRAFT SYSTEMS AND THEN EGRESSED WITHOUT INJURY.  IN THE FOLLOW UP INVESTIGATION THE ENGINE WAS ROTATED BY HAND AND NO FIRM COMPRESSION FROM ANY CYLINDER WAS NOTED.  AN AIR INTAKE TUBE WAS THEN REMOVED FROM A CYLINDER TO LOOK FOR METAL DEBRIS.  METAL SHAVINGS WERE FOUND IN THE TUBE.  THE METAL SHAVINGS ARE SUSPECTED TO BE FROM THE SUPERCHARGER UNIT.  A DETERMINATION OF THE ACTUAL FAILED COMPONENT HAS YET TO BE DETERMINED AS A TEARDOWN OF THE COLLECTOR CASE AND SUPERCHARGER ASSEMBLY HAS NOT BEEN ACCOMPLISHED.  THE NTSB HAS ARRANGED FOR A TEARDOWN INSPECTION WITH AN ENGINE OVERHAUL FACILITY.  UPON RECEIPT FROM THE NTSB OF THE RESULTS OF THE TEARDOWN INSPECTION THIS REPORT WILL BE AMENDED. ON DECEMBER 20, 2013 A TELEPHONE CONVERSATION WITH RON HOLLIS AT COVINGTON AIRCRAFT ENGINES WAS MADE TO DISCUSS THEIR FINDINGS ON THE TEARDOWN INSPECTION OF THE BLOWER UNIT.  MR. HOLLIS STATED THEY FOUND THE SUPERCHARGER BLOWER AFT BEARING TO HAVE FAILED .  HE CONFIRMED THAT THE BEARING WAS AN FAA-PMA PART AND HE EMAILED A PICTURE OF THE BEARING AS FOUND.  UPON QUESTIONING HE STATED THAT ALTHOUGH IT IS NOT A FREQUENT OCCURANCE HE HAS SEEN THESE BEARINGS FAILED IN OTHER ENGINES.  HE ALSO DID NOT FEEL THAT THE PMA BEARING IS A SUBPAR PART BECAUSE OF THE FREQUENCY OF FAILURES.

AFTER LANDING AND ON ROLLOUT, THE RENO TOWER TOLD THE PILOT THAT THEY SAW ?SPARKS? COMING FROM THE LANDING GEAR. NOTE: AIRCRAFT MAINTENANCE IS AVAILABLE AT RNO; HOWEVER, THE PILOT ELECTED NOT TO HAVE THE AIRCRAFT INSPECTED AFTER THE ABOVE FLIGHT.     ON SUNDAY AFTERNOON, MAY 12, 2013, THE PILOT AND HIS FAMILY DEPARTED RENO FOR A FLIGHT BACK TO CONCORD.  NO ADDITIONAL FUEL WAS ADDED PRIOR TO MAY 10, 2013, LIVERMORE, CA (LVK) FUELING.  THE PILOT STATED THAT IN THE INTEREST OF SAFETY, HE DECIDED TO MAKE THE ENTIRE RETURN TRIP WITH THE LANDING GEAR EXTENDED.  THE PILOT STATED THAT PERFORMANCE OF THE AIRCRAFT WAS DEFINITELY LESS THAN WHAT HE WAS USED TO, BUT HE ATTRIBUTED THAT TO THE FULL LOAD OF PASSENGERS AND LUGGAGE, THE EXTENDED LANDING GEAR, AND THE HIGH DENSITY ALTITUDE.  HE WENT ON TO STATE THAT AFTER PASSING AUBURN, CA THE ENGINE HAD A SUDDEN LOSS OF POWER.   HE SWITCHED FUEL TANKS, AND THE ENGINE JUST SPUTTERED.  AFTER INFORMING NORCAL APPROACH, HE BEGAN A CIRCLING DESCENT TO THE AUBURN AIRPORT.  AS THE AIRPLANE GOT LOWER, THE ENGINE SEEMED TO RUN BETTER, AND BY THE TIME N54TW LANDED ON AUBURN?S RUNWAY 25, THE ENGINE SEEMED TO DEVELOP FULL POWER AGAIN.  AFTER TAXIING TO TRANSIENT PARKING, THE PILOT DID A FULL RUN-UP TO EVALUATE PERFORMANCE.  SPECTATORS STANDING NEARBY REPORTED THAT THEY SAW ?BLACK SMOKE? AND?OIL RUNNING OUT OF THE ENGINE?.  A FEW DAYS LATER, THE FAA AND AN AIRCRAFT MAINTENANCE FACILITY IN AUBURN, CA INSPECTED THE AIRCRAFT AND DISCOVERED SEVERAL SIGNIFICANT MECHANICAL PROBLEMS: LANDING GEAR: HYDRAULIC PUMP CONTINUES TO RUN. HYDRAULIC PRESSURE SWITCH INTERMITTENT. NOSE GEAR ACTUATOR LEAKING.  ENGINE: THE TURBOCHARGER HAS 3 BROKEN BLADES.  THE DUAL MAGNETO HAS AN INCORRECT GASKET INSTALLED, AND THE SINGLE DRIVE MAGNETOS IS INSTALLED UPSIDE-DOWN. THE  MAGNETO ROTATES INTERMITTENTLY DUE TO LOOSE HARDWARE AFFECTING ENGINE TIMING. CYLINDER #4 EXHAUST MANIFOLD WAS CRACKED.  FUEL: FUEL CAP O RINGS ARE CRACKED. BELLY FUEL SUMP DRAIN VALVE LEAKING. LEFT WING SUMP DRAIN LEAKING. THE ENGINE CRANKSHAFT AT THE SHEAR POINT HAD NO SIGNS OF TWISTING WHICH ALSO SUPPORTS THE CONCLUSION OF THE ENGINE NOT PRODUCING POWER. FUEL SELECTOR FOR THE AIRCRAFT WAS COMPLETELY DESTROYED (MELTED) AND WAS NOT AVAILABLE FOR DETERMINATION OF TANK SELECTED, HOWEVER, BOTH WING TANKS BURNED IN A MANNER SUGGESTING FUEL WAS PRESENT DURING THE FIRE.  DETERMINATION OF WHETHER THIS ACCIDENT WAS CAUSED BY A MECHANICAL FAILURE OR IT WAS PILOT INDUCED IS NOT POSSIBLE DUE TO THE EXTENT OF DAMAGE TO THE AIRFRAME, AND THERE WERE NO CREDITABLE WITNESSES OF THE ACCIDENT.

THE AIRCRAFT LANDED WITH NO DAMAGE OR INJURIES IN A GRASSY AREA EAST OF THE RUNWAY 5 CENTERLINE AND EAST OF THE RUNWAY 9R DEPARTURE END ON A NORTHEAST HEADING.  FIRST RESPONDER, MELBOURNE AIRPORT OPERATIONS MANAGER CLIFFORD GRAHAM, WHO WITNESSED THE INCIDENT WHILE HOLDING SHORT OF RUNWAY 5, STATED THAT FUEL WAS POURING OUT OF A LINE ON THE LEFT SIDE OF THE ENGINE WHEN HE ARRIVED AT THE AIRPLANE IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE POWER OFF LANDING.  THE FUEL FLOW WAS STOPPED BY THE INSTRUCTOR WHO LANDED THE AIRPLANE.  THE FIT INSTRUCTOR AND AN FIT STUDENT WERE THE ONLY OCCUPANTS ON BOARD THE AIRCRAFT.  BOTH INSTRUCTOR AND STUDENT INDICATED THAT EVERYTHING PRIOR TO THE LOSS OF ENGINE POWER APPEARED TO BE NORMAL.  SUBSEQUENT TO THE POWER OFF LANDING BOTH THE INSTRUCTOR AND STUDENT INDICATED THAT THE ENGINE FUEL SUMP WAS LEAKING FUEL.  FUEL DRAINING FROM THE ENGINE SUMP DRAIN DURING THE AIRPLANE?S OPERATION PRIOR TO THE POWER OFF LANDING WAS EVIDENT AS INDICATED BY BLUE FUEL DYE STAINS ON THE COWLING, FUSELAGE, AND WING.  INSPECTION OF THE ENGINE FUEL SUMP VALVE REVEALED THAT THE SUMP VALVE WAS CATCHING ON THE ENGINE COWLING WHICH PREVENTED THE VALVE FROM CLOSING AFTER SAMPLING FUEL.  INSPECTION OF THE RUN-UP AREA WHERE THE RUN-UP WAS COMPLETED REVEALED EVIDENCE OF AVIATION FUEL STAINING ON THE ASPHALT.  THE TIE DOWN SPOT WHERE THE AIRCRAFT WAS ORIGINALLY PARKED HAD A LARGE FUEL STAIN, APPROXIMATELY 6 FEET BY 10 FEET, RUNNING FROM WHERE THE ENGINE SUMP DRAIN WAS LOCATED TOWARD A STORM DRAIN.  A REVIEW OF THE FIT NORMAL PROCEDURES CHECKLIST REVEALED THAT THE COCKPIT PREPARATION CHECKLIST READS; FUEL SELECTOR?TURN OFF TO VERIFY OPERATION.  THE PIPER, PA-28-161, WARRIOR III, PREFLIGHT CHECK, COCKPIT CHECKLIST DOES NOT INCLUDE THIS STEP/PROCEDURE.  THIS ADDED PROCEDURAL STEP PREVENTS THE ENGINE FUEL SUMP FROM BEING PROPERLY SAMPLED.  FURTHERMORE, IF THE SUMP DRAIN IS NOT PROPERLY CLOSED AFTER FUEL SAMPLING THE OPENED DRAIN MAY NOT BE DETECTED PRIOR TO REENTERING THE COCKPIT FOR FLIGHT.  ONCE AIRBORNE WITH MAXIMUM ENGINE POWER FOR TAKEOFF THE ENGINE FUEL DEMAND WAS GREATER THAN COULD BE PROVIDED DUE TO THE FUEL LOSS THROUGH THE ENGINE FUEL SUMP DRAIN.  WITH A FUEL/AIR RATIO INADEQUATE TO SUSTAIN COMBUSTION THE ENGINE FAILED TO CONTINUE TO PRODUCE POWER.  THE AIRCRAFT LOGBOOKS AND VISUAL INSPECTION INDICATE THE AIRCRAFT WAS AIRWORTHY AT THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT.  WEATHER WAS NOT A FACTOR IN THIS INCIDENT.  THE INSTRUCTOR AND STUDENT ACTIONS ARE NOT CONSIDERED TO HAVE CONTRIBUTED TO THIS INCIDENT AS THE ENGINE SUMP DRAIN WAS NOT LEAKING FUEL DURING THE PREFLIGHT INSPECTION AFTER SAMPLING FUEL IN ACCORDANCE WITH FIT NORMAL PROCEDURES.

UNFORTUNATELY, IT WAS TOO LATE; THE RIGHT MAIN LANDING GEAR COLLAPSED AND THE AIRCRAFT BEGAN TO VEER TO THE RIGHT.  THE PILOT WAS ABLE TO STEER THE AIRCRAFT ONTO THE GRASS ADJACENT TO THE RUNWAY. THE RIGHT ENGINE INCURRED A PROPELLER STRIKE AGAINST THE GROUND AND SUDDEN ENGINE STOPPAGE.  IN THE PILOT?S WRITTEN STATEMENT, HE INDICATED THAT HE ALWAYS STRIVES TO BE SAFE AND PROFESSIONAL IN HIS FLYING.  MOREOVER, IN REVIEWING THE EVENTS OF THE EVENING OF THE ACCIDENT, HE HAS COME TO REALIZE THAT EXCEPT IN CASES OF EXTREME PERFORMANCE (I.E., SHORT-FIELD LANDINGS), THERE IS NO NEED TO ALTER THE CONFIGURATION OF AN AIRCRAFT UNTIL FULLY STOPPED ON THE TAXIWAY, AND AFTER SAFELY EXITING THE ACTIVE RUNWAY. 20131015021399A	ON OCTOBER 15, 2013, AT APPROXIMATELY 1902 LOCAL (0002 UTC), AN AIRLINE TRANSPORT PILOT-RATED PILOT-IN-COMMAND (PIC) AND EQUALLY RATED SECOND-IN-COMMAND (SIC), WERE INVOLVED IN AN AIRCRAFT ACCIDENT RESULTING FROM THE AIRCRAFT EXITING THE RUNWAY SURFACE DURING LANDING ROLL-OUT AT THE COLONEL JAMES JABARA AIRPORT (KAAO), WICHITA, KANSAS. THE AIRCRAFT INVOLVED IN THIS ACCIDENT IS AN EMBRAER EMB-500 PHENOM 100, WHICH IS OWNED AND OPERATED BY A 14 CFR PART 135 AIR CARRIER. VISUAL METEOROLOGICAL CONDITIONS (VMC) PREVAILED AT THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENT; KAAO ASOS REPORTED CLEAR SKIES, TEN STATUTE MILES OF VISIBILITY AND SURFACE WINDS FROM 320 DEGREES AT 10 KNOTS. THIS REPOSITIONING FLIGHT ORIGINATED FROM THE CHARLES B. WHEELER DOWNTOWN AIRPORT (KMKC), KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI; THE FLIGHT WAS OPERATED IN ACCORDANCE WITH 14 CFR PART 91.THIS FLIGHT WAS DISPATCHED WITH TWO QUALIFIED AIRMEN; THE AIRMAN, WHO WAS ALSO THE PIC FOR THIS FLIGHT, WAS FULFILLING THE ROLE OF PILOT-NOT-FLYING (PNF) OR PILOT MONITORING (PM), WHILE THE SIC, WHO HOLDS THE APPROPRIATE PIC TYPE RATING, WAS THE PILOT FLYING (PF). FOR THE SOLE PURPOSE OF ALLOWING THE NEWLY RATED SIC TO GAIN VALUABLE AIRCRAFT OPERATING EXPERIENCE, THE PIC AND SIC MUTUALLY AGREED TO HAVE THE SIC OCCUPY THE LEFT SEAT WHILE THE EXPERIENCED PIC WOULD ASSUME THE PNF DUTIES FROM THE RIGHT SEAT. DURING THE PRE-DEPARTURE BRIEFING BOTH THE PIC AND SIC DISCUSSED THAT THIS WOULD BE THE SIC?S FIRST FLIGHT IN THE AIRCRAFT AS ALL PREVIOUS TRAINING WAS CONDUCTED IN THE SIMULATOR. ACCORDING TO THE AIRMEN?S STATEMENTS, THE FLIGHT FROM KMKC TO KAAO WAS UNEVENTFUL. PRIOR TO THE APPROACH AND LANDING, BOTH THE PIC AND SIC BRIEFED THE GPS RWY 36 INSTRUMENT APPROACH AND FURTHER DISCUSSED ANY CONCERNS THAT THE PF HAD WITH REGARDS TO THE AIRCRAFT?S HANDLING CHARACTERISTICS AND BRAKING NUANCES UPON TOUCHDOWN. THE FINAL APPROACH SEGMENT WAS UNEVENTFUL; THE AIRCRAFT WAS APPROPRIATELY CONFIGURED FOR LANDING, OPERATING AT ITS PUBLISHED APPROACH REFERENCE SPEED UNTIL LANDING. UPON TOUCHDOWN, BOTH THE PIC AND SIC RECALL THAT FULL BRAKE PRESSURE WAS APPLIED BY THE PF.  IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWING THIS APPLICATION, THE AIRCRAFT BEGAN TO DEVIATE LEFT OF THE RUNWAY CENTERLINE. THE PF IMMEDIATELY INITIATED A CONTROL INPUT WITH THE RIGHT RUDDER TO CORRECT THE DEVIATION; THE AIRCRAFT SUBSEQUENTLY BEGAN TO DEVIATE LATERALLY. WITH EACH CORRECTIVE CONTROL INPUT THE AIRCRAFT?S DEVIATION FROM THE RUNWAY CENTERLINE BECAME MORE EXCESSIVE. THE OVER-CORRECTION BY THE PF ALSO CAUSED EXCESSIVE SIDE-LOADING ON THE AIRCRAFT?S LANDING GEAR AND TIRES. THIS CONTINUOUS SIDE-LOADING RESULTED IN THE CONSTANT SKIDDING OF THE AIRCRAFT?S THREE TIRES UNTIL IT VACATED THE RIGHT SIDE OF THE RUNWAY SURFACE. PRIOR TO THE AIRCRAFT VACATING THE RUNWAY, THE AIRCRAFT?S LONGITUDINAL AXIS WAS APPROXIMATELY 45 DEGREES TO THE RUNWAY CENTERLINE; THE EXCESSIVE SIDE LOADING AND TIRE SKIDDING INEVITABLY CAUSED THE AIRCRAFT TO EXIT THE RIGHT SIDE OF THE RUNWAY INTO THE GRASS.  THE AIRCRAFT?S FORWARD-SKIDDING MOTION, COMBINED WITH EXCESSIVE SIDE-LOADING CAUSED THE LEFT MAIN GEAR ACTUATOR ARM TO FOLD UP INTO THE LEFT WING AND PUNCTURE THROUGH THE UPPER SKIN STRUCTURE. SUBSTANTIAL DAMAGE WAS SUSTAINED AS THE AIRCRAFT?S LEFT MAIN GEAR PARTIALLY COLLAPSED INTO THE WING STRUCTURE. A POST-ACCIDENT REVIEW OF THE AIRCRAFT?S BRAKE-BY-WIRE CONTROL UNIT AND FLIGHT DATA RECORDER INDICATES THAT THE AIRCRAFT DID NOT EXPERIENCE A BRAKE SYSTEM FAILURE NOR DID ANY ANOMALIES TRANSPIRE PRIOR TO THE ACCIDENT AS EVIDENCED BY THE LACK OF SYSTEM-SPECIFIC CREW-ALERTING SYSTEM (CAS) MESSAGES. REVIEW OF THE BRAKE CONTROL UNIT DATA INDICATES THAT THE AIRCRAFT?S BRAKES WERE NEVER RELEASED FROM THEIR INITIAL APPLICATION. ADDITIONALLY, THE PF REMAINED ON THE FLIGHT CONTROLS THROUGHOUT THE ENTIRE EVENT. ALTHOUGH AN ATTEMPT WAS INITIATED TO RELINQUISH AIRCRAFT CONTROL TO PIC/PNF, THIS INEVITABLY DID NOT TRANSPIRE. THE PIC AND SIC WERE UNINJURED; NO PASSENGERS WERE ON-BOARD.

UPON TOUCHDOWN THE CREW REALIZED THE GEAR WAS IN THE RETRACTED POSITION.  THE AIRCRAFT CAME TO A STOP APPROXIMATELY HALFWAY DOWN THE RUNWAY.  UPON EXAMINATION OF THE AIRCRAFT BY THE IIC, IT WAS FOUND THAT THE GEAR HANDLE WAS IN THE RETRACTED POSITION.  IT WAS ALSO FOUND THAT THE "ANNUNCIATOR TEST" SWITCH WAS IN THE "DIM" POSITION.  THIS WAS LIKELY DUE TO THE FACT THAT THE AIRCRAFT HAD BEEN FLOWN ON A NIGHT MISSION PREVIOUS TO THIS FLIGHT.  THIS SWITCH POSITION WOULD MAKE THE GEAR POSITION LIGHTS, AND THE GEAR WARNING LIGHT MORE DIFFICULT TO SEE DURING DAYTIME CONDITIONS.

FLIGHT INSTRUCTOR, ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^, WITH A STUDENT, ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^, ATTEMPTED TO START THE AIRCRAFT PRIOR TO FLIGHT. DURING THE START-UP PROCEDURES THE INSTRUCTOR DIRECTED THE STUDENT TO PRIME THE ENGINE WITH FUEL UTILIZING THE ACCELERATOR PUMP IN THE CARBURETOR INSTEAD OF THE FACTORY INSTALLED PRIMER SYSTEM. THIS PROCEDURE IS CONTRARY TO THE PILOT?S OPERATING HANDBOOK. THE INSTRUCTOR STATED HE ?TOLD [AIRMAN ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^] TO DEFER THE USE OF PRIMER AND MERELY OPEN AND CLOSE THE THROTTLE TWO TIMES WHICH I FELT FROM EXPERIENCE WOULD BE SUFFICIENT TO START THE ENGINE.? THIS PROCEDURE REQUIRES ACTUATING THE ENGINE THROTTLE; IN THIS EVENT THE THROTTLE WAS ACTUATED TWICE PRIOR TO START-UP. THE DESIGN OF A LYCOMIMNG 0-235 ENGINE, INCORPORATES AN UP-DRAFT CARBURETOR WITH AN ACCELERATOR PUMP. WHEN THE ACCELERATOR PUMP IS ACTUATED IT SPRAYS FUEL OUT OF THE CARBURETOR INTO THE INDUCTION. IF THE ENGINE IS NOT TURNING THE FUEL CAN, AND IN THIS CASE DID, DRAIN BACK DOWN THROUGH THE CARBURETOR AND INTO THE CARBURETOR AIRBOX. MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL INSPECTED THE ENGINE AFTER THE FIRE AND DISCOVERED THE IGNITION TIMING WAS ADVANCED BY 2 DEGREES. THIS MAY HAVE CONTRIBUTED TO THE FIRE BY PRODUCING A SPARK WHILE THE INTAKE VALVE WAS OPEN, THUS IGNITING THE FUEL IN THE INDUCTION.

THE PILOT EXECUTED A BALKED LANDING/GO-AROUND PROCEDURE AFTER THE SECOND PORPOISE. THE NOSE GEAR STRUT AND FARING WAS SLIGHTLY DAMAGED DURING THE BALKED LANDING MANEUVER.  A BYSTANDER WHO WAS ON THE GROUND AT FALLBROOK TOOK A PICTURE OF THE NOSE GEAR AND EMAILED THE PHOTO TO A PASSENGER ON THE AIRCRAFT. AFTER REVIEWING THE PHOTO OF THE NOSE GEAR ON THE PASSENGERS IPHONE, THE PILOT ELECTED TO RETURN AND LAND AT HIS HOME AIRPORT (CARLSBAD-PALOMAR, KCRQ). THE AIRCRAFT LANDED UNEVENTFULLY ON RUNWAY 24 AT CARLSBAD ALTHOUGH THE DAMAGED NOSE WHEEL WAS BENT ENOUGH TO PRECLUDE A NORMAL TAXI. GROUND CREWS ASSISTED THE PILOT AND THE AIRCRAFT WAS TOWED TO THE PILOTS HANGAR FOR REPAIRS.   THE NOSE STRUT (LEG) ON VANS RV-A SERIES AIRCRAFT IS A KNOWN WEAK DESIGN SINCE THE AIRCRAFT WAS ORIGINALLY DESIGNED AS A CONVENTIONAL GEAR AIRCRAFT WITHOUT A NOSE WHEEL. THE NOSE WHEEL SYSTEM WAS LATER ADDED AND IS OF MINIMAL DESIGN TO KEEP THE TRICYCLE -9A MODEL SIMILAR IN WEIGHT TO THE -9 CONVENTIONAL MODEL.    SINCE 1988 THERE HAVE BEEN SEVERAL MANUFACTURER MODIFICATIONS TO THE NOSE GEAR STRUT AND YOKE WHICH HAVE RESULTED IN ISSUING SEVERAL SERVICE BULLETINS. EVEN SO, THERE ARE OTHER MANUFACTURERS THAT CONTINUE TO DESIGN AND SELL "NOSE GEAR STRUT STIFFENERS" FOR TRICYCLE MODEL VAN'S AIRCRAFT.   THE PILOT (AND ORIGINAL BUILDER OF THIS AIRCRAFT) HAD INSTALLED A NOSE STRUT STIFFENER MECHANISM (KIT) MADE BY A COMPANY CALLED "ANTI SPLAT AERO". THE STIFFENER KIT KEEPS THE NOSE STRUT FROM BENDING BACKWARDS AND THIS KIT HELPED AVOID A PROP-STRIKE AND OTHER COSTLY DAMAGE TO THE AIRCRAFT IN THIS INCIDENT. THE MODIFIED NOSE GEAR SUSTAINED VERY MINOR DAMAGE TO THE NOSE GEAR AND NOSE GEAR FAIRING DURING THIS INCIDENT.

20131230024979I	RECEIVED REQUEST FROM MANAGEMENT TO GO TO AIRPORT BECAUSE AIRPLANE LANDED SHORT OF RUNWAY 35. AIRCRAFT  DEPARTED LAS VEGAS A FEW HOURS BEFORE, VFR FLIGHT PLAN (NOT FILED) WEATHER CHECKED BY COMPUTER. WAS CLEARED FOR FINAL AND TURNED SHORT FINAL AND ENGINE STOPPED. FUEL SELECTOR WAS ON LEFT TANK, HE SWITCHED TO THE RIGHT TANK AND ENGINE WOULD NOT RE-START. BOTH FUEL LOW INDICATOR LIGHTS WERE ON BUT HE FELT HE HAD 17 GALLONS OF FUEL BASED ON THE FUEL FLOW SYSTEM INSTALLED (JPI). GAUGES WERE BOUNCING NEAR EMPTY AND HE FEELS THEY ARE UNRELIABLE. THE A/C STARTED TO STALL, HE PUSHED THE NOSE OVER TO GET FORWARD AIRSPEED AND THEN TURNED TO AVOID THE LANDING LIGHTS AND FLARED TO LAND IN THE SNOW. WHEN ASKED ABOUT FUEL HE STATED THAT TO TOOK 10 GALLONS IN NORTH LAS VEGAS PRIOR TO DEPARTURE WHICH GAVE HIM A TOTAL OF 44 GALLONS WHEN HE LEFT.
20131230025349I	THE PILOT TOOK TWO PASSENGERS ON A LOCAL FLIGHT. DURING THE APPROACH TO LANDING THE PILOT STATED HE WAS EXPLAINING TO THE PASSENGER IN THE FRONT SEAT HOW PILOTS LAND AIRCRAFT.  THE PILOT STATED THAT HE FAILED TO EXTEND THE GEAR DUE TO THIS DISTRACTION.
20131230025699A	THE AIRCRAFT LANDED ON RUNWAY 30 (TURF RUNWAY) AND EXITED THE RUNWAY ON AN APPROXIMATE HEADING OF 45 DEGREES TO THE RIGHT OF THE RUNWAY HEADING, 2200 FEET FROM THE APPROACH END AND 143 FEET FROM THE DEPARTURE END.  THE WIND AT THE TIME, AS REPORTED BY AWOS, WAS 230 DEGREES AT 11 KNOTS. THE AIRPORT IS SITUATED ON A HILL WITH THE TERRAIN GRADUALLY SLOPING TO THE EAST WITH A SHARPER SLOPE TO THE WEST. THE RUNWAY WAS SHORT GRASS (SEASONAL DORMANT) AND THE GROUND WAS FROZEN.   THE PILOT STATED HE TOUCHED DOWN PAST HIS INTENDED LANDING POINT AND THEN INTENTIONALLY STEERED THE AIRCRAFT TO THE RIGHT SIDE OF THE RUNWAY TO ALLOW THE HIGHER VEGITATION TO SLOW THE AIRCRAFT. THE AIRCRAFT THEN STRUCK A BERM, HIDDEN BY THE TALLER VEGETATION WHICH CAUSED THE AIRCRAFT TO ELEVATE AND THE NOSE GEAR FORK TO BREAK OFF.  THE AIRCRAFT FLIPPED OVER AND CAME TO REST IN AN INVERTED POSITION.  THE CREW AND PASSENGERS EXITED THROUGH A DOOR WINDOW.   THE AIRCRAFT SUSTAINED SUBSTANTIAL DAMAGE AND THERE WERE NO INJURIES TO THE PILOT OR PASSENGERS.
20131231025139A	01/06/2014, UPON LANDING ROLL OUT THE PILOT LOST CONTROL OF THE AIRCRAFT AS IT DRIFTED LEFT OF THE CENTER LINE. AS THE PILOT APPLIED RIGHT RUDDER TO CORRECT DRIFT THE PILOT ALSO APPLIED RIGHT BRAKES IN WHICH THE PILOT OVER CORRECTED. THIS ACTION CAUSED THE AIRCRAFT TO ENTER INTO A GROUND LOOP EFFECT AND ROTATED 270 DEGREES WITH THE AIRCRAFT POINTED ACROSS RUNWAY 18 WITH THE TAIL WHEEL IN THE GRASS BOARDERING THE RUNWAY. THE PILOT AND PASSENGER EXITED THE AIRCRAFT UNHURT AND REMOVED THE AIRCRAFT FROM THE RUNWAY. THE GROUND CREWS REPOSITIONED THE AIRCRAFT TO THE TRANSIENT PARKING AREA.  THE AIRCRAFT EXPERIENCED DAMAGE TO THE LEFT LANDING GEAR ATTACH POINT TO THE FUSELAGE. THE AIRCRAFT WAS EVENTUALLY MOVED FROM THIS LOCATION TO A MAINTENANCE HANGAR.  INSPECTION TO THE AIRCRAFT REVEALED SKIN WRINKLES ON THE LEFT SIDE OF THE FORWARD FUSELAGE AND EXTENDING DOWNWARD TO UNDER THE AIRCRAFT  FORWARD OF THE LEFT LOWER WING STRUT ATTACH POINT.
